News.title: Afghanistan national, 26, arrested over death of Brit woman in Athens after ‘confessing to dumping body in suitcase’
News.content:
SUITCASE ARREST Afghanistan national, 26, arrested over death of Brit woman in Athens after ‘confessing to dumping body in suitcase’

AN Afghan national has been arrested in Athens over the death of a British woman whose body was found in a suitcase.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, was found stuffed inside the travel bag in an abandoned building last week.



Greek police said a 26-year-old man from Afghanistan is in custody on charges of manslaughter, robbery and violating weapons law – though the exact details have not yet been finalised.

The suspect reportedly confessed to dumping Elisabeth inside a suitcase before hauling it to an abandoned site in Kypseli where she was later found.



Cops analysed CCTV footage showing the suspect carrying a large travel bag to the site.

Cops said they believe the suspect also used the victim’s bank cards to withdraw money in Athens.



Elisabeth’s cause of death is still yet to be confirmed.

Raids of the suspect’s home uncovered a fake pistol and a knife, according to local media.

Greek cops had previously probed whether Elizabeth – a “good Samaritan” and committed Christian – was murdered by someone she was trying to help.

She was a regular traveller to Greece, volunteering with NGOs in the country.



She had reportedly been spotted befriending homeless people across Athens.

Critical autopsy tests were fast-tracked to help solve the grim mystery.

Police believe she was killed near to where her body was found in the derelict building.



Elisabeth, known as Lisa, was reportedly seen chatting to homeless people close to an abandoned car park where they take drugs, drink and sleep rough.

Greece’s version of the FBI are said to be “seriously contemplating” suffocation as the cause of death of the Scottish woman.

Elisabeth’s body was identified on Wednesday – the day her mobile phone was mysteriously deactivated by suspects believed ” to have intimate knowledge ” of her last movements.

A homeless man who made the grim discovery has insisted the suitcase was not in the building the two days prior.

His testimony has led police to believe her body was taken to the building at 7 Evelpidon Street on the evening of July 17 or the following morning.



Elisabeth arrived in the Greek capital on a flight from Edinburgh on June 26.

A Greek couple who Elisabeth was staying with in Keratsini told cops she was going to stay with some Americans she knew in Kypseli.

Investigators are now hunting the mystery pals as authorities expand the probe abroad.



“We see these Americans as key,” a source told The Sun. “We believe they have valuable information.”

It comes after reports that the friends may not be real and that Elisabeth just wanted to be alone.

So far, cops have not been able to confirm the exact date of Elisabeth’s death or if it is considered murder.

Her heartbroken father revealed he had received haunting text messages from his daughter’s phone after her death.

The dad, a lawyer in Edinburgh, told Greek cops he was sent several messages for two weeks after Elisabeth’s passing from a man now being viewed as the prime suspect.



One message sent on the last day she was seen alive said she “needed some time to herself” and “wanted to be alone for a while”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Police said the messages were sent from Athens – helping them to track down the phone.

They added: ” It is clear whoever sent them was trying to buy time.”

News.title: Heartbreaking 1st responder testimony about desperate attempts to revive kids that left Lindsay Clancy shaking in court
News.content:
‘KILLER’ mom Lindsay Clancy broke down in court as the jury heard heartbreaking testimony from first responders about the desperate attempts to revive her children.

The 35-year-old former nurse was left shaking with her head in her hands as evidence was given on Friday, the fifth day of her trial, as she stands accused of murdering her three children.



On January 24, 2023, her husband Patrick came home from running errands to find Clancy lying injured outside under their bedroom window, and their three children dead inside their Massachusetts home.

If you or someone you know needs help or support for their mental health, text “STRENGTH” to the Crisis Text Line at 741-741 to be connected with a certified crisis counselor.





Five-year-old Cora, three-year-old Dawson and eight-month-old Callan had been strangled with exercise bands by their mother, who was allegedly suffering from undiagnosed postpartum psychosis.

After a voice allegedly told her to kill the children, Clancy cut her wrists and neck and leapt out of the bedroom window in an apparent botched suicide attempt that left her paralyzed from the waist down.

read more on Clancy trial BLURRED LINES Hidden tactics as Lindsay Clancy's trial divides USA - murderer or victim?

Sitting in her wheelchair alongside her defense attorney Kevin Reddington on Friday, Clancy broke down sobbing and shaking as emergency medicine doctors recalled desperate attempts to revive her children.

Paramedic Jennifer Stratton told the court how she “scooped him up in my arms and carried him outside to the truck” while pictures from the basement showed an exercise band next to Callan’s Mickey Mouse pajamas which were taken off by paramedics.



Emergency medicine doctor Benjamin Kaufman spoke about trying to revive eight-month-old Callan at Bell Israel Deconess Hospital in Plymouth where he regained a pulse but had no evidence of “brain function.”

“The first thing we do is give a dose of epinephrine, and in this case, you can look directly at the heart with an ultrasound,” he explained, with hopes that the adrenaline would re-start the heart.

“His heart started beating after we were able to give that dose. At that point, we continued compressions, continued giving him breaths through the breathing tube.

“At no point in time during his care did he have any brain function.”

Callan was flown to Boston Children’s Hospital but at no point was able to breathe on his own and was pronounced dead three days later after being put on life support.



Meanwhile Kaufman’s colleague and fellow ER doctor Mark Tenerowicz, told the court how medical staff spent 40 minutes desperately trying to revive three-year-old Dawson after taking over from paramedics at hospital.

“It did not look like his heart would ever start again,” the doctor said, detailing how they gave the child IV fluids, doses of adrenaline, and other treatments all while performing CPR.

At no point did he have a pulse or start breathing on his own.

Both Cora and Dawson were declared dead at that night.

Their mother clutched tissues in court as photographs were displayed on a large screen in front of her showing the scene where responders attempted to revive her children.



They included several pieces of medical equipment including a heart monitor, children’s pajamas, and blood on the floor.



Other emotional scenes played out in court when Clancy heard Patrick’s heart-wrenching 911 call in which the devastated father can be heard screaming in pure agony, court reporters revealed.

Clancy sobbed the entire time the audio was played in court with Reddington holding her hand and a recess was called after jurors were left in tears.

Meanwhile, Duxbury police officer Stephen Hall appeared visibly shaken as he took the stand and recalled arriving at the scene and finding Patrick in the backyard while Clancy was drifting in and out of consciousness “in pain.”

While recalling working the scene, Hall took deep breathes and at one point removed his glasses to wipe his eyes.

“I heard a loud scream from inside the house,” he said, after Patrick went inside the house to check on the children.



Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial Lindsay Clancy is accused of strangling her three children, Cora, five, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan, with exercise bands inside their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home on January 24, 2023. The former labor and delivery nurse does not deny killing them, but has pleaded not guilty and claims she was not criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors argue Clancy deliberately sent her then-husband Patrick out to collect medicine and dinner so she could be left alone with the children. The trial began with Patrick on the witness stand, describing Clancy’s declining mental health before recounting how he returned home, found her injured outside and discovered the children in the basement. Jurors have since heard his harrowing 911 call, seen the bands that were removed from the children’s necks and viewed their pajamas and other evidence from the home. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT? Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial is expected to last between six and eight weeks, meaning testimony could continue well into September.

Proceedings are scheduled to begin at around 9am ET on sitting days and normally continue through the afternoon, with morning, lunch and afternoon breaks.

Prosecutors will present their case first, calling first responders, police officers, investigators, medical professionals and other witnesses connected to the killings.

The state listed more than 180 potential witnesses, although prosecutors are not expected to call everyone named.

Jurors are also expected to visit the Clancy family’s former Duxbury home with the judge and lawyers to see the scene for themselves.

Once prosecutors rest, Clancy’s defense will begin calling its own witnesses, including people who knew her and experts expected to testify about her medication, mental health and alleged postpartum psychosis.

The defense listed more than 60 possible witnesses, but some overlap with the prosecution’s list and may not be called twice.

After both sides finish presenting evidence, lawyers will deliver closing arguments before the judge instructs jurors on the law.

The jury will then decide whether Clancy is guilty of murder or was not criminally responsible because of her mental state when she killed her children.

He added the scream had no words, “It was just a sound” and that he walked to the basement to find one of the children lying on his back, shirtless in a diaper, before all the kids were rushed out of the home by medical responders.

Hall described Cora and Callan as being “motionless” on the floor while being worked on by paramedics and detailed how he had to keep helping Clancy put her oxygen mask back on as she kept removing it.

The outcome of the murder case will largely hinge on testimonies from first responders about her physical condition and the attempt to end her life, which included critical ‘code blue’ evidence.

The jury of 12 women and six men who were taken on a harrowing tour of the crime scene and other locations related to the case on Friday, will have to determine if Clancy killed her children with intent or if she was mentally incapable of knowing what she was doing.



Her defense team argue she is not-guilty by reason of insanity, due to her extreme mental health struggles at the time rendering her not criminally responsible for the deaths of her children.

Her now ex-husband Patrick filed a wrongful death lawsuit in January 2026 against Clancy’s healthcare providers after she was prescribed 13 different medications and hospitalized several times but discharged weeks before the killings.

Clancy faces life in prison without parole if found guilty of three counts of murder.

You can catch up on the trial with a recap on our YouTube Channel. Also, see our exclusive breakdown of the hidden trial tactics LindsayClancyy’s team are using to clear her.

News.title: Horror moment two firefighting helicopters collide midair while battling Greek wildfires as one sent crashing to ground
News.content:
TWO helicopters have crashed mid-air in Athens while battling the wildfires raging across Greece.

A frantic search and rescue operation is underway to recover the pilots and crews of the downed aircraft.



The helicopters crashed near Psatha, west of Athens, after taking off from the Elefsina military airport.

Dramatic footage shows the two choppers drifting terrifyingly close before smashing into each other.



One of the helicopters erupts into a ball of flames with debris exploding into the air.

The helicopter plummets to the ground followed by a thick stream of smoke.

One of the helicopters appears to fly away from the crash site.

Greece’s fire service said in a statement the BELL helicopters had a crew of two people each on board.



Rescue teams have reportedly recovered the crew of one of the helicopters “safe”, a government official said.

The other helicopter has been located, they added.

But searches are now underway to locate those who were on board the crashed aircraft.

The helicopters were part of an operation to tackle a huge wildfire which has destroyed over 100 homes northwest of Athens.

Dozens of roaring blazes are being fuelled by gale-force winds across several Greek islands, destroying vegetation and burning houses.



On Saturday morning, 29 planes and helicopters began crucial water drops in Viotia, in southern central Greece, where a fire broke out on Friday.

Another fresh blaze forced evacuations on the popular tourist island of Kefalonia on Sunday.

Nearly 500 Greek firefighters have been deployed to the region, assisted by personnel from France and Romania.



Ground forces, including 18 firefighting units and 92 fire engines, reinforced 325 firefighters as they battled ferocious infernos overnight.

And firefighters continue to battle a large wildfire on the Greek island of Crete that ignited earlier this week.

Around 8,000 people were ordered to move to safety as flames closed in on southern resort villages, destroying homes, farms, and livestock in their path.

At least three emergency responders have lost their lives during the crisis, including two firefighters who became trapped in their vehicle near the mountain village of Krya Vrysi.

Fires have also broken out on the islands of Paros, Andros and Kalymnos.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

It comes amid a spate of deadly wildfires wreaking havoc across Europe – including the UK – as the continent tackles record-breaking heatwaves.

Flames in Spain and France are understood to be dying down, leaving Greece and Turkey to bear the brunt of the soaring temperatures.

News.title: Jeremy Clarkson slams young people on benefits ‘sitting at home all day’ – as Burnham tries to tackle welfare bill
News.content:
JEREMY Clarkson has slammed young people on benefits for “sitting at home all day.”

The Clarkson’s Farm star let loose in his latest column saying youths on benefits should offer gratitude to the taxpayers who support them.



It comes as new PM Andy Burnham pushes to get more young people into work – signalling last week that ministers could tighten rules on benefit claimants.

Speaking in his column today, Clarkson said more than 1million young people are not working.



The TV presenter said instead, youths were “sitting at home gormlessly watching shortform nonsense.”

According to the Clarkson’s Farm star – unemployed youngsters with ADHD or other mental health issues can claim up to £194 a week.



To pay for it, Labour has introduced tax rises at the party’s last two budgets – both under Rachel Reeves.

In her first budget Reeves raided some £40billion, promising it would be a one off.



But at her next budget the former Chancellor took a further £26billion in tax rises.

Clarkson goes on to explain that he is happy to pay for his dogs’ lives, look after them, and put up with their nonsense because in return he gets gratitude.

Writing in The Sunday Times, the former Top Gear host said: “Which is what gave me my big idea. At present, people who work hard, feed, clothe and entertain those who won’t work at all. And what do we get in return? Nothing.

“So how’s this for a plan? Burnham appeases his back benches by saying that taxes will rise to pay for those who are incapacitated by some kind of issue with neurodivergence.

“And then he appeases us by insisting we get something in return. Which is a thank you letter.”



Going on, Clarkson explains that he would be happy with further tax raids to pay for a growing welfare bill in exchange for heartfelt thank you notes from people claiming benefits.

He suggests giving the email address of a working person to people claiming benefits and ensuring a thank you letter is sent to them.

His tongue-in-cheek suggestion comes as analysis revealed some teens on sickness benefits receive around £100 a week more than others working part-time on minimum wage.

New PM Andy Burnham plans to deal with the problem by encouraging young people into work.

He has unveiled a shake-up of secondary schools to better prepare youngsters for the job.



Mr Burnham said: “I want an education system based on parity between academic and technical which gives all young people a clear path in life.

“From today, Britain will value the hard hat every bit as much as the graduation cap.”

Mr Burnham’s education reforms sit alongside a wider attempt to tackle Britain’s soaring welfare bill.

In an interview with the BBC, he signalled some benefits could come with tougher conditions, saying: “It’s about changing the nature of the support and making some of it conditional on people taking opportunities that are presented.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“So you might increase the conditions required to receive benefits.”



But he insisted he was not blaming people already claiming.

News.title: We live next to huge migrant detention centre which will triple in size – we were lied to & now we’re trapped
News.content:
'HELL ON EARTH' We live next to huge migrant detention centre which will triple in size – we were lied to & now we’re trapped

RESIDENTS living next to a proposed immigration detention centre have said they are “prisoners” in their own homes after plans were revealed to triple its size.

The proposals to expand Haslar Immigration Removal Centre (IRC) in Gosport, Hampshire, has sparked fury with homeowners.



People living by the controversial detainment site claim they have been “lied to” about its size with plans indicating it will become three-storeys high.

The seaside residents say that they have seen their house prices drop by as much as £25,000 after the plans were introduced and feel that they are “trapped” because they are not able to sell their homes.



Some have also said that the building process has been two years of “hell on Earth“, where they are unable to sleep because of the constant construction noise starting in the early hours of the morning.

The detention centre – which will have 600 beds provided for the detained men who will be unable to leave the centre or access the local area – has been a nightmare for residents who feel they will be “overlooked” by the detainees.

Haslar immigration removal centre is set to increase its capacity from 198 beds to 600 beds.

It is being refurbished after shutting down in 2015 following a parliamentary review, which highlighted immigration detention as “expensive and damaging to detainees”.



Dave Wakefield has lived directly opposite the site with his wife Katie for 27 years said “of course we are worried about it”.

He said: “We know it is going to be different. How can you go from 150 to 600 people?

“Now we have seen everything that has gone on, and it is getting bigger and bigger. The people who are going there are criminals, so I have no time of day for them.”

He questioned the planning process and how it was to be governed, saying “normally issues like this are sorted out by the boroughs”.

“Of course we are worried about it. When they were here before, people were trying to break out. If that happened then when it wasn’t people that were criminals, and when it is 600 people and only 450 staff, you can imagine,” he added.



A woman who lives only 50 metres away from the centre and wanted to stay anonymous said that she had been searching for who she should contact about mitigating the damage the centre will cause.

She said: “At the moment we are prisoners in our own homes. We can’t sell our properties. They are unsellable.

“We are trapped. We feel like prisoners. We can’t go on social media and voice our concerns because if you do you do you get trolled.



“It is nothing to do with the political side of things, it is about a way of life. It is about mental health. We feel we are being run roughshod over.

“They just aren’t taking into consideration the close proximity of it.”

The woman said she had experienced “hell on Earth” while the construction has been going on because of the ‘antisocial behaviour’ of builders creating massive amounts of noise at 6am and blocking her car in.

She said that the amount of dust generated during the building work has made her worry for her health, and she feels like she can’t leave any of her windows open, even in the sweltering heat.

Another resident, Sandra Card, whose house backs out onto the development, said that she felt she had been lied to about the plans as she believed it was only going to be two storeys and was then developed into three.



The 67-year-old said: “The main issue is the fact that they have lied over it. They have said there was going to be 600 people, but they said it was going to be a two-storey building and now it is going to be three.

“I think it is going to have a big impact on our privacy. They say it isn’t.”

One woman, who did not want to be named, said that she had her house valued recently and it had gone down in value by £25,000.

She said that people had been struggling to sell their houses, and her family had planned to move but she didn’t think that would be possible anymore.

Gosport MP Caroline Dinenage said she is pressing ministers for answers about the detention centre, having raised the issue in Parliament and written to the Home Secretary after a promised meeting with a minister was cancelled.



Redevelopment at Haslar has taken a phased approach, with Phase 1 consisting of the refurbishment of existing buildings, and Phase 2 involving the building of new build accommodation.

Phase 1 will provide 130 beds and is expected to be ready by autumn, while the first inmates are anticipated to move in to the site in Spring 2027.

Dame Caroline has called for the application to be considered by Gosport Borough Council as the local planning authority – currently it is due to be decided by an inspector appointed by the Secretary of State after the local planning authority makes representations.

In a letter to the Home Office, she said she had “serious concerns” that the Government were pushing through the application with “minimal scrutiny, which isn’t acceptable”.

“We’re now approaching crunch time for this application, and nothing has changed. There needs to be more engagement over these plans before decision-making drifts out of reach of local people,” she said.



“Planning decisions of this nature should be determined locally, by those with proper knowledge and understanding of the area, its infrastructure, and the impact this development would have on the surrounding community.

“Local councillors are best placed to consider these matters, having been elected by the very residents who will be affected.

However, the Home Office insist that the proposal for three-storey buildings were included in plans presented to a public engagement event last October.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A spokesperson said: “All Crown Development planning applications require extensive engagement, and we encourage residents and stakeholders to share their views through the formal process.

“We make no apology for significantly expanding our detention capacity which will see more than 45,000 additional foreign criminals and illegal migrants removed over the coming decade.”

News.title: Brit woman found dead in suitcase ‘may have been suffocated’, say Greek FBI as cops continue to hunt for ‘key’ witnesses
News.content:
GREEK cops are said to be “seriously contemplating” suffocation as the cause of death of the Scottish woman found in a suitcase in Athens.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross was discovered by a homeless man in a derelict building in the Kypseli district of the Greek capital on July 18.



Greek authorities say headway is being made in unmasking the mystery case.

The possibility Elisabeth was suffocated is being “seriously contemplated” given the lack of evident injuries on her body, a well placed source told the Sun.



Cops have narrowed their search for suspects to a two-square- mile radius of the scene and say they are “confident” of success.

“The best trained officers in the Greek FBI are working around- the-clock on this and they feel optimistic,” the source said.



“They have had a lot of successes when it comes to other cases, so it’s only a matter of time”, they added.

“We will catch them.”



It comes after Greek authorities said her cause of death could be revealed in “days” as they fast-track crucial tests.

Tests on blood, urine and vital organ tissues will be key to determine if foul play was involved.

Elisabeth’s body was identified on Wednesday – the day her mobile phone was mysteriously deactivated by suspects believed ” to have intimate knowledge ” of her last movements.



The homeless man who made the grim discovery has insisted the suitcase was not in the building the two days prior.

His testimony has led police to believe her body was taken to the building at 7 Evelpidon Street on the evening of July 17 or the following morning.

Elisabeth arrived in the Greek capital on a flight from Edinburgh on June 26.

Police believe she was killed not far from where her body was found in the abandoned building in Kypseli.

A Greek couple who Elisabeth was staying with in Keratsini told cops she was going to stay with some Americans she knew in Kypseli.



Investigators are now hunting the mystery pals as authorities expand the probe abroad.

“We see these Americans as key,” said the source. “We believe they have valuable information.”

It comes after reports that the friends may not be real and that Elisabeth just wanted to be alone.



Meanwhile, cops are also reportedly searching for a heavily-tattooed homeless man who allegedly tried to rape a woman at knifepoint after Elisabeth’s body was found.

So far, cops have not been able to confirm the exact date of Elisabeth’s death or if it is considered murder.

Her heartbroken father revealed he had received haunting text messages from his daughter’s phone after her death.

The dad, a lawyer in Edinburgh, told Greek cops he was sent several messages for two weeks after Elisabeth’s passing from a man now being viewed as the prime suspect.

One message sent on the last day she was seen alive said she “needed some time to herself” and “wanted to be alone for a while”.



An officer told the Sun that the emergence of the messages has helped investigators track the location of phone.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They said: “They were sent from Athens and it is clear whoever sent them was trying to buy time.”

The investigation remains ongoing.

News.title: Council house where Ann Widdecombe’s ‘killer’ lived is sealed up with steel shutters after man, 28, charged with murder
News.content:
SEALED UP Council house where Ann Widdecombe’s ‘killer’ lived is sealed up with steel shutters after man, 28, charged with murder

THE council house home of Ann Widdecombe’s alleged killer has been sealed up with steel shutters.

Joshua Kerry, 28, was arrested at the red-brick terraced property in Rotherham, South Yorkshire, four days after the veteran politician was murdered.



The 78-year-old was struck over the head 21 times with a hammer at her remote home on July 8, a court was told.

A kitchen camera is said to have caught the alleged killer entering her Dartmoor bungalow as the Reform spokeswoman ate lunch.



He is believed to have been inside for just two minutes before driving off.

Separate CCTV footage obtained by The Sun showed Kerry leaving his home on the morning of the murder and returning later that night.

Ring doorbell footage also captured the moment cops pounced on their prime suspect.

His home was forensically searched and his red Vauxhall Corsa seized.



Kerry was arrested on suspicion of murder and then further arrested for the alleged “commission, preparation and instigation” of a terrorist act.

The doors and windows of his former home were this week covered by steel shutters.

He has not been charged under terrorist legislation, but police say investigations continue to try to establish whether the motive was political.

Kerry has since appeared at the Old Bailey charged with Strictly star Ann’s murder.

He was arrested 300 miles away from Widdecombe’s home when cops stormed his property.



It was confirmed to the court that an investigation into terrorist offences is ongoing, but no definite position had been reached.

During Kerry’s court appearances the court heard Ann had been eating her lunch when a man arrived at her property in a red Vauxhall Corsa.

He allegedly walked in through an open front door and asked Ann: “Don’t suppose you have bank cards and ID?”

The former MP was then hit 21 times with a hammer over the head before being tipped from her chair on to the floor, it was said.



Ann’s wallet was removed from her handbag and the suspect left just two minutes later, the court heard.

Ann had carried out two media interviews that morning and was due to appear in an online chat with C5’s Matt Allwright at 12.50pm that day, it was said.

Kerry appeared emotionless in the dock as he was flanked by two plain clothed police officers and single security guard.

He spoke only to confirm his name, date of birth and address during the hearing.



At the Old Bailey it was heard Kerry allegedly hit Ann in a “planned and targeted” attack carried out with a “ferocity of violence.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The defendant was then remanded into custody ahead of a hearing on October 9.

He was driven away from court by counter-terror cops in a three-car escort of a Mercedes, Land Rover Defender and Kia.

News.title: Map reveals UK’s worst stalking and harassment hotspots – as offences soar with thousands more attacks in the last year
News.content:
THE UK’s worst stalking and harassment hotspots have been revealed as numbers continue to soar, according to new statistics.

Shocking new figures show 623,574 incidents of stalking and harassment recorded in England and Wales in the year to March 2026 – a 4 per cent rise, or 24,526, compared to the previous year.

But there’s one area that has emerged as the country’s worst with a rate of 18.7 stalking and harassment offences per 1,000 people – soaring above the national average of 10.1.



West Yorkshire Police, the fourth largest police force in the UK, recorded the highest rate of stalking and harassment cases per head, according to Home Office data.



The force covers five areas in the county – Bradford, Calderdale, Kirklees, Leeds, and Wakefield – and also ranked as the second worst area for sexual offences.

Remarkably, the figure of 10,639 offences is one percentage point down on the previous year.

Overall, police recorded stalking and harassment increased by 4 per cent to 623,574 offences.

The ONS say this is because of a 6 per cent rise in stalking to 143,704 offences and a 6 per cent rise in harassment – including racially or religiously aggravated harassment – to 320,914 offences.

And the area to see the biggest increase over the last twelve months was Devon and Cornwall which saw an astonishing 32 per cent surge.



There was also a 14 per cent rise recorded in London, a 13 per cent rise in Essex and a 12 per cent rise in Hertfordshire.

Meanwhile, British Transport Police recorded a horrifying 34 per cent rise in stalking and harassment across railways in England and Wales.

The second worst area for stalking and harassment offences recorded by police is Avon and Somerset where 15.0 offences were recorded per 1,000 people.

It is closely followed by Humberside (14.6), Greater Manchester (14.4), Cleveland (14.0) and Gwent (13.9).

London still places below the national average with a rate of 7.0 stalking and harassment offences per 1,000 despite the percentage increase.



In October last year, Samuel Hunter, 33, was jailed for bombarding a woman with unwanted messages, tracking her car and assaulting her.

He was sentenced at Leeds Crown Court after he admitted a series of offences against the woman in addition to stalking offences against another woman and a man.

During a period of between September and December 2024, he emailed her 95 times and rang 130 times.



Elsewhere, a “cruel” man who traumatised four women was sentenced to 12 months behind bars for stalking in Bristol.

Piersaverio Finizio, aged 30, approached four women who were on their own.

Police said on one occassion he told a victim three times “you look lonely, I want to be your valentine” before he followed her as she fled.

In another incident, he told a woman he would accompany her to where she was going before saying “you will be an angel soon” and asking for her phone number several times.

One victim said in a statement read out at court: “Since it happened, I haven’t known peace. I’m anxious all the time. I flinch at footsteps or when someone walks too close. I scan faces in crowds, always expecting to see him again.



Full list of areas ranked by stalking and harassment offences Stalking and harassment offences per 1,000 people in year to March 2026 West Yorkshire 18.7 Avon and Somerset 15.0 Humebrside 14.6 Greater Manchester 14.4 Cleveland 14.0 Gwent 13.9 Staffordshire 13.7 South Yorkshire 13.5 Derbyshire 12.9 North Wales 12.3 South Wales 11.9 Dyfed-Powys 11.7 Durham 11.7 Cheshire 11.6 West Midlands 11.4 Merseyside 11.3 Lancashire 10.8 Northumbria 10.4 Devon and Cornwall 10.4 Hampshire 10.2 Cumbria 10.1 Kent 9.8 Gloucestershire 9.7 Essex 9.7 Northamptonshire 9.4 Leicestershire 9.2 Hertfordshire 9.0 West Mercia 8.6 Lincolnshire 8.5 Nottinghamshire 8.5 Cambridgeshire 7.6 Thames Valley 7.5 Bedfordshire 7.0 Metropolitan Police 7.0 Dorset 6.9 Warwickshire 6.7 Surrey 6.6 Sussex 6.5 Norfolk 6.1 Wiltshire 5.8 North Yorkshire 5.3 Suffolk 4.8

“That first time, he said, ‘it must be scary being a girl at night’. That sentence broke something in me. It wasn’t just cruel, it was deliberate. He knew what he was doing.”

The police force area with the lowest number of stalking and harassment offences was Suffolk (4.8 per 1,000), followed by North Yorkshire (5.3).

In the year to March 2026, of people aged 16 and above, the ONS said around 4.9million people had experienced some form of harassment, including one-off incidents.

That marks a 8.3 per cent increase compared to incidents in the year to March 2025.

They added that an estimated 1.1million people experienced repeated harassment in the last year.



Earlier this year, the Government published its Crime and Policing Act 2026 which makes it easier for Stalking Protection Orders (SPOs) to be made.

SPOs were introduced in 2020 to restrict the activities of suspected offenders without the need for them to be convicted first – breaching one can result in five years in prison, an unlimited fine or both.

And in March, the CPS launched its first Stalking Action Plan to help prosecutors “tackle the offence in the digital age”.

On National Striking Awareness Week in April, Professor Clive Ruggles, father of Alice Ruggles and Chair of Alice Ruggles Trust said: “Ten years ago, my daughter Alice was stalked relentlessly by an ex-boyfriend after she ended their relationship.

“Over the next three months, the stalking rapidly escalated. He then broke into her flat and killed her. Could her death have been prevented if the right measures had been taken during those three months? I absolutely believe so.



“This keeps happening and we need to stop it. We urgently need practitioners across criminal justice and beyond to better understand the risks of stalking and the very real danger of escalation all the way to homicide.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Emma Lingley-Clark, Interim Chief Executive Officer of the Suzy Lamplugh Trust added: “If the Government is serious about its commitment to halve violence against women and girls it must mandate specialist independent training for criminal justice professionals working on stalking cases and ensure that stalking is included in the ‘Steps to Safety’ training programme for healthcare professionals.

“Failure to do so will continue to cost lives.”

News.title: Two helicopters smash into each other while fighting wildfires in terrifying mid-air collision
News.content:
Two helicopters smash into each other while fighting wildfires in terrifying mid-air collision

Two helicopters have crashed into each other while putting out wildfires west of Athens in Greece

View Image A firefighting helicopter drops water over a wildfire in the area of Porto Germeno (file photo) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Two firefighting helicopters have collided in mid-air while attempting to tackle wildfires west of Athens, Greece.

‌



A search and rescue operation is underway to locate the crews in the ⁠Psatha area, Greece's fire ⁠department said.

‌



Each helicopter had two people on board.

‌



"During the aerial firefighting operation, two BELL helicopters, leased by the fire department, with a crew of two people each, crashed in the wider area of Psatha, Attica," the department said in a statement.

"The helicopters had taken off from the Elefsina military airport. The search and rescue operation is under way," they added.

Article continues below

Parts of Greece have been hit particularly hard by the spate of wildfires that have gripped Europe this summer, with three firefighters tragically losing their lives battling blazes in Crete and the mainland earlier this week.

Nearly 500 Greek firefighters have been deployed to the region, assisted by personnel from France and Romania.

News.title: UK wildfires cause devastation to rare wildlife habitats that could take 25 years to recover
News.content:
UK wildfires cause devastation to rare wildlife habitats that could take 25 years to recover

Hundreds of wildfires devastated areas across the UK from Snowdownia National Park to Suffolk, after the driest July in England and Wales since records began

Video shows destruction of Suffolk wildfires

Rare wildlife habitats that have been devastated in the UK heatwave could take 25 years to recover, according to conservationists.

‌



Cooler temperatures forecast for many parts of the UK might ease the pressure on firefighters. But the brief respite came after crews responded to hundreds of grassland fires from the Snowdownia National Park to Suffolk, after the driest July in England and Wales since records began.

‌



Campaigners and Government Ministers warned that extreme weather could become the 'new normal' due to gobal warming. Stark images showed hundreds of acres of land were destroyed in Sychnant Pass in North Wales last month.

‌



View 6 Images Scorched earth shown after the wildfires in Wales (Image: Patrick O'Neill / SWNS)

Wildfire expert delivers sobering warning about impact of climate change READ MORE :

A major incident was declared after the flames on the Conwy Mountain forced the evacuation of 36 homes due to the fast-moving fire on July 12. Dramatic photos now show acres of scorched earth.

Much of the Sychnant Pass is in Snowdonia National Park where swathes of land are a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest. North Wales Fire and Rescue Service (NWFRS) said: "We continue to urge the public to stay away from affected areas as we are aware of people travelling to wildfire locations to take aerial photographs and videos.

‌



View 6 Images The scene of devastation follwing the recent wildfire which spread out over the Sychnant Pass in Wales (Image: Patrick O'Neill / SWNS)

"Mountain rescue colleagues have reported an increase in visitors to affected areas with the intention of 'wild camping.' This is not only dangerous but places an additional strain on resources and can hinder firefighting and emergency access.

‌



"Please avoid using disposable barbecues, ensure cigarettes are fully extinguished, take litter home and never leave glass bottles behind, as these can increase the risk of wildfire."

England and Wales are set for the driest July since records began. The Met Office described last month as an 'exceptional combination of extreme heat, abundant sunshine and an almost complete absence of rainfall'.

View 6 Images The habitat could take up to 25 years to recover (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

‌



Provisional statistics showed only 5.6mm of rain fell in England in July - less than half the previous record low of 13.4mm set in 1911. Wales saw only 7.9mm, almost a third of the previous record of 22.6mm also set in 1911. The conditions have left much of England and Wales in drought, with more than 24 million people under official hosepipe bans.

The worst blaze hit Dunwich Heath in Suffolk, which firefighters brought under control. National Trust's director-general Hilary McGrady described the loss of an important habitat for some of the UK's rarest species as 'devastating'. Adam Rowlands, the RSPB's area manager in Suffolk, told the BBC that the habitats devastated by the 'utterly sickening' fire could take up to 25 years to recover.

View 6 Images The wildfire in Suffolk devastated habitats important for some of the UK's rarest species (Image: Humphrey Nemar/PA Wire)

‌



"The acrid smell, it's not just smoke, you have a sense that animals have perished in the flames," he said. The 371-acre blaze on the heath, three miles from the Sizewell B nuclear power plant, began at the nearby RSPB Minsmere wetland reserve at 5.30 p.m. on Wednesday.

A shortage of certain food products may also hit UK supplies if the current drought conditions continue. National Farmers' Union (NFU) President Tom Bradshaw said wheat and oat yields were "very, very poor" this year and warned livestock farmers have had to use their winter feed rations because they couldn't grow grass.

‌



View 6 Images An aerial view shows smoke rising from wildfires near Dunwich Heath (Image: TOLGA AKMEN/EPA/Shutterstock)

Mr Bradshaw said high temperatures and drought conditions have placed all areas of farming under increasing pressure. He said vegetable producers are running low on water, which reduces the amount of food produced in the UK and increases the cost of growing it.

‌



"We can't change what's happening at the moment, there is no water in our rivers, but we must use this to take action for the future," he told the BBC. "We have to recognise that water security is a critical part of our food security and food security is our national security."

More reservoirs are needed as water collected during winter is instead pumped out into the North Sea. "We can't change what's happening at the moment, there is no water in our rivers, but we must use this to take action for the future," he added.

View 6 Images Sychnant Pass in Wales was one of the areas worst hit by the wildfires. (Image: Patrick O'Neill / SWNS)

Article continues below

He suggested farmers should be given tax breaks to build water storage systems to prepare for the years ahead. He warned: "We have taken our food supply for granted for far too long. The climates of those other countries around the world that we currently rely on to produce our food and vegetables are changing as well. It does feel like there is going to be some shortage of food products."

Drought has been declared across large parts of England and all of Wales as successive heatwaves strained water supplies, with more than 20 million people now under hosepipe bans. Amber heat health alerts have also been issued for large parts of England, including the Midlands, the South-East and the South West, until Wednesday.

The UK Health Security Agency has issued amber heat health alerts for the East Midlands, East of England, London and the south-east up to 9am on Wednesday, August 5. Yellow alerts are also in place for the North West, Yorkshire, West Midlands and the South West for the same period.

News.title: 'Royal shake-up could prove decisive for Prince Harry's public reunion with King Charles'
News.content:
Forlorn, battered and bruised from his experiences in the courtroom, Prince Harry declared he could no longer fight anymore - for in his own words, “life is precious”.

That sentence was uttered more than a year ago, following the loss of his appeal over the levels of security he believes he and his family are entitled to while in the UK.

Since Harry and his wife Meghan quit their royal roles in 2020, the Duke of Sussex has been no stranger to the court room, nor to earning incredible amounts of money at the expense of the family he left behind.

Prince Harry could face paying millions out of own pocket after failed legal action READ MORE :

View 4 Images Harry with his father at the first Invictus Games in London in 2014 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Only now, after the book promos, the interviews and the Netflix series have all but dried up, he is seeking reconciliation with his loved ones that he has largely been estranged from for the past six years.

There is of course the matter of his father’s health. To his credit, Harry did drop everything, although no one can be quite sure how full his schedule is aside from his various legal disputes, to rush to be by his father’s side following his announcement in February 2024 that he had been diagnosed with cancer.

Since that meeting, which lasted just 30 minutes, Harry’s dealings with the King have been brief and showed little signs of significantly moving toward the rapprochement he now craves.

The King has shown no signs of clearing the decks for that to happen, continuing with a packed schedule of commitments and engagements both at home and abroad. Those close to him suggest if you didn’t know his diagnosis, there would be little clue to the suffering he has endured.

‌



View 4 Images Harry in happier days with his father and older brother, Prince William (Image: Getty Images)

Weekly treatments, a hospitalisation mid-way through - described merely as “a bump in the road” - and the weight of expectation he has put on himself to secure a legacy, while not fully knowing his prognosis or how his treatment may turn out in the long run.

Those in his circle suggest that is the absolute demonstration of service and duty that has become such a debate to those that have left the camp.

Long before the announcement that they were leaving their royal roles in search of “financial freedom”, Harry and Meghan plotted a scenario where they would be the first royals to create a new way of working for The Firm.

‌



The ‘half in-half out’ model suggested was roundly shot down by the late Queen Elizabeth II leading to the Duke and Duchess of Sussex having to leave the institution with nothing other than their association with the royal family.

View 4 Images Harry has said he wants reconciliation with his family (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

For a good while, that connection served as almost the sole vehicle to earning tens of millions of pounds in the corporate world, seemingly without regard to the destruction of the relationships they had vowed to honour. There is no doubt, aside from those who fawn over their every announcement or TV appearance, their star has fallen along with their global popularity.

What better way to resurrect one’s profile than to cosy up to the royal family who enjoy favourable approval ratings and a monarchy who has garnered as much respect for his global statesman role, as he has genuine sympathy for the way he has handled this particular family fallout.

‌



Harry and Meghan’s latest meeting with the King and Queen, who attended as a watchful eye over any potential deviations from the planned pleasantries, is a key moment for the Sussexes. There is little chance the Prince and Princess of Wales will welcome them back into palace grounds, let alone the royal fold.

Now I have learned that Harry wants to capitalise on this new found relationship by planning to convince his father to be by his side for the homecoming of his Invictus Games event.

It just so happens that the one man who would have had the power to convince the monarch against the idea, the King and Queen’s principal private secretary Sir Clive Alderton, is to step down from his role next year after more than two decades of service to the royal household. This may yet prove decisive in Harry’s plan to achieve a very public reunion.

‌

News.title: Prince Harry hopes to convince King Charles to join him at UK Invictus Games
News.content:
Prince Harry is hoping to convince the King to appear with him at the 2027 Invictus Games in Birmingham, sources have revealed.

The Duke of Sussex is planning to offer a major reconciliation gesture to his father, as he brings the Games back to the country of his birth for the first time since its launch in 2014. The prince's plan could see the monarch join him at major events during the Games - or at one of the opening or closing ceremonies during the home event.

Harry has been buoyed by his recent meeting with the King, which took place earlier this month, alongside his wife Meghan and their two children, Archie and Lilibet.

Prince Harry could face paying millions out of own pocket after failed legal action READ MORE :

View 5 Images Prince Harry is hoping to convince the King to appear with him in public at the 2027 Invictus Games (Image: WWD via Getty Images)

‌



The family gathering, which the Queen also attended, took place at the monarch’s Highgrove estate in Gloucestershire, at the end of a stressful week for the duke. Harry, 41, recently visited the UK for the one year countdown celebration at the National Exhibition Centre (NEC) in Birmingham.

Harry was forced to find alternative accommodation after publicly stating he would stay at a royal residence during his week long trip, only for Buckingham Palace to deny him saying he had responded to the invitation in time.

The duke was also handed a devastating loss in his high stakes legal battle against Associated Newspapers, publishers of the Daily Mail and Mail Online, when all 97 claims made by Harry and his six other co-claimants were dismissed in full.

Harry, who has lived permanently in California since he and Meghan quit their royal roles in 2020, had planned for his family to join him in the UK for the entirety of his visit, but was forced to alter arrangements when he learned he would not be granted taxpayer funded security.

‌



View 5 Images Harry is due to travel back to the UK in September for the WellChild Awards, that he has supported for 15 years (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

However, Meghan - who was due to appear with Harry on stage before she pulled out of traveling to London or attending any public engagements - and the children did eventually reunite with him later in the week, when Harry managed to secure a meeting with the King.

The duke has been buoyed by the emotional reunion with his father, alongside his wife Meghan and their children, earlier this month for the first time in four years.

Sources have revealed Harry wants to arrange further meetings with the monarch to allow him to spend time with his grandchildren, who he has hardly seen since the Duke and Duchess quit their royal roles in 2020 and moved to the United States.

‌



One insider said: “Harry’s intention is two fold. He would love the King’s support at the Games, while having his father by his side would also add considerable weight to his argument for security for his family to accompany him on the trip. “

Harry is due to return to London for the annual WellChild Awards in September, the charity he has supported for 15 years. It is understood that he will accept an offer from his father the king to stay at Buckingham Palace when he returns to Britain, marking a stunning turnaround from the last time he was in the UK.

The Mirror revealed earlier this month that Harry is to continue his controversial campaign demanding taxpayer funded security - paving the way for future visits with his family.

View 5 Images Harry's relationship with the King has been strained since the prince left his royal role in 2020 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Sources close to the duke suggest his desire to have his father by his side at next year’s Invictus Games serves a dual purpose. Another source said: “Next year is a big deal for Harry. He is determined that the Birmingham Games will be the best ever and it would mean the world to him to have his father there." Another royal source suggested the King “would welcome the opportunity to see his grandchildren again”.

Harry’s case against the Daily Mail was heard in court again on Wednesday, with the trial judge asked to rule over whether the duke and other household names have to pay millions of pounds to cover the costs of their failed legal action.

A group of seven household names, which also includes Baroness Doreen Lawrence and Sir Elton John, sued Associated Newspapers Limited (ANL) over allegations of unlawful information-gathering.

ANL strongly denied the claims, which were heard at an 11-week trial in London earlier this year. On July 7, Mr Justice Nicklin dismissed the claims in their entirety in a 436-page judgment and the cases returned to the High Court for a hearing on Wednesday over costs.

‌



View 5 Images The Duchess of Sussex is keen on joining Prince Harry at next year's Invictus Games in Birmingham after cancelling plans to attend the event this year (Image: ANP/AFP via Getty Images)

The court heard there was a shortfall between their insurance cover and ANL’s costs which are more than £34 million. After the trial Harry and Baroness Lawrence, mother of murdered teenager Stephen Lawrence, called the case “an obvious whitewash”.

Harry has since returned to California and is continuing with planning for next year’s Games. He originally launched the global event in London in 2014, with the competition aiming to challenge "perceptions of disability, champion adaptive sport, and demonstrate the resilience, determination and unconquered spirit of wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans”.

It has since been held in Orlando, Toronto, Sydney, The Hague, Düsseldorf and Vancouver-Whistler, Canada for the inaugural winter games in 2025.

‌



In early July, Harry travelled to Britain to attend the One Year To Go ceremony, where he competed in a variety of sports alongside former Labour minister Al Carns and TV personality Alison Hammond.

Following his visit to the UK, Harry revealed that the Games will next be held in Daejeon, South Korea. The announcement means the event, held every two years, will be brought to Asia for the very first time.

The duke said he was “delighted” for the city to stage the sporting competition for its first time on the continent. The event will take place between October 6-15, 2029 in and around the Daejeon Convention Centre in Yuseong-gu. It will bring together 550 competitors from 26 nations, supported by 1,100 family members and friends in 12 sports.

‌

News.title: Conman used semi-naked women to sell fake Pablo Escobar-branded flamethrowers and smartphones
News.content:
Conman used semi-naked women to sell fake Pablo Escobar-branded flamethrowers and smartphones

Olof Kyros Gustafsson, 32, CEO of Escobar Inc, ran an international fraud scheme where he tricked buyers of merchandise, which he falsely claimed was linked to Colombian drug lord

View 4 Images Gustafsson used scantily clad models to advertise goods (Image: Credit: Escobar Inc)

A fraudster who used Pablo Escobar’s name to market flamethrowers and luxury goods using scantily clad models which he never delivered has been jailed.

‌



Olof Kyros Gustafsson, 32, CEO of Escobar Inc, ran an international fraud scheme where he tricked buyers of merchandise, which he claimed was linked to the infamous late Colombian drug lord.

‌



The Swedish national, who had the nickname El Silencio, used semi-naked women to advertise the products like branded phones and an “Escobar Flamethrower” but when people bought them online, they were never delivered.

‌



He registered Escobar Inc in Puerto Rico and held successor-in-interest rights to the persona of Pablo Escobar who was the head of the Medellin Cartel and killed in 1993.

View 4 Images Gustafsson has been jailed (Image: Instagram)

Gustafsson used that notoriety to market items like the "Escobar Flamethrower" gold foldable smartphones, and a physical cryptocurrency called "Escobar Cash" at prices far lower than what would be the normal market price from 2019 to 2023.

‌



He even sent foil-wrapped Samsung Galaxy flip phones to tech reviewers to drum up public demand. When paying customers demanded refunds for non-existent goods, Gustafsson mailed them items like a "Certificate of Ownership" or promotional books instead.

View 4 Images People would buy goods advertised that never arrived (Image: Credit: Escobar Inc)

And in so doing Gustafsson raked in a $1.3million fortune but some suspicious recipients quickly noticed red flags and YouTuber Marques Brownlee highlighted the scam in a video posted in 2024. “Those people were getting scammed out of their money,” he said. “Honestly, in hindsight, I don’t know how they thought they were gonna get away with this.”

‌



Brownlee then claimed he was visited by the FBI who asked for the phone and communications which he had had with Escobar Inc.

The money that Gustafsson is alleged to have been laundered from bank accounts in the United States, Sweden, and the United Arab Emirates.

View 4 Images Pablo Escobar was the head of the Medellin Cartel (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Article continues below

He was extradited from Spain in 2023 back to the US, and he has been in federal custody since March 2025. He previously pleaded guilty in July 2025 to a myriad of fraud and money-laundering charges and has now been jailed to four years in prison by a Los Angeles court.

A statement from the US Attorney's Office read: "A Swedish national who licensed the rights of the late Colombian narco-terrorist Pablo Escobar was sentenced today to 48 months in federal prison for defrauding investors by marketing and selling products – including flamethrowers and cellphones – that he never delivered.

"Olof Kyros Gustafsson, 32, a.k.a. “El Silencio,” was sentenced by United States District Judge Fernando L. Aenlle-Rocha, who also fined him $25,000, and ordered him to pay $1,300,193 in restitution. Gustafsson has agreed to forfeit funds that were proceeds of the fraud schemes, including money currently held in a bank account in Sweden."

News.title: What are legal rights when neighbour's CCTV or Ring doorbell points at your house
News.content:
What are legal rights when neighbour's CCTV or Ring doorbell points at your house

It's understandable if your neighbour's camera makes you feel uncomfortable

View 2 Images Do you have an issue with a neighbour's smart doorbell device? (Image: Getty Images)

Spotting a neighbour's CCTV camera or video doorbell pointing towards your property can quickly raise concerns about privacy. However, whether they are breaking the law depends on more than simply where the camera is facing.

‌



According to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), homeowners are generally free to install CCTV or smart doorbells to protect their property. But if the device captures images or audio beyond the boundary of their home, such as a neighbour's garden, driveway or a public footpath, data protection laws are likely to apply.

‌



The government's guidance on domestic CCTV says cameras should be positioned to minimise intrusion into other people's privacy wherever possible. It advises homeowners to think carefully about what their system records and whether less intrusive options, such as changing the camera angle or using privacy settings, could achieve the same level of security.

‌



That does not mean a camera is automatically unlawful simply because part of your property appears in view. The ICO says many domestic systems cannot avoid capturing small areas outside the owner's boundary, but the person operating the camera must have a legitimate reason for doing so and comply with their obligations under data protection law if those recordings include neighbouring property or public spaces.

Mum loses seven teeth and use of hand after tripping on pothole and landing face-first in another READ MORE :

If you are concerned, the first step is usually to speak to your neighbour. According to the ICO, many disputes can be resolved by explaining your concerns, as the camera owner may be willing to reposition the device or activate privacy masking to block parts of the image.

‌



People recorded by a domestic CCTV system may also have certain rights under UK data protection law. The ICO says you can ask the camera owner whether you are being recorded, object to the processing of your personal data in some circumstances and request a copy of footage containing your image through a subject access request.

View 2 Images Can you prove it is an invasion of your privacy? (Image: sturti)

If informal discussions fail, complaints about domestic CCTV can be raised with the ICO. According to the regulator, it may consider whether the camera owner is meeting their legal responsibilities where data protection law applies, although not every complaint will result in enforcement action.

Article continues below

It is also important to remember that simply owning a Ring doorbell or CCTV system is not, on its own, evidence of wrongdoing. The government says many people install surveillance devices for legitimate reasons such as deterring crime and protecting their home, provided they operate them responsibly and respect the privacy of others.

If the issue develops into a wider disagreement with your neighbour, it may be worth attempting mediation before considering legal action. GOV.UK recommends trying to resolve neighbour disputes informally where possible, as court proceedings can be time-consuming and costly.

Ultimately, the key question is not whether the camera points towards your home but what it records and how the footage is used. If your neighbour's CCTV or Ring doorbell captures areas beyond their property, they may need to comply with UK data protection laws, but that does not automatically mean the camera must be removed.

News.title: 'I fell in love with an army general, then he stole my children's £128,000 inheritance'
News.content:
A retired teacher who was conned out of her life savings by a romance scammer posing as a retired British Army general has warned about the dangers of online dating. Losing her husband of 42 years, Diana Jenkins - not her real name - was lonely when she fell for a man who she thought was a retired military officer, with a knighthood.

Saying he had been recommissioned to perform sensitive military duties overseas, charming, attentive and patient, he sent daily messages asking how she was feeling. When he said he loved her, Diana believed him - she was falling in love with him too. But, after sending him more than £128,000 - the bulk of her life savings - she realised she’d fallen for a massive scam.

Looking back, the intelligent 67-year-old from the London area can’t believe she allowed herself to be fooled. Even now, more than two years since the debacle, she is using a pseudonym, as she can’t bring herself to tell her adult son what happened. Diana’s revelations come as Freeview channel Great! TV’s Great Romance becomes the first TV channel to donate commercial airtime to the National Crime Agency, in order to tackle the growing menace of romance fraud.

Odyssey's Matt Damon says 45 year wait for phone call from Ben Affleck is finally over READ MORE :

Cape Fear stars tell of life-changing advice from Hollywood greats READ MORE :

View 6 Images The intelligent 67-year-old exchanged daily messages with the man she thought was a retired Army general (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Still kicking herself, Diana says: “Why did I do that? I know I was lonely and vulnerable but still…” Three years before she met the ‘general’ online in October 2022, Diana's world had fallen apart, when her husband died from heart failure. She says: "It was a massive shock. In the end I suffered a nervous breakdown.”

Her son moved in to care for her and she took time off from her adult education job. Lonely, Diana joined an international pen-pal website. She says: "It wasn't really about finding romance, but friendship. You write a profile and people from all over the world can get in touch."

One message stood out, supposedly from the retired general, who had been called back into service to do covert work in Mali. With a family background in the military, his post caught Diana’s attention. She checked out his name online and found photographs, videos, articles and even pictures of him with Queen Camilla. Diana says: "I looked him up and everything seemed genuine.”

But investigators say sophisticated romance fraudsters rarely invent entirely fictional identities, instead stealing the names and photographs of respectable people whose public profiles lend instant credibility. Soon exchanging private messages, he said he could not voice or video call because of his covert work and Diana accepted that.

‌



She says: "He was just the person I'd been looking for. He was kind and attentive. We were messaging at least once every day, often more. We became very close, even though we’d not actually spoken or seen each other. Then he told me he loved me. And I believed I was in love with him too."

View 6 Images The romance scammer supplied official-looking documents

Investing months in building trust, the scammer soon became the person Diana turned to every day. Three months in, he told her that, while serving in Mali, he had discovered a cache of gold. Legally his, it needed to be transported through Turkey to get to Britain. But there were taxes to pay.

Because he was getting divorced, his finances were tied up in a joint bank account with his estranged wife. Could Diana possibly help? He needed just £4,000 - and produced official-looking documents bearing what appeared to be London Port Authority stamps and certificates. Diana remembers: “They looked so genuine. There were certificates and stamps and everything.”.

‌



But the costs kept growing, with increasing storage charges, then the shipment had been held up, incurring more fees. There was always another obstacle. Another cost. Each explanation sounded plausible enough. And the ‘general’ reassured Diana that the gold would arrive, then he would return to Britain and they could start their life together.

Diana recalls: "There was always another reason why more money had to be paid. But I believed him." Living in a cycle of hope, anxiety and mounting financial demands, she still hadn’t seen or heard him and her suspicions were aroused. But she’d parted with thousands of pounds and, like so many victims of sophisticated fraud, she thought one final payment would unlock everything.

Diana, who made 16 bank transfers in all, says: “In the end almost everything I had put aside for my retirement was gone. This was my children’s inheritance…what had I done?” Continuing to love bomb her, Diana wanted to believe the ‘general.’ She explains: "When you've been lonely and you've lost someone you've been with for over 40 years, hearing those things means everything."

View 6 Images Maxwell Rusey posed as a British Army general (Image: Kent Police / SWNS)

‌



Then, the ‘general’ messaged saying he was finally coming home - even sending her a copy of his airline boarding pass, plus the flight number, departure details and arrival time at Heathrow. But, still suspicious, Diana phoned the airline. No one with his name was on that flight. Hoping she was wrong, she travelled to Heathrow Airport to meet him.

He never appeared. Instead, she was told he’d been whisked away by a Ministry of Defence official for a debriefing. Then he was sent urgently to Ukraine for more hush-hush operations. Diana demanded that he rang her, so she could hear his voice. She says: “That’s when the penny dropped. Instead of the cultured tone of a British general it was someone speaking in a foreign accent. I was devastated.”

Threatening him with the police, the fraudster told her the gold shipment was illegal and she would be implicated if she involved them. She says: “He told me I would go down with him. I was horrified and didn’t know what to do.”

Fortunately, by then, staff at the Halifax, where she banked, had noticed the extraordinary pattern of payments leaving her account and contacted her. Broken, Diana - who has since told her daughter, but not her son, the truth - told them everything and they persuaded her to go to the police, who arrested the fake general in the UK.

‌



View 6 Images The conman sent his victim official looking documents

And in September 2024 her conman, Maxwell Rusey, 53, who had been operating from Nuneaton, Warwickshire, was jailed for five years for the romance fraud at Woolwich Crown Court. After Diana contacted the Financial Ombudsman, the Halifax reimbursed every penny of the £128,000 he had taken.

There is a happy ending, as Diana has found genuine love with a man she did not meet online. Diana says: “These romance fraudsters do not target people because they are gullible. They target you because you're lonely. They're very clever. They win your emotions over. And if you're vulnerable, they'll use that against you. The moment they ask for money, that's it. Walk away.”

A spokesperson for the National Crime Agency says: “Diana is incredibly brave to come forward and share her story. We hope it will serve as a warning to thousands of vulnerable potential victims.”

‌



Diana’s tips to protect against romance scammers:

Take things slowly

Protect your personal information

Don't reveal too much about yourself

Be wary of anyone who quickly declares their love

Never send money

View 6 Images Great! TV is giving commercial advertising space to the National Crime Agency on Great! Romance to warn against romance scammers

Broadcaster Great! TV is the first UK television company to hand commercial advertising airtime - in peak-time slots across Freeview, Sky and Virgin Media - to the National Crime Agency, in a bid to stamp out romance fraud. Figures released by Report Fraud reveal that from April 2025 to March 2026 there were 12,348 reports of romance fraud, with victims - 51% of whom were aged 50+ - losing £116 million.

‌



The NCA’s Nick Sharp said of the campaign, featuring 11 bespoke adverts which tie romance fraud advice to the storylines of Great! romantic films: “Raising awareness as a form of prevention. This campaign with Great Romance is designed to do exactly that.”

Great Marketing Director Kate Gartland said: “This joint campaign with the NCA will give viewers the awareness they need to spot the tell tale signs and protect themselves and their friends and family from these devastating crimes.”

News.title: Premium Bond 'delay' alert as customers given new date to claim big money wins
News.content:
Premium Bond 'delay' alert as customers given new date to claim big money wins

Millions of Premium Bond customers are being forced to wait just that little bit longer to see if they have won £1 million

View 2 Images The August draw is expected to see more than 6.4 million prizes paid out

August is finally here, but Premium Bond holders will notice something has changed. Millions of customers must now wait a little longer to find out whether they have landed a huge prize after NS&I issued a new update.

‌



Normally, Premium Bond draws take place at the start of each month. However, because August 1 falls on a weekend this year, the August 2026 draw will instead be held on Monday, August 3.

‌



That means the two £1 million jackpot winners will learn of their life-changing windfall on Monday. The remaining prize winners will be able to check whether they've won from Tuesday, August 4, when NS&I updates its online Prize Checker and app.

‌



The August draw is expected to see more than 6.4 million prizes paid out, with a total prize fund of around £447 million. Alongside the two millionaire prizes, there will also be awards worth £100,000, £50,000, £25,000 and thousands of smaller tax-free prizes down to £25.

Customers who have registered for notifications may receive an email or text from NS&I if they have won. Those alerts do not reveal the prize amount, meaning savers will still need to use the Prize Checker to find out how much they've received.

‌



The quickest way to check is through the official NS&I Prize Checker, which is available online and through the Premium Bonds app. According to NS&I, the checker also displays prizes won in the previous six draws, along with any older unclaimed prizes linked to your holder's number.

View 2 Images NS&I has announced key changes to the Premium Bonds scheme (Image: Getty)

Anyone hoping to take part in future draws should remember that newly purchased Premium Bonds are not entered immediately. NS&I says bonds must be held for one full calendar month before they become eligible for a prize draw.

Article continues below

The delay may leave savers waiting an extra couple of days, but it will not affect their chances of winning. Premium Bonds continue to offer tax-free prizes backed by HM Treasury, with savers able to hold up to £50,000 worth of bonds.

Even if you don't receive a notification this month, it could still be worth checking your account. NS&I says there is no time limit to claim a Premium Bonds prize, with thousands of winning prizes remaining unclaimed because customers have moved house or failed to update their contact details.

News.title: Prolonged drought could cause shortage of some foods, farmers' union head says
News.content:
There could be a shortage of certain food products if the current drought conditions continue, the National Farmers' Union (NFU) has warned.

NFU president Tom Bradshaw said yields of wheat and oats were "very, very poor" this year and warned livestock farmers have had to use their winter feed rations because they have been unable to grow grass.

Drought has been declared across large parts of England and the whole of Wales as successive heatwaves left water supplies under strain, with more than 20 million people now under hosepipe bans.

Amber heat health alerts have also been issued for large parts of England, including the Midlands, the south-east and south-west of England, until Wednesday.

News.title: Man admits killing British woman found in suitcase, Greek police say
News.content:
Greek police say a man has admitted killing a Scottish woman whose body was found in a suitcase in an abandoned building.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, was found in the Kypseli district of Athens on 18 July, days after she was reported missing.

Local officers launched an investigation with cooperation from authorities in the US, the UK and Scotland, and now say they have arrested a 26-year-old man - the BBC understands he is from Afghanistan.

The force said he was brought to police headquarters on Thursday where he "confessed to his actions". He was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter, robbery and weapons offences, but the exact charges have yet to be finalised under the Greek legal system.

News.title: Fastest runner to cross the Alps says it was an incredible experience
News.content:
Runner Sophie Woods became the fastest person to complete the 2,000km (1242-mile) Via Alpina ultramarathon beating both the men's and women's record.

Woods ran the route through storms, heat of up to 37C and dodged floods and wildfires across eight countries.

"Through the whole thing, I was only ever thinking about the day, the hour, the sort of minute that I was in", the runner told BBC Breakfast.

The previous record was 35 days and Woods did it in just 29, crediting ice cream slushies for helping her power through.

News.title: Why I don't regret choosing a vasectomy in my 20s
News.content:
Because he was asking for a vasectomy at such a young age, Sam had prepared for the questions his doctor was going to ask him: Don't you think you're too young to know you don't want kids? Could you change your mind in future? You do know reversals are expensive and aren't always successful?

"[The doctor] actually said he had very recently changed his view," says Sam. "And that, if I had come in half a year earlier, he would have turned me away instantly."

His vasectomy took place a couple of months after he first contacted the clinic.

The questions from Sam's doctor were designed to ensure he was making a decision he could live with; men under 30 are more likely to regret a vasectomy, according to guidance from NHS Scotland, external.

Dr Sarah Salkeld, a former GP who is now a medical director for MSI Reproductive Choices, a group of clinics offering various contraceptives to NHS and private patients, says a vasectomy is "very safe and effective".

But she cautions it is important for men to "really think about" whether a vasectomy is right for them.

"We offer everyone counselling to talk about it if they want to, just toâ¦ make sure they've got all the information they need to make that decision."

She says reversals are not routinely available on the NHS as there are strict criteria for having one.

The NHS website points out that other forms of contraception, external are available to men, including condoms and the fertility awareness method - avoiding sex or using condoms on the days when their female partner is most fertile.

Sam told his doctor that, while he loved kids and had a happy childhood himself, he wanted to stay focused on his job as a sound designer for video games.

News.title: Solitude as a new aspirational lifestyle: 'We are not lonely'
News.content:
It's a Friday night. A young woman trudges back to her apartment after a day of work. She enters a spotless kitchen, unloads a bag of groceries, and unwraps a frozen pizza before sliding it in the oven.

What follows is a nightly routine that is almost meditative in its mundanity: she lights a candle and gazes briefly at the snow-covered landscape outside her window, piles a premade salad onto a plate with the pizza, and settles on her sofa to eat in front of the TV.

The tagline that accompanies the scene reads: "POV you're a childfree and single girl that has no friends and lives alone so this is how you spend your Friday night."

At the centre of the video â which has amassed seven million views on TikTok â is Lana Isa, a software sales manager in her 20s based in Toronto.

In addition to chronicling her nightly self-care routines, she takes her almost 400,000 followers across TikTok and Instagram on late-night fast food drives, reading sessions perched on a rock by the lake, even a saga of getting locked out of her apartment in the middle of the night.

Isa is part of a growing, albeit niche corner of the internet where content creators, many of them women, share their daily rituals of living alone, choosing to spotlight a lifestyle that prioritises peace and solitude - the antithesis of social media excess.
