For Isa, unveiling the "no friends" aspect of her life was less of a tagline, but the "reality" she had been living for several years.

News.title: Peak District's rebrand deal brings in cash but also criticism
News.content:
A deal between Peak District bosses and car firm Skoda to put up temporary signs welcoming tourists to "the Peaq District" in honour of the firm's new electric model has given the park authority's coffers a welcome boost.

However, it has also sparked protests from campaigners and residents unhappy about the commercial aspect of the arrangement.

One campaigner said: "If national parks are prepared to sell their very name to the highest bidder, then we're already on the path to industrial extraction of the most protected landscapes."

Park bosses have defended the "fantastic" deal and said the partnership brought in extra funds for conservation and heritage work.

With national parks continuing to grapple with funding pressures, could the partnership be a sign of things to come for the Peak District and beyond?

News.title: Ginger hair portraits show unexpected 'golden thread' connecting Americans
News.content:
For Kieran Dodds, photographing people with red hair has become something of an obsession over the past decade.

The 45-year-old, from Edinburgh, who is himself a "proud ginger", began taking pictures in his homeland in 2013 as part of a series examining Scottish identity.

His interest in the subject soon took him to other ginger hotspots such the Russian city of Perm and Jamaica's Treasure Beach.

His 2020 book Gingers spanned the world but after its release he noticed there was a "huge gap".

"I realised I didn't have any American citizens," Kieran told the BBC.

"Then all these people got in touch."

News.title: Love Island has a problem, say fans - 'there hasn't been much love'
News.content:
What's your dream Love Island series on paper?

Some watch for the heartwarming romances, like Molly-Mae Hague and Tommy Fury falling for each other back in 2019, while others prefer intense dramas - we see you 2022 winners Ekin-Su CÃ¼lcÃ¼loÄlu and Davide Sanclimenti.

Others tune in for exciting challenges like Snog, Marry, Pie or the ones which literally send heart rates soaring.

For most, it's a mix of all of the above, and it's a balance TV producers have been trying to strike for years with the original UK series, as well as a host of spin-offs and international editions.

It's no secret that Love Island UK linear viewing figures have dropped from their 2019 heyday, with streaming and social media becoming more of a focus.

Across the pond the US edition has been reaching new heights, with the latest eighth series ranked as the number one reality show for five weeks in the States across all streaming platforms, according to its streamer Peacock. , external

It also had an injection of star power as US celebrity fans, including Lizzo, Demi Lovato and Kesha, sent messages of support to the finalists, while rapper Megan Thee Stallion has become a regular guest.

BBC Newsbeat has been speaking to fans, commentators and an ex-Islander to see what they feel the UK edition could learn from the US version to regain its spark.

News.title: Body of mountaineer Nirmal Purja recovered after Pakistan avalanche
News.content:
Prince William said he was "truly saddened to hear of the tragic death" of Purja, who he said "served with distinction" as a soldier before "becoming one of the greatest mountaineers".

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in a post on X: "Incredibly sad to learn of the passing of Nirmal (Nims) Purja and those he was climbing with.

"He was an inspirational man who served in our Armed Forces for many years - and whose incredible mountaineering adventures are known the world over."

Naila Kiani, a spokesperson for the Alpine Club of Pakistan which is involved in the rescue efforts, told BBC's Newshour programme on Saturday that her organisation feared all members of the group were dead, and that Purja had led many expeditions she was on.

Praising his leadership skills, she described him as a "very experienced climber and fearless".

Teams in Pakistan have been searching for the climbers on the world's 12th-highest summit since Thursday's avalanche on the 8,047m (26,400ft) peak in the Karakoram range.

The multinational climbing group was being led by Purja. Also known as Nims, he rose to prominence in 2019 when he climbed all 14 of the world's mountains with peaks above 8,000m in 189 days - smashing the previous record by more than seven years.

He became widely known following a Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible, released two years later.

At the time, he said: "It has been a gruelling but humbling six months, and I hope to have proven that anything is possible with some determination, self-belief and positivity."

Purja served in the British military for 16 years, 10 of which were spent in the special forces, and he was awarded an MBE by the late Queen in 2018 for his achievement in extreme high-altitude mountaineering.

Purja, who lived with his wife and three-year-old daughter in Hampshire in southern England, said he was also the first Gurkha to climb Everest while serving in the British military.

In his last post on X, published on Monday, he said he had not intended to climb Broad Peak.

"Initially, the plan was to climb just G2," Purja wrote, referring to Gasherbrum II, another peak in the Karakoram mountain range.

But right before he set off for Pakistan, he realised if he also managed to climb Broad Peak while he was there, he would have only one more mountain to conquer before becoming the "first person in history to climb all 14 eight-thousanders twice. Without oxygen."

An eight-thousander is a mountain that rises more than 8,000m above sea level.

"This wasn't planned," Purja wrote. "But opportunities don't scream: they whisper to those already working in silence."

"Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down. I take zero mountains for granted," he wrote.

Broad Peak is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for climbers. The first successful ascent was in 1957, when an Austrian expedition reached the summit.

Since then, many more have climbed the mountain, but dozens have lost their lives.

One of Broad Peak's deadliest years was 2013, when at least six fatalities were recorded.

News.title: Son of Wicker Man maker dies just weeks before his sequel to film premieres
News.content:
British filmmaker Justin Hardy, who directed a sequel to his late father Robin's 1973 cult horror classic The Wicker Man, has died aged 61.

His family said Hardy died on Friday night after suffering a heart attack, remembering him as "a man of family, of boundless creativity" and "so full of life right to the end".

A Bafta and Emmy nominated writer and director, Hardy was known for the documentary Children of the Wicker Man in 2024, made with his brother Dominic, which chronicled the legacy of their father's iconic film.

He had just completed production on Wrath of the Gods, the concluding chapter to the Wicker Man trilogy, which was due to premiere in London later this month.

Hardy also directed historical films and documentaries for the BBC, Channel 4 and CNN, including Princes In The Tower, Trafalgar Battle Surgeon, The Relief Of Belsen and Spanish Flu: The Forgotten Fallen.

His family said they were "devastated" by his death and "heartbroken" Hardy would not be able to see Wrath of the Gods open.

Dominic described his brother as having "an incredible appetite for life".

"We've lost him and we've lost that larger-than-life presence looking over us all," he said. "He really became a filmmaker his own right."

Dominic also praised Hardy's work on his last film as "incredibly beautiful", adding it was "a great satisfaction to him" to have made something new.

The Wicker Man, starring Edward Woodward and Christopher Lee, is the story of a police officer sent to a remote Scottish island community to investigate the disappearance of a local girl.

Wrath of the Gods was inspired by recently discovered scripts and storyboards by Hardy's late father Robin, marking the end of the trilogy that began with The Wicker Man and the 2011 follow-up The Wicker Tree.

Hardy, who also taught screenwriting at University College London, is survived by his wife Larissa, and their four children.

News.title: Teenager dies after 'medical episode' at Kendal Calling festival in Cumbria
News.content:
A teenage girl died at the Kendal Calling festival in the early hours of the morning, police have said.

The 17-year-old suffered a medical episode at about 02:15 BST and was pronounced dead at the scene, according to Cumbria Police. The force asked people not to speculate about the circumstances of the incident.

It added officers were looking into the circumstances and wanted to speak to anyone who was in the area of the Calling Out tent and the Big Wheel around the time of the girl's death.

A spokesperson said: "Officers are particularly keen to speak with a group of women who alerted first responders to the girl after becoming concerned for her welfare."

They said the girl's family had been informed and were being supported by specialist officers.

The force asked people not to speculate, saying it could have a "significant impact" on the family and friends involved.

"We would ask that the investigation be allowed to take its course."

News.title: Ballot paper for Clacton by-election is longest in British electoral history
News.content:
The longest ballot paper in British political history is costing four times as much to print than regular ballot papers, the local council has said.

The list for the Clacton parliamentary by-election, which was prompted by the resignation of Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, is 90cm (3ft) long.

When people unfold the paper, they will find it is longer than most adults' arms.

Tendring District Council chief executive Ian Davidson - who is the acting returning officer for the by-election in the Essex constituency - said organising the vote had been "manic".

People have already started returning postal votes to town hall and most registered voters will go to polling stations on 13 August.

Davidson said: "We've logistically been looking at the size of the ballot paper, how we fold it to get it into the envelope so we can send it out to our postal voters [and] how we manage the polling stations."

News.title: Three in hospital after fire and crush at festival in London
News.content:
Three people were taken to hospital after a fire and crush at the entrance of a festival.

Organisers of Ghana Party in the Park, also known as Shattafest UK, at Copthall Playing Fields in Barnet, London, said the event was stopped following a "major incident" at about 18:00 BST on Saturday.

The Metropolitan Police said a fire had started near the gates, which meant they were closed temporarily.

A crowd built up, and there was a surge when the gates reopened, it said.

Organisers said the decision to end the festival was made on health and safety grounds.

It said in a statement the day had been "one of the most difficult" in the event's history and called what happened "deeply upsetting".

News.title: The legacy of Epping's asylum protests a year on: 'It's still discussed in shops, pubs and cafes'
News.content:
When Anita bought her house in the upmarket town of Epping, she dreamed of a happy retirement enjoying the nature surrounding her.

What she did not bargain for was her Essex home becoming a battleground of anti-asylum seeker protests and counter-demonstrations in July 2025.

It followed the arrest of Ethiopian migrant Hadush Kebatu, who was living at The Bell Hotel in the town when he sexually assaulted a schoolgirl and a woman.

Most protests that followed were peaceful - and protesters argue they were a force for good. However, some descended into chaos and six people have been jailed for violent disorder so far.

At one point, Epping Forest District Council considered evacuating nearby houses due to the chaos.

The case sparked a wider conversation about the effect of housing asylum seekers in hotels in British communities.

"Overnight, our local social media platforms went from people seeking lost cats to the most vitriolic, horrible things," recalls Anita.

Like others in this story, she does not want her full name used for fear of being targeted.

News.title: Stembridge to 'reassess' future after England miss out on medal
News.content:
England tried to rally themselves following their semi-final defeat by New Zealand, but came up against a Diamonds team recovering from one of the biggest shocks in the tournament's history.

Australia - who had previously been in every Commonwealth final and won the tournament four times - were stunned by Jamaica on Saturday afternoon, giving them less time to recover for the bronze-medal match than England.

The Roses worked hard to shut down the Diamonds' forward-passing options from the start, but the team in green and gold found their rhythm with devastating consequences, overturning an early 9-7 deficit to lead 19-11 in a bruising first-quarter spell for the Roses.

Stembridge's side, who lost 66-47 to the same opponents in the pool stage, then lacked impetus in the second period, showing signs of tired legs against one of the world's most established shooting partnerships in Kiera Austin and Sophie Garbin.

A loose pass from England captain Fran Williams allowed Austin to calmly extend the gap to 28-16 and her side kept the margin steady, resulting in a half-time score of 35-24.

The presence of substitute shooter Eleanor Cardwell in the third quarter helped the Roses score five without reply to trail 45-34, but they were still 49-36 behind with 15 minutes left to play.

Bronze is not a colour of medal that Australia ever imagined they would be playing for, but what seemed just as important to them was reminding the world what they are capable of and why they have been such feared opponents.

In that sense, Stacey Marinkovich's Diamonds shone as ultimate professionals, and England again came up short against a top side, losing by one less point than the pool stage match between the teams.

"It's so tough after we lost yesterday and the disappointment of not making a final, to pull yourself up. I'm just so proud of the girls, the fight that we had through this 10 days to keep showing up and responding," Williams told BBC Sport.

"Probably a few of our errors came through that fatigue and the mental drain that being in tournament netball is, and that is no excuse.

"For so many of us, 10 of us, that was our first Commonwealth Games experiencing that and maybe that showed in a final-day game where you've got to turn it on when medals are on that line.

"I'm not going away from that World Cup next year without a medal and standing on that podium, hopefully with a gold, so we'll be doing as much as we can in the next 12 months to make sure that we are in a better position to fight in these final games."

News.title: Trust, grief and betrayal: Inside the Legacy funeral case
News.content:
This story contains details some might find distressing.

I've reported on many criminal cases before, but nothing like that of undertaker Robert Bush.

Now the case is over, we can report on what it was like to follow a story that began when whistleblowers raised concerns about Legacy Independent Funeral Directors with Humberside Police in March 2024.

Bush, the former owner of Legacy in Hull, admitted 67 offences, including fraudulent trading, denying 30 people a decent and proper burial, and giving some bereaved relatives the ashes of strangers.

The scale of Bush's offending was extraordinary. Police identified 300 victims.

Some were families who had paid Bush for funeral plans and services.

Others were relatives left questioning whether the ashes they had received really belonged to their loved ones.

There were also the deceased, whose bodies he had been trusted to bury or cremate with dignity.

Bush's scores of victims meant seats in courtroom four at Hull Crown Court for his five-day sentencing were in high demand.

Every day, diligent ushers stood like bouncers at the court's heavy, soundproof doors. They ensured families were given priority to see the man who wronged their loved ones face justice.

Court staff escorted them in with boxes of tissues, paper cups of water and a kind hand on their arms. Some were wiping away tears before they even walked into the room.

Fearful of what they were about to hear.

Their worries were not misplaced. The details of Bush's crimes were harrowing.

Among them, discarding stillborn premature baby Sunny Beverley-Conlin on the floor in a paper bag, and abandoning one victim naked on the floor to "let nature take its course".

They are descriptions one grieving mother said "will never leave me".

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. got into it with CNN’s Dana Bash on Sunday in an interview segment that quickly evolved into Kennedy angrily berating Bash and her network for “punishing” people during the Covid-19 pandemic.

The segment on Sunday comes as measles outbreaks have broken out in several states, with public health officials warning that a unvaccinated communities were supercharging the spread of a disease to historic levels.

Bash, host of CNN’s State of the Union, prodded Kennedy repeatedly to look “into the camera” and urge parents to get their kids vaccinated against the measles virus. Kennedy did repeat the urging, but the interview went south from there as they debated the treatment of skeptics and those opposed to the Biden administration’s public health guidance during the pandemic.

“Of course you want to move on!” an angry Kennedy insisted as Bash tried to pivot from a question about Covid-era guidance. “Because you were part of the problem!”

“No, I wasn’t!” Bash replied indignantly.

Robert F. Kennedy Jr. grew heated and began yelling at CNN's Dana Bash on Sunday ( CNN - State of the Union )

“There was absolute press malpractice [during Covid],” Kennedy continued. “You weren’t allowing-- your job is a furious skepticism toward authority. And you weren’t doing that. You were beating up on people who were dissenting.”

After Kennedy finished, Bash attempted to take down the temperature, and said in a calmer tone: “Okay. Do you want to sit here and attack me or do you want to have a conversation about public health?"

“You’re sitting here and attacking me!” responded the secretary.

The CNN host went on to say that she would not allow Kennedy to “use this interview to say things that are not entirely true”.

They would then go back and forth over the Covid vaccine, its efficacy, and whether or not it posed a greater risk than benefit to children who received it. The two quarreled also over CNN and other media networks’ citing of advice from “experts” like Fauci and other public health officials and academics who appeared on TV frequently during 2020 and 2021 to promote things like masking, social distancing, and following public health guidelines.

“I can tell you, that, when it comes to the vaccine, there have been studies that show that because of vaccine disinformation, disinformation, there could have been 100,000-200,000 lives in the U.S., saved, but because people didn’t get the vaccine, that’s why--”

“You are saying nonsense!” a frustrated Kennedy replied. “You are saying something that you cannot show me [evidence to support].”

“I am not saying nonsense!” Bash shot back.

All in all, the segment lasted more than 20 minutes, uninterrupted, before Bash ended the interview by repeating the explanation that it was her job to find the best information, from experts, and provide it to the public. She finished her statement by beginning to say that it concerned her when Kennedy came on the program and said untrue things, or statements that were not supported by evidence or scientific studies, before she was cut off by the secretary one last time, who finished her sentence for her.

“[Things] that your ‘experts’ do not agree with,” Kennedy interjected, using air quotes around the word “experts”.

“Yes!” Bash replied. “People with scientific backgrounds.”

This is a breaking news report. More to follow...

US President Donald Trump is set to visit Ireland for at least two days in September.

The trip will include a visit to Co Clare, where he is expected to attend the Irish Open golf tournament at Trump International Golf Links and Hotel just outside the town of Doonbeg, the Press Association understands.

He is also expected to visit Dublin, but details on many elements of the engagement have yet to be finalised.

On his last visit to Ireland in 2023, Mr Trump was warmly welcomed to Doonbeg where locals waved American flags, and some donned the Make America Great Again cap.

But his last visit when he was in office in 2019 sparked protests from climate change, left-wing, pro-Palestine, pro-choice, anti-racism and anti-war activists, who flew the Trump baby blimp in Dublin.

open image in gallery Trump is expected to attend the Irish Open golf tournament at his course in Doonbeg ( Getty )

The last visit of a sitting US President to Ireland was by Joe Biden in 2023 to mark the 25th anniversary of the Good Friday Agreement.

Mr Biden visited Belfast, Dublin, Co Louth and Co Mayo, exploring his ancestral links to the former and declaring “Mayo for Sam”.

Ten of Mr Biden’s 16 great-great-grandparents are believed to hail from Ireland, and while he has links in Co Louth, those with Co Mayo associations are believed to be the strongest through the Blewitt family. He keeps in close contact with the Blewitt family, who attended the White House St Patrick’s Day receptions in 2022 and 2023.

The then-president was accompanied during the visit by former taoiseach Enda Kenny, who hails from Co Mayo, and his wife Fionnuala, as well as his son Hunter and sister Valerie Biden Owens, to a musical welcome from a harpist and fiddle player.

Mr Biden met historian Sinead McCoole, who showed him three artefacts from the Jackie Clarke Museum in Ballina, including the cockade which Theobald Wolfe Tone wore on his hat at the time of his capture by the British in 1798.

He also spoke to expert Brendan Walsh about the history of North Mayo, the Irish-American connections, and the background of the Blewitt family.

Phil Collins has revealed his loved ones were told to say their goodbyes while the Genesis frontman spent seven months in intensive care.

The British singer, 75, who has been open about his addiction to alcohol in the past, started drinking again after several years of sobriety – resulting in him being rushed to a Swiss hospital in November 2023.

Speaking about his hospital stay in a new interview, Collins revealed that he spent seven months in intensive care and was very close to death. The singer’s five children – Joely, 53, Simon, 49, Lily, 37, Nicholas, 25, and Matthew, 18 – were all summoned to his bedside as he lay unconscious.

“Because there were some decisions to be made about ‘Do we keep Phil on life support?’ kind of thing,” he told The Sunday Times. “My kidneys were packing up, my organs were just seizing up. People were coming to say goodbye.

“But I don’t remember them coming, I didn’t have no idea this was going on. They were all worried that they wouldn’t see me again. It could all have gone so terribly wrong.”

open image in gallery Phil Collins with his son, Mathew Collins ( Instagram/Mathew Collins )

Collins admitted that he was “very lucky” to make it out of intensive care and hasn’t touched alcohol since – however, he has been left with long-term health issues as a result.

He told the publication that his pancreas is permanently scarred and his kidneys “barely function”, but he also suffers with other health problems following a serious spinal injury in 2007. He now walks on crutches and is cared for by a live-in nurse 24 hours, while also managing his type 2 diabetes.

In January, Collins revealed that he had undergone multiple operations on his knee, telling Zoe Ball in an interview: “I had everything that could go wrong with me, go wrong with me.”

Collins previously spoke about his alcoholism while promoting his 2016 memoir I’m Not Dead Yet, revealing that he started drinking heavily after his third marriage broke down and he retired from music. “You start drinking, and then you start drinking too much. Then it physically hurts you. I came very close to dying at that point,” he told The New York Times at the time.

The “In the Air Tonight” singer would open a bottle of wine at 11am in the morning at the height of his addiction, having split from his third wife, Orianne Cevey, in 2006 after seven years of marriage and two sons, Nicholas and Mathew. He was previously married to Andrea Bertorelli for five years until 1980, adopting her daughter Joely and welcoming son Simon with her in that time. He then wed Jill Tavelman, who is the mother of his daughter Lily, in 1986 before the pair divorced in 1996.

open image in gallery Phil Collins with his daughter, actor Lily Collins, in 2012 ( Getty )

In the new interview, Collins also revealed that he spent last New Year with his family in London, while daughter Lily – who is best known for starring in Netflix’s Emily in Paris – sat beside him “in tears” saying, “I never thought I’d get these moments”.

The pair’s relationship has come a long way in the last 10 years, with the Netflix star admitting in an open letter in 2017 that a “terrible disconnect” had developed between them since her parents’ divorce. Phil Collins has now said that he was “quite shocked and a little bit sad” by his daughter’s open letter, but that they’ve patched things up.

“But she’s told me why now, and she takes it all back. She wished she’d never done it,” he said. “I have a wonderful relationship with Lily now. So everything has a happy ending, most of the time.”

Collins is set to be inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in November, marking his second time being honoured after making it in as a member of rock band Genesis in 2010.

If you or someone you know is suffering from alcohol addiction, you can confidentially call the national alcohol helpline Drinkline on 0300 123 1110 or visit the NHS website here for information about the programmes available to you.

News.title: Idaho shooting latest: At least 3 dead and seven injured in mass shooting at In-N-Out with casualties expected ‘to rise’
News.content:
Officials give update on In-N-Out shooting in Idaho

At least three people were killed and seven others were injured in a shooting at an In-N-Out in Idaho, officials said.

Authorities found the body of the suspected shooter — an unidentified male — near the fast food restaurant in Twin Falls, a city of about 56,000 people located roughly 130 miles southeast of Boise.

One of the people killed was an associate at In-N-Out, the chain’s president, Lynsi Snyder, confirmed.

Joshua Palmer, a city spokesperson, told The Independent that the number of victims may change. “We want to emphasize that that number may change,” Palmer said. “That was just the first number we got.”

The shooting unfolded around 2 p.m., and police urged people at the time to avoid the area, saying roads nearby would be closed as officers responded. Shelter-in-place orders were lifted Saturday night, police said.

The FBI is assisting in the investigation, and authorities were still working to determine the suspect's identity and motive, Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said during a Saturday news conference.

“We believe the threat to the community is over,” Hicks said. “It was a very chaotic scene.”

Life on the set of Happy Days wasn’t always as cheerful as it appeared on screen, according to Henry Winkler.

The Emmy-winning actor — who played Arthur “Fonzie” Fonzarelli on the beloved Seventies sitcom — revealed during an interview at a Tennessee fan expo last month that there was one costar who let his fame get to his head.

“The truth of the matter is really on our set, there was no stardom,” Winkler, 80, said at the July 11 panel alongside former co-stars Anson Williams and Don Most, according to Entertainment Weekly. “We were an ensemble. We worked hard at making it funny every week.”

However, he went on to recall: “One guy came on as a guest star, and then he was brought back a few times. And he would mention his fan mail. And I said, ‘You don’t wanna talk to me about fan mail. I got 50,000 letters a week.’”

“And I said, ‘We don’t talk about that on the set. We are all here as one,’” the Arrested Development actor added. “And he kept doing it, and he was an assback.”

Henry Winkler has revealed one actor who annoyed him on the set of 'Happy Days' ( Getty )

While not naming the actor, Winkler then revealed: “He played Eugene.”

Eugene Belvin appeared as a recurring character in 10 episodes across seasons 8 and 9 of the show from 1980 to 1982.

The character was played by actor Denis Mandel, who went on to act in shows including Knots Landing and Homefront before stepping away from acting entirely. His last appearance onscreen was in 2006, according to IMDb.

While Winkler did not gel with Mandel, the Barry star spoke about his harmonious relationship with co-star Ron Howard, who went on to become an Oscar-winning director after his time on Happy Days.

Winkler said that, after one particularly frustrating moment on set, Howard offered him a crucial piece of advice: learn to control his temper.

“I was having trouble with a scene. I started punching my script,” the actor said, adding that Howard “put his arm around me, he walked me to the back of the soundstage, and he said, ‘You know, the writers are working as hard as they can. Let’s not hit our script.’”

“I said, ‘Ron, I will never hit my script as long as I live,’” Winkler said. “And he is, and was, even at that tender age, so wise. He just is easy, he just kind of goes through life and he’s an amazing fellow.”

Reigning William Hill Premiership champions Celtic begin their defence of the title when Dundee head for Glasgow.

Martin O’Neill’s men return to action at Celtic Park a little less than three months after clinching their latest crown in a dramatic final-day showdown with Hearts.

Elsewhere, the West Indies go head to head with Pakistan in the second Test in Port of Spain, and there is Hundred action from Cardiff as Welsh Fire and Southern Brave meet in both the women’s and men’s competitions.

Here’s what is happening in the sporting world on Monday – and where you can catch the action in the UK.

The Bhoys are back in town

open image in gallery Martin O’Neill will lead Celtic into Premiership battle with Dundee on Monday evening (Andrew Milligan/PA) ( PA Wire )

Celtic will attempt to strike an early blow in their Old Firm rivalry with Rangers when they entertain Dundee in their opening fixture of the new Premiership campaign.

The men from Ibrox could only draw 1-1 at Dundee United on Friday evening and O’Neill’s side will have a chance to establish a two-point advantage during the season’s first weekend.

Dundee proved something of a thorn in Celtic’s side last season, winning the first league clash between the sides 2-0 at Dens Park in October before going down 1-0 in Glasgow in December and 2-1 at home in April either side of a 2-1 Scottish FA Cup defeat in which they led 1-0 heading into the last minute of normal time.

All the action is on Sky Sports Football and Sky Sports Main Event from 6.30pm.

What else is happening on Monday?

open image in gallery Joe Root’s Welsh Fire are in men’s Hundred action against Southern Brace in Cardiff on Monday (Adam Davy/PA) ( PA Wire )

It is day two at the Queen’s Park Oval in Port of Spain, Trinidad as the West Indies attempt to build upon their first Test victory over Pakistan in Tarouba. Coverage begins on TNT Sports 2 at 2.30pm.

In the Women’s Hundred, Welsh Fire meet Southern Brave at Sophia Gardens on Sky Sports Cricket from 2.45pm and Sky Sports Main Event from 3pm. Their male counterparts take centre stage on Sky Sports Cricket at 6pm.

Sky Sports Tennis has action from the Canadian Open at 4pm with Sky Sports Main Event taking over at 10.15pm, while stage three of the Tour de France Women is on TNT Sports 1 at 2.30pm.

On this day in history

open image in gallery Thierry Henry completed his move from Juventus to Arsenal on this day in 1999 (Tony Harris/PA) ( PA Archive )

1999: Arsenal completed the £10million signing of France striker Thierry Henry from Juventus.

2012: There were Olympic gold medals for British rowers Katherine Grainger and Anna Watkins (double sculls) and cyclists Victoria Pendleton (keirin) and Ed Clancy, Geraint Thomas, Steven Burke and Peter Kennaugh (team pursuit). Britain also won four bronze medals, while Jessica Ennis – now Ennis-Hill – broke the British record and heptathlon world record for the 100 metres hurdles in 12.54 seconds.

2017: Neymar became the most expensive footballer of all time after joining Paris St Germain for 222 million euros – worth £200.6m at the time. Earlier in the day, his legal representatives paid Barcelona the world-record fee to secure his release from his contract.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
For many the 100m is the Blue Riband event the one everyone wants to watch and the race that steals all the headlines. For these Commonwealth Games, however, tonight’s mile race is the one that has grabbed all the attention – and it is not hard to see why.

Josh Kerr, fresh from his new world record of 3:42.66 (a time that beat a mark that had stood since 1999) takes on fellow Scot Jake Wightman and Australia’s new superstar Cameron Myers. Three great runners over a distance that evokes sepia-tinted memories of Roger Bannister and the seminal four-minute mark.

Some of you may be wondering why the mile is back at an international event. Well, Seb Coe, the president of World Athletics and someone who broke the mile record three times, says the race distance is easy to understand and resonates with fans. And, coming on the back of Kerr’s world record, who can argue with him?

This is the first time the mile has been run at the games since 1966 and the hope is that tonight’s final matches the Miracle Mile run in 1954. Earlier that year Bannister broke the four-minute barrier, only for Australia’s John Landy to go lower with a time of 3:58.0 soon after. The Games in Vancouver were the first time two sub-four minuters had gone head-to-head. And the race didn’t disappoint – Bannister beating Landy with a time of 3:58.8 minutes. The Australian also ran under four minutes, making it the first time two men had done so in the same race.

Obviously all three of the expected main protagonists will go well under four minutes, but if they can recreate the drama of the 1954 final then we’ll have a race to savour.

Stay here for all the action with the gun set to go off at 8.55.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur 2 Chelsea 1

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.



Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

Sports.title: TNT Sports presenter Olivia Buzaglo stuns in purple bikini as she enjoys Turkey getaway after World Cup
Sports.content:
OLIVIA BUZAGLO has stunned fans in a purple bikini during a post-World Cup getaway.

The TNT Sports presenter has had a busy summer covering the tournament across the Atlantic Ocean.



Olivia, 32, will be back in action once the 2026/27 Premier League season gets underway but has taken the opportunity for a relaxing break.

The presenter has jetted off to Bodrum, Turkey, to soak up some sun by the Aegean Sea.



She has shared a post from the holiday as she showed off her time enjoying a luxury holiday.

Olivia could be seen swimming in a purple bikini as she and her partner – YouTuber Tom Garratt took a boat trip.

They even had their own diving competition to see who could have the better form going into the water.

She also switched up her swimwear and wowed in a brown bikini as she posed for a picture.

Olivia shared the snaps on Instagram for her 125k followers on the social media platform.

They loved the snaps and flooded the comment section with praise.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish being monitored by Atletico Madrid as two Premier League clubs consider transfer move for Man City outcast

ATLETICO MADRID are considering a surprise move for Manchester City outcast Jack Grealish.

SunSport understands the £100million winger has admirers at the Wanda Metropolitano due to his workrate on and off the ball.



The 30-year-old is seen as a good tactical fit for Diego Simeone, who has previously signed English players in Kieran Trippier and Conor Gallagher.

But there are some hurdles in getting a deal done considering Atletico are already well stocked in attacking positions.



Simeone has already brought in Lee Kang-In from PSG and has options such as Alex Baena, Thiago Almada and Ademola Lookman on the wing.

And Grealish would likely have to accept a rotation role if he did secure a move to the Spanish capital.



The former Aston Villa man hasn’t played since January after picking up a foot injury on loan at Everton.

He has returned to training after recovering from the issue but missed out on Man City’s pre-season tour of Hong Kong and Seoul.

Grealish has since started working with RCD Mallorca to keep himself ticking over and drum up interest from other sides.

And should a move to Atletico not work out, he could target a return to Everton after a decent loan spell saw him score twice and provide six assists.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Toffees are keen to take Grealish on another loan and see it as a realistic and risk-free move.

A return to boyhood club Aston Villa is also a possibility, five years after he left Villa Park.

Grealish played 213 times for Villa and captained the side, who are now flying under Unai Emery after winning the Europa League last season.

It’s understood Villa have discussed the idea of bringing Grealish back and believe he could offer much needed depth in the wide areas as they prepare to sell Leon Bailey to Hull.



The exits of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans have also meant Villa have lost some of their creativity and Grealish would provide a spark.

There are also options for Grealish in Saudi – with Al-Hilal, Al-Ahli and Neom all making enquiries.

The three clubs are prepared to make Grealish offers of between £17m and £21m a year.

And Grealish also has interest from the MLS, who believe his profile and personality would be a great commercial fit for the league.

Sports.title: Arsenal legend reveals who the Gunners’ biggest title rivals will be this season in brutal snub to both Manchester clubs
Sports.content:
PAUL MERSON has named the club he believes will be the biggest threat to Arsenal’s title defence this season – and it is not Manchester City.

The Gunners ended their 22-year wait for a Premier League crown in May, topping the table by seven points.



They are now braced to defend their title, with each of their main rivals having added to their squads.

City have signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest in a huge deal worth £116million, along with Jeremy Monga in a £10m swoop from Leicester City.



Chelsea hijacked Arsenal’s move for Morgan Rogers and paid Aston Villa £117m for the attacking midfielder.

The Blues have also added the likes of Maxence Lacroix, Danny Welbeck and Marco Palestra to their ranks.



And third-placed Manchester United have recruited Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, Karl Darlow and Tynan Thompson over the last few months.

However, former Arsenal and England midfielder Merson does not believe that any of those clubs will challenge the Gunners this term.

Instead, he thinks that Liverpool will become their biggest rivals.

In his latest Sky Sports column, Merson wrote: “I don’t think Man City will win the Premier League this year anyway.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“They didn’t win it last year with the best manager in the world. They were only ever in the title race because Arsenal had a bad three weeks.

“I think Liverpool are Arsenal’s nearest challengers this season.”

So far this summer, Liverpool have welcomed new head coach Andoni Iraola from Bournemouth.

They have also signed Spanish winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna and French centre-back Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes.



The Reds are now plotting an audacious swoop for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola – who is valued at £145m by the French side.

Barcola has also been linked with a move to Arsenal, but the Gunners recently shifted their attention to Vinicius Jr as they look to strengthen their attack.

In his column, Merson highlighted concerns about City’s midfield, despite the addition of Anderson.

He believes that Anderson will not fit into the same starting line-up as Rodri.

Merson claimed: “Rodri is one of the top two holding midfielders in the world, alongside Moises Caicedo. But I don’t see how him and Elliot Anderson play together.



“Rodri is the best in the business at ticking it over, Anderson is going to be the best in the business at ticking it over. But to play both of them in there? I don’t think they need that.

“How many teams are going to have a go at Man City? People go to the Etihad and shut up shop and counter-attack.

“Do you need two holding midfielders against Hull? No, of course not. Then all of a sudden, someone’s not playing.

“Don’t get me wrong, in the big games, when they’re playing back away in the Champions League in a quarter-final or the last 16, then you need two holding midfield players. They were a bit too open in the Champions League and were well off it last year.

“But the holy grail is the 38 games in the Premier League. And there aren’t enough games in the Premier League for them both to play in the same team.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Unless they bought Anderson and he gets a season of learning under the best in the world in Rodri. But £116m is a lot to spend on someone to be an understudy. Rodri will want to play, and he won’t want to sit there and be someone’s understudy.

“But you’re still selling one of the best players in the world.”

Sports.title: Leny Yoro insists Man United can win the Premier League THIS SEASON despite 15th-placed disaster just a year ago
Sports.content:
LENY YORO believes a Premier League title triumph is possible for Manchester United next season.

United finished third last term, having ended in an embarrassing 15th the previous campaign – their worst in 51 years.



But the appointment of Michael Carrick in January led to 12 wins from 17 games and only two defeats, fuelling hope among United fans of an end to their title drought.

Rivals Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea appointed new managers in the summer, while Roberto de Zerbi was installed at Tottenham in late March.



With champions Arsenal the team to beat, United have emerged as potential challengers amid a rare prolonged period of stability under Carrick.

Yoro echoed team-mate Bryan Mbeumo’s promise of a “big” season when asked if United can win the title.

The Frenchman said: “Yeah, of course. We’re Man United so we have to think like that. And I know we have the potential to do it, so we have to do it.

“The mood is really good. We work really hard, and outside the pitch, we have a good vibe, good mood.

“So the target this season is to win every game, to be honest. For the team to be the best, for myself to do good games every time, to win trophies, and to be at the top.”

United came from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 in their third pre-season friendly in Stockholm on Saturday.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Centre back Yoro started at right back for the third game running in the absence of Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui, who will report for pre-season after their post-World Cup breaks on Monday.

United signed Yoro from Lille for £58.7million in July 2024 and the 20-year-old has made 33 appearances in each of his campaigns due to a combination of injuries and competition.

Fellow centre half Matthijs de Ligt is certain to miss the start of the season after back surgery while Lisandro Martinez sustained a thigh injury in the World Cup final, though he is not expected to miss any United games.

Carrick has played Harry Maguire and Ayden Heaven at centre back in a right-footed-left-footed combination in pre-season, with Yoro filling in at right back.

Yoro was keen to stress he is a centre back first and foremost but acknowledged it is time he established himself at United in his third season.



He added: “I hope I’m not going to be injured this pre-season. That will help me to improve as well, and to be ready for the start of the season.

“But the team is doing really well. No injuries yet as well. So hopefully we’re going to continue like that.

“I know I did a great season but I know I can do much, much better. I know my potential, for sure, and I hope I’m going to have a really good, good season.

“Obviously, I have no excuses, but I hope I’m not going to be injured this season, and I’ll show to everyone what I can do.



“Sometimes people forget I am still only 20, still a lot to learn, so I have a lot to improve.

“And like I said, I know my potential, I can learn a lot. I can improve a lot.

“So I hope this season’s gonna be a big, big step for me as well.”

Sports.title: Shocking amount Gianni Infantino would have made from shameful World Cup sell-off plot revealed as he clings on to job
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO would have been earning nearly £1MILLION per week if his controversial World Cup sell-off plot came off.

The Fifa president, who has dominated the headlines since the beginning of the World Cup in June, was forced into a U-turn on his plans to sell the World Cup to investors in a humiliating ordeal.



Despite insisting that “nobody is selling football”, Infantino‘s £42million salary increase from his current £4.5m deal would make sport’s highest earners drool.

As the commissioner or chief executive, he would be expected to be placed on a stunning salary and bonuses package, according to the Times.



Infantino would have been paid nearly £1million-a-week, picking up around £47MILLION a year.

To put it into context, it’s the equivalent of what the top paid players earn in the renowned money pit that is the Saudi Pro League.

However, Infantino might have to settle for his more modest current salary for the time being after announcing he was backtracking on his plan to allow private investors to buy up a chunk of the global tournament.

The Fifa president hoped to secure £3.1billion of private funding for his FFE project by October.

US bank JP Morgan were reportedly brought on board in an advisory capacity.

And Thrive Capital, backed by Donald Trump‘s son in law Jared Kushner, were tipped to purchase a 20 per cent stake in the money-making venture.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

But despite having dollar signs in his eyes, Infantino was brought back down to earth, as European football governing body Uefa had their say.

Uefa‘s member nations threatened to boycott the next Fifa tournaments, including the World Cup, while Concacaf and the AFC also hit out.

The FA also weighed in on Infantino’s lucrative project, saying: “We fully support UEFA’s position.

“It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.”



Despite his countless controversies, the Italian is still determined to hold on to his role in the 2027 Fifa elections.

He isn’t about to walk away from the top job – even after his senior advisor quit and the whole of Uefa turned on him.

In his own statement, Infantino said: “Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.

“Our purpose has always been – and will always be – to unite and improve.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“As a result, this proposal will not proceed.



“Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.”

Sports.title: Former Man Utd star Casemiro devastated as his horror double blunder on Inter Miami home debut leaves Messi stunned
Sports.content:
CASEMIRO suffered a nightmare home debut for Inter Miami as he gifted possession and then scored an own goal moments later.

The former Manchester United midfielder, 34, only linked up with Lionel Messi’s side last week as a free agent after leaving Old Trafford.



His first appearance came just days after arriving as he played 90 minutes in a 1-0 win over Montreal.

But his home debut against Columbus Crew got off to a disastrous start just 33 minutes into the game.



Miami were 1-0 up thanks to Luis Suarez‘s strike when Casemiro inexplicably gave away the ball under no pressure.

A cross was then fizzed into the box, which the Brazilian then diverted into his own net.

Casemiro looked totally dejected after his moment to forget – and his new team-mate Messi didn’t seem too happy either.

The camera cut to the Argentine scowling on the bench after Casemiro’s embarrassing gaffe.

Fans couldn’t believe Casemiro’s first home game had gone so badly as they debated the moment on X.

Miami did go in front again thanks to Noah Allen’s goal on the stroke of half time.

Messi was then sent on as a substitute in his first game since returning from his World Cup heartache with Argentina.

But the 39-year-old was unable to guide his team to victory in his 37 minutes on the pitch as Brais Mendez struck in the 84th minute to snatch a draw.

The Dutchman lifted the Premier League crown in his debut season at Anfield but the Merseysiders struggled to hit those heights last term. Liverpool slipped to fifth in the table, just about squeezing into the Champions League.

"Iraola will need all of his players fully fit, but if we have a fully fit squad, we have a chance of winning the league this year, without question," Thompson told the BBC. “The fans want to see a bit more aggression, but I could see, just from watching (pre-season) from the stands, the demands of the manager.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino 'certain to go' according to FIFA insiders after botched World Cup plot
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino 'certain to go' according to FIFA insiders after botched World Cup plot

A source described the FIFA President as a 'dead duck' while opponents were reportedly lining up candidates as his successor

Donald Trump addresses his call to Infantino over Balogun

Gianni Infantino looks certain to be ousted as FIFA President after his 'shabby' attempts to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.

‌



Infantino, 56, could have profited from the "Fifa Forward Enterprise" scheme (FFE) and is trying to stay in his post. But his support is flooding away.

‌



A source told the Sunday Times that Infantino is a 'dead duck' while opponents were reportedly lining up candidates as his successor.

‌



The FA and UEFA, European football's governing body, said that they had lost confidence in Infantino.

In a stinging statement, which the English FA said it supported, Uefa described the scheme as a "shabby, back-room, opaque deal he [Infantino] hatched and tried to force through".

Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

View 3 Images And it's goodbye from him: Sources suggest Infantino's days at FIFA are numbered (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

‌



It added: "The current Fifa leadership has not only lost Uefa's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family."

Former FA chief Mark Pallios was among those calling on Infantino to go. He said: "He should not survive.

"He has delivered these plans with a complete lack of transparency." England legend Peter Reid slammed Infantino and called for him to resign for the good of the game.

‌



He told the Mirror: "He must go - look at the World Cup: the hydration breaks for advertising, the half time show in the final.

"FIFA has hundreds of millions already, they should be putting more money into grassroots."

CONCACAF, which governs the north and central American associations, plus the Caribbean, called for a "comprehensive reckoning" with Infantino's presidency.

‌



View 3 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino speaks during the 2026 World Cup draw (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"A proposal of this magnitude does not reach that stage by accident," CONCACAF said in a statement. "It is a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first.

"This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour."

‌



Uefa led the way in opposing the plan with its 55 members, including the FA, agreeing on Thursday to boycott all Fifa competitions.

"We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast-track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game," it said.

"We must identify those responsible and hold them to account. This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story.

‌



"The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in Fifa has only just begun."

Sources told the Sunday Times that senior figures in FIFA were looking to find a successor to Infantino.

View 3 Images Peter Reid the England legend called for Infantino to resign (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

‌



A spokeswoman for the FA said: "We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart."

Infantino is likely to face an emergency FIFA council meeting where he will be asked to resign.

If he refuses, a single candidate backed by all his opponents would be put up to challenge him in next year's election.

Article continues below

Candidates for the role include Concacaf president Victor Montagliani, Asian football president Sheikh Salman and Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al Khelaifi.

There may also be support for a less high-profile candidate who has backing from across the various continents.

Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go

Gianni Infantino has been told to leave FIFA following the doomed plan to sell off the World Cup with UEFA and CONCACAF declaring losses of confidence in the current president

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has u-turned on the plan to sell a share in the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino has been told to RESIGN from FIFA by a whopping 99% of Mirror readers. The president finds himself under huge pressure, having performed a dramatic u-turn on his plan to sell off a share of the World Cup to an investment group.

‌



FIFA announced the plot earlier this week, to widespread criticism from fans, governing bodies and even UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham. There were suggestions that some confederations would consider boycotting any FIFA-organised competitions in the face of the plan.

‌



But Infantino and FIFA performed a huge backtrack by cancelling the proposal in its entirety. That, however, has not seen the current president escape criticism, with some still calling for the 56-year-old to be removed from his position.

‌



Since the baffling plan was originally unveiled, Mirror Football has been running a poll for fans to decide whether Infantino should resign or not. In total, 6832 fans had their say, with a huge 99 percent of them suggesting that Infantino’s position was now untenable.

That vote follows UEFA declaring a loss of confidence in the current president. A statement from UEFA on Saturday: "We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

"It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

‌



"When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA's Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, 'Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA.

“You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA,' before telling the assembled stakeholders, 'The money of FIFA is your money. It's not the money of the FIFA President. It's your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.'

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been told to leave his post (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through were anything but transparent."

CONCACAF followed suit with their own scathing statement, while bizarrely the Qatari FA have spoken out in support of Infantino.

A statement read: “We welcome FIFA President Gianni Infantino's decision to withdraw the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal in the interest of the global football community.

Article continues below

“While the proposal had merit, we applaud the wisdom behind prioritising unity among Member Associations. The Qatar Football Association fully supports President Infantino's efforts to continue growing and strengthening the game globally.”

Sports.title: Ex-Man City captain gives health update after being diagnosed with devastating rare condition
Sports.content:
Ex-Man City captain gives health update after being diagnosed with devastating rare condition

Former Manchester City captain Andy Morrison was diagnosed with neurological condition Ramsay Hunt Syndrome earlier this year but he now appears to be firmly on the mend

View 2 Images Andy Morrison previously captained Man City (Image: Getty Images)

Ex-Man City captain Andy Morrison has revealed how he has left doctors ‘amazed’ with his recovery from Ramsay Hunt Syndrome. The 55-year-old was diagnosed with the devastating neurological condition earlier this year.

‌



The condition is caused by a virus in the facial nerve and can lead to face paralysis, blistering rashes near the ear, severe earache and hearing loss. But it appears that the former City man is firmly on the mend, having issued an update to supporters on social media following a return to the commentary booth.

‌



He said: “Evening everyone. Just a quick update after the first day back working at City with the matchday live team, which I thoroughly enjoyed.

‌



“It was fantastic to be back. Felt the voice was strong enough to go back and do co-commentary today. That's my first time back in five-and-a-half months. I really appreciate all the support and working with Ali Mann, who makes it very easy.

Arsenal star refused to go on pre-season tour to force through summer transfer READ MORE :

“An enjoyable game. I struggled with a few words, a few names, but nothing too bad. I did struggle with (Ryan) McAidoo. Could have a player there by the way, watch this space. There was enough there to think he could be the next one on the conveyor belt, hugely impressive in the second-half.

‌



“Birthday yesterday, that was a great day with grandkids and family. I had a specialist on Wednesday and it was really positive, he was really delighted and amazed at the progress I had made, from House-Brackmann (nerve grading scale) six to a four and he is really positive that within a year I'll get my eye back and be able to blink, so I won't have to tape it down at night.

“I still have to take juice to swallow and I have no taste in the side of my mouth and the whole side of the face is numb, so I have to drink through a straw still. He wasn't sure just how much that would progress because it's still really weak. But if sucking through a straw is worst case scenario then so be it. I won't be posting now because I won't see a specialist for another three months.

View 2 Images Andy Morrison has offered an update on his condition (Image: @AndyMorri5on/X)

Article continues below

“A really good day and it just felt great to be back doing something when that seemed a million miles away. I didn't get out of bed for four weeks and couldn't speak for a month.

"I had some really dark days in this conservatory but I stayed positive and this too shall pass, everything passes, good or bad, everything comes and goes and sometimes you just have to dig in and get through it. But thanks for listening and see you all soon.”
