The dramatic turnaround was completed in stoppage time when Toyosi Olusanya was hauled down by Findlay, who saw red, and Nisbet despatched the spot-kick.

The St Mirren manager, Craig McLeish, believes his team’s 2-0 win at Falkirk augurs well for a successful campaign.

McLeish is convinced his squad will improve on last season’s struggles before he steered Saints to safety when the interim head coach.

He has set a high bar of the top six and a European qualification bid this term, and a double from Killian Phillips helped St Mirren get off to a fine start at Falkirk Stadium.

“I thought the performance was excellent and if we can build on that we can go and achieve something as a group,” McLeish said. “I’m delighted for the group. We got the result our performance deserved. I thought we were excellent.”

Sports.title: Transfer news: Welbeck joins Chelsea, Brentford complete record Sangaré deal
Sports.content:
Chelsea have signed Brighton’s veteran striker Danny Welbeck in a deal worth a reported £5m. Welbeck has agreed a two-year contract and will link up with Xabi Alonso’s squad on their pre-season tour.

The 35-year-old’s move to Stamford Bridge is a break from Chelsea’s policy of signing younger players with the potential to be developed. It is the first time they have paid a transfer fee for a player over the age of 26 since they signed Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang from Barcelona in 2022 when the striker was 33.

“When you hear of interest from Chelsea, it’s something that fills you with such immense pride. Knowing the history of Chelsea, it’s a club that wants to win trophies and is pushing to do that every single season,” Welbeck said.

“I’m really honoured to come to a club of this stature at what feels like a really exciting time. I know a few of the boys already and I’ve had fantastic conversations with the manager and already feel that connection. I’ve got that fire in my belly and I’m ready to give it everything for this club to make everyone at Chelsea, and the supporters, proud.”

Alonso was keen to add experience to his squad after last season’s disappointing 10th-place finish in the Premier League. He opted for Welbeck after the former Manchester United and Arsenal forward enjoyed a memorable campaign with Brighton.

Welbeck, who has 42 caps for England, scored 13 goals in 37 Premier League games last term after netting 10 times in 2024-25.

Welbeck’s arrival in west London will raise questions about the future of Chelsea striker Liam Delap, who signed from Ipswich last season, as well as fellow forwards Nicolas Jackson and Marc Guiu.

Welbeck is the latest player to move from Brighton to Chelsea in recent years after João Pedro, Moisés Caicedo, Robert Sánchez and Marc Cucurella, who joined Real Madrid earlier this summer.

Chelsea spent a British record £117m to sign the England forward Morgan Rogers, 24, from Aston Villa in July. They also secured the France defender Maxence Lacroix, 26, from Crystal Palace for £52m earlier this week and signed Atalanta defender Marco Palestra, 21, for £43m.

Brentford seal record Sangaré deal

Brentford have signed the Mali international Mamadou Sangaré from ⁠Lens for a club-record fee, reported to be £39m. Sangaré, 24, joins Brentford on a five-year contract, with ⁠the option to extend for another year.

“Mamadou ​is someone ‌that we’ve tracked ‌for quite some time. He’s been on ‌our radar and was a player we were really keen to bring in,” the Brentford head coach Keith Andrews said. “He’s a humble young man, but he’s equally as ⁠determined to succeed in his career. He ​fits ​everything we want from ​a Brentford player, on and ​off the ‌pitch.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Sangaré left Austria’s Rapid Vienna to ‌join Lens last year, and featured prominently as they won the ​French Cup for the first time and finished second in Ligue 1.

View image in fullscreen Mamadou Sangaré has swapped RC Lens for Brentford in a £39m move. Photograph: Stéphanie Lecocq/Reuters

Bournemouth have announced the signing of António Silva from Benfica for a fee believed to be in the region of £25m. The 22-year-old defender becomes new manager Marco Rose’s second signing of the summer after the arrival of Álvaro Rodríguez earlier this week.

Silva made 235 senior appearances for Benfica and collected six major honours during his time in Portugal. He told the club website: “I am very happy to be here. It’s a pleasure to play for Bournemouth and in the Premier League.

“The mentality is always to win. I will try my best, and I will play for the fans. We have everything here that helps us perform on the pitch, and I can’t wait to get started.”

Sports.title: De Zerbi wants ‘lovely guy’ Richarlison to stay at Tottenham after winner sinks Chelsea
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi wants Richarlison to stay at Tottenham, but says the striker, who has been linked with a move away, is still unsure about his future.

The Brazilian scored a last-gasp winner as 10-man Tottenham defeated Chelsea 2-1 in a pre-season friendly in Sydney, with Kevin Danso sent off just minutes after coming on as a half-time substitute.

Speaking after the game, De Zerbi said Richarlison had not clarified if he was going to depart this summer. “I don’t know, I didn’t understand well, because sometimes he said to stay, sometimes he leaves, we have to speak. Anyway, there is not any problem, he’s a lovely guy. All of us love him, the teammates, the club, the staff, because he works hard every day.”

Richarlison has less than a year left on his contract after joining Tottenham from Everton in 2022. He has struggled to find consistent form during his time in north London but De Zerbi said it would be difficult to replace his goals.

“For me he’s still an important player because it’s not so easy to find another striker as Richarlison, because Richarlison scored goals and he knows the way. The new striker, we don’t know, the other striker, we don’t know. He [Richarlison] scored 12 goals last season, not for luck, because he feels the way to score.”

Richarlison bagged a 92nd-minute winner for Tottenham against Chelsea in front of more than 80,000 fans at Sydney’s Accor Stadium. The Brazilian was the first player to react after Jamie Donley’s shot came back off a post, prodding the ball into an empty net to avert the need for a penalty shootout.

It was the first time that the two sides have met outside the UK and the match started in the spirit of a true London derby. Conor Gallagher flew into a challenge on Dário Essugo after 10 minutes, picking up a yellow card and a fair few heckles from the largely Chelsea-supporting crowd. Jan Paul van Hecke clattered into João Pedro, while Dominic Solanke and Levi Colwill tussled off the ball.

This fixture has had its fair share of red cards over the years and there was another one to add to the list, after Danso was sent off three minutes after coming off the bench. A poor surface got the better of the Spurs defender as he failed to control a backpass, allowing João Pedro to run on to the ball and through on goal. Danso lunged headfirst into the Chelsea forward, with the referee reaching straight for his pocket.

View image in fullscreen Kevin Danso is shown a red card three minutes after coming on as a substitute. Photograph: David Neilson/EPA

De Zerbi said the sending off made the game harder for both sides. “It was worse for us and for Chelsea, because if you consider the condition of the pitch, very bad. And if you consider we are starting from two weeks, maybe less than three weeks, the second half you start the fatigue and playing, attacking against 10 players behind the line of the ball is tough for every team.”

De Zerbi’s side were on top in the early stages and took a deserved lead on 17 minutes when the new signing Sandro Tonali scored his first goal for Tottenham. The midfielder’s side-footed effort from outside the area took a deflection, wrong-footing the Chelsea goalkeeper Teddy Sharman-Lowe before nestling into the bottom corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Spurs were only ahead for four minutes, as Estêvão Willian got the better of Andy Robertson to head home at the back post after some good work from Jamie Gittens down the left.

The game lost its competitive edge in the second half with both sides making a flurry of substitutions, before Richarlison settled it at the death.

Chelsea will now head to Hong Kong where they will be joined by Mykhailo Mudryk, who has been cleared to play again after the Football Association and the World Anti-Doping Agency resolved his appeal against a ban for failing a doping test. The Ukrainian winger was suspended for four years after failing a drug test in 2024. De Zerbi, who managed Mudryk at Shakhtar Donetsk, said he viewed the player as one of his “sons”.

“I’m very happy – he deserves to play, he’s a good guy, top player. Hopefully he can show what he suffered in the last two years, in the next season, maybe not against Tottenham, but he’s a lovely guy and he’s a very, very good player.”

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola reveals why his Liverpool coach rejected EFL jobs this summer
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola says assistant Tommy Elphick's Liverpool support convinced him not to take a Championship job this summer.

Iraola is continuing his preparations to lead Liverpool into the new season after succeeding Arne Slot in the Anfield dugout.

2 Iraola signed a two-year contract as Liverpool's new head coach Credit: Getty

And he's brought with him to Merseyside two of his colleagues from Bournemouth, who he guided to an historic seventh-placed Premier League finish last season.

Elphick and Shaun Cooper, both Bournemouth legends as players, were coaching at the club when Iraola arrived in 2023 and have followed him to his next job in charge of the Reds.

And Iraola is glad to have them with him, telling Liverpool club media: "Yes, for me, Tommy and Shaun are very valuable because they have been English players, they’ve played in the Premier League, the Championship, League One; they understand the culture, they understand what the players are thinking.

"And they’ve gone through the process of understanding how to build a team, because we didn’t know each other when I arrived at Bournemouth and they have seen all the process during these three years where we’ve been evolving, we’ve been adding different things.

"So now, I think they are the best ones to transmit the same thing to the players and to the new coaches, that we already had in the club. They are helping me a lot.

"I think they are sometimes in more touch with the players than me because always with the manager there is a little bit of more distance, I think the players are more comfortable sometimes with the assistants.

"They know also when to filter the information – when I need to know things. Sometimes they don’t tell me the things that for sure stay between them and the players. They are brilliant in this."

Who could Elphick have joined?

Iraola might have lost Elphick this summer, as he explained: "Tommy, I tell him, he is living his dream. I think he had this summer a chance to coach in the Championship. Good clubs called him, but I think he couldn’t miss this because he’s been a big Liverpool fan.

"We were talking the other day, meeting with the legends we have here, with Robbie Fowler, Ian Rush – he was like, ‘Oof, this is big.’ I like how he is feeling it and I think it’s very nice for him, yes."

Elphick held talks with Bristol City over his first senior role in management.

2 Elphick worked under Iraola at Bournemouth Credit: AFP

Despite the 38-year-old being impressed with the Robins' plans, he decided against the move.

Burnley were also believed to have shown interest in Elphick.

Liverpool beat Wrexham 1-0 in New York in their latest pre-season friendly on Thursday.

The Reds round off their US tour by taking on Leeds in Chicago on Sunday night, before home friendlies against Monaco and Como.

They begin the new Premier League campaign away to Newcastle on August 23 then meet Nottingham Forest in their home opener six days later.

Liverpool fell short in the defence of their Premier League crown last term, finishing fifth – and while that was enough to clinch Champions League qualification, their performance ultimately cost title-winning boss Slot his job.

Iraola is one of eight confirmed new Premier League managers for 2026/27.

That number will rise to nine after Eddie Howe stepped down as Newcastle boss on Friday.

The Magpies are expected to appoint Al-Ahli head coach Matthias Jaissle as Howe's successor.

Sports.title: Secret details of Cristiano Ronaldo’s wedding to Georgina Rodriguez ‘leaked’ but he cannot deliver on one vow
Sports.content:
Secret details of Cristiano Ronaldo’s wedding to Georgina Rodriguez ‘leaked’ but he cannot deliver on one vow

Cristiano Ronaldo is set to marry fiancee Georgina Rodriguez on his home island of Madeira.

The couple will reportedly tie the knot at a cathedral in Funchal next Saturday (August 8).

3 Ronaldo and Rodriguez have been together for a decade Credit: Getty

And they're said to have booked the nearby five-star Savoy Palace hotel for their wedding reception.

A source told The Sun: "Guests at the hotel have been told two floors will be out of use on Friday and Saturday, as well as several bar areas."

Ronaldo was born in Funchal, the capital of Madeira – an archipelagic autonomous region of Portugal around 500 miles south-west of the mainland.

He began his youth career with local clubs Andorinha and Nacional before joining Sporting Lisbon as a 12-year-old.

Ronaldo and Rodriguez have been in a relationship since 2016.

The superstar striker, 41, got engaged to the Argentine-Spanish model, 32, last August.

Ronaldo had previously said the pair had planned to marry after this summer's World Cup.

In fact, the five-time Ballon d'Or winner told Piers Morgan: "I hope to arrive at my wedding with the [World Cup] trophy."

Unfortunately for Ronaldo, that dream ended as Portugal were knocked out of the tournament by Spain in the last 16.

The Portugal captain has not retired from international football but did confirm he had played his last World Cup game.

3 Ronaldo played in a joint record six World Cups Credit: Getty

With 233 caps and 146 goals, he is the most-capped and highest-scoring international footballer of all time.

Ronaldo met Rodriguez while he was playing for Real Madrid.

He revealed she was the only woman he'd dated who he felt like settling down with.

Nowadays, Ronaldo continues to play his club football in Saudi Arabia for Al-Nassr, who he captained to the 2025/26 Saudi Pro League title.

He still has just under a year left to run on his contract in the Saudi capital, Riyadh.

As such, he's set to still be playing professionally beyond his 42nd birthday in February.

3 Ronaldo and Rodriguez met in 2016 Credit: https://x.com/Cristiano

Ronaldo is now managed by former Tottenham boss Ange Postecoglou, who was appointed by Al-Nassr last month.

Meanwhile, away from the pitch, Ronaldo has been tipped for a surprise move into acting.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish warned his Man City career is over as Enzo Maresca admits he hasn’t spoken to £100m man
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish warned his Man City career is over as Enzo Maresca admits he hasn’t spoken to £100m man

Jack Grealish has been warned that his future lies away from Man City.

That’s what The Athletic’s City correspondent Sam Lee told Weekend Sports Breakfast as speculation surrounding his next club continues.



3 Grealish scored two goals and contributed six assists for Everton before his injury Credit: Getty

The 30-year-old returned to his parent club this summer with his future unclear after spending last season on loan at Everton.

The 39-cap England international scored twice and registered six assists in 22 appearances for the Toffees across all competitions.

However, he sustained a stress fracture in his foot playing against another of his old clubs, Aston Villa, in January.



Grealish's injury not only ended his club season early, but also ruled out any hope of making a late dash for England's World Cup squad.

Everton opted against activating their £50million buy option in the winger's loan deal, which saw him return to the Etihad Stadium.



talkSPORT understands that there is interest from the Saudi Pro League for Grealish, with Al Hilal a potential option.

Having been frozen out by Pep Guardiola, Grealish may have harboured hopes of making a fresh start after Maresca replaced the Spaniard following the latter's decision to step down in May.



However, that foot injury ensured he's been unable to make the club's pre-season tour, and Lee claimed the writing is on the wall for his future at the Etihad.

"I think it's only a question mark insofar as where he's gonna go, how much," He said on talkSPORT's Weekend Breakfast.

"It's like a couple of years ago when there was, I'm not saying there's been like a falling out with Grealish, but it's a similar situation where I don't think he's got much of a future there.

3 Maresca a new manager may still mean the same outcome for Grealish Credit: Getty



"But with [Joao] Cancelo a couple of years ago when there was a falling out, he was on the preseason tour, but it was like, they are gonna get rid of him. It's just a question of where he goes.

"With Grealish, he wasn't really left out explicitly. He's still kind of coming back from that injury you mentioned.

"He had foot surgery in February. Obviously, [Enzo] Maresca has changed, and there's a chance that he could have a different view on it from [Pep] Guardiola.

"But under Guardiola, he was very much out of the picture.

"Guardiola and Maresca are close. They'll have talked a lot. I'd be surprised if Grealish gets another look in, to be honest."



Maresca’s response

Maresca was asked about Grealish’s future and surprisingly admitted that he has not even spoken to him.

3 Grealish chipped in with eight goal contributions for Everton when on loan last season

Speaking to the media, Maresca said: "I didn't speak with Jack while I am here. Jack is a City player. When we are back in Manchester, if he is fit he will work with us."

Grealish joined City from Villa for £100m in the summer of 2021 and has enjoyed a trophy laden spell at the Etihad.



He played a vital role in their treble success during the 2022/23 season and has won three Premier League titles overall.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi vents fury as Casemiro howler sees Inter Miami drop points in home debut
Sports.content:
Messi was far from impressed as Casemiro's own goal gifted Columbus an equaliser on his return to Miami

Casemiro suffered a horror home debut for Inter Miami, as he gave away possession and then scored an own goal moments later.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid midfielder signed with the Major League Soccer club on July 22, as a 34-year-old free agent.

6 Casemiro scored an own goal on a home debut to forget for Miami Credit: Getty

He will play alongside Lionel Messi, who returned on Saturday night for his first minutes since losing the World Cup final with Argentina.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner appeared as a second-half substitute against Columbus Crew, in a match that finished 2-2 and featured a moment to forget for Casemiro.

Casemiro risks Lionel Messi wrath with Miami mistake

Just 33 minutes into his home debut, the Brazilian slipped as he attempted to find a teammate with a pass out of the back line.

It was intercepted by Columbus midfielder Hugo Picard, who pushed forward on the counter.

A sweeping move ended with Taha Habroune playing the ball into the Miami box, where an off-balance Casemiro poked the ball past his own goalkeeper.

The own goal handed Columbus an equaliser from nothing, after Luis Suarez had opened the scoring in the 16th minute.

Casemiro looked dejected after his mistake -- and new team-mate Messi appeared rather upset too.

MLS cameras cut to the forward scowling on the bench.

"A goal is a goal," Columbus' official X account later posted on social media, rubbing salt in the wounds by sharing a clip of Casemiro's embarrassing slip.

Miami went on to restore their lead through Noah Allen in added time at the end of the first half, but a late goal from Brais Mendez ensured the points were shared at Nu Stadium.

6 Casemiro's gaffe gifted Columbus an equaliser against Miami Credit: Apple TV

6 The 34-year-old midfielder looked devastated after his own goal Credit: Apple TV

6 Cameras caught Messi's scowl on the bench as he watched the moment unfold Credit: Apple TV

It was the first time the team has dropped points since resuming play following the World Cup.

While he didn't get off to the best of starts alongside Messi, Casemiro has vowed to help the greatest player of all time in his request for more trophies.

"The amount of trouble Messi gave me, of course, I dreamed of playing with him," the midfielder said, after joining Miami.

"I always wanted to play with the best. I could never stop him, I always needed the help of my teammates.

"I am very happy to be alongside him now and I want to continue winning titles with him. I want to enjoy being alongside him, help him and make him even greater.

"He is one of the gods of football, if not the God of football himself, and I want to help."

6 Casemiro has insisted he wants to help Messi win trophies at Miami Credit: Getty

At 34, Casemiro has agreed a contract through the end of the 2027 MLS season.

Casemiro no longer in Brazil national team plans

He will be fully focused on club football, with Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti confirming last month that the midfielder is no longer in his national team plans.

Ancelotti is looking to build a younger squad for the 2028 Copa America, meaning Casemiro, Danilo and the recently-retired Neymar will all miss out.

"I think this World Cup marks the end of ⁠a generation of very important players," the coach told Brazilian broadcaster Ge TV.

6 Ancelotti has confirmed Casemiro is not part of his Brazil plans Credit: Getty

"Starting with Neymar, going through Danilo, Casemiro, all ​those players who were over 30 years old at the World Cup.

"We are going to map out new players who can enter, I'm not saying for the next World Cup in 2030, but who can already be competitive in the first objective, which ​is the Copa America in 2028."

Sports.title: Man United consider surprise move for Premier League star as Lewis Hall alternative
Sports.content:
Manchester United could make a move for Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly.

talkSPORT understands that while Newcastle's Lewis Hall remains Man United's preferred left-back target, Lewis-Skelly is being considered.

2 Lewis-Skelly was part of Arsenal's 2025/26 Premier League-winning squad but didn't feature as much as he'd have liked Credit: Getty

Man United are looking to bolster their options on the left-hand side of defence, with Luke Shaw currently the only senior player in that role.

talkSPORT initially reported in March that Man United had identified Lewis-Skelly as a possible signing.

The 19-year-old saw minutes hard to come by at Arsenal last season, and his cause won't be helped by the permanent signing of the versatile Piero Hincapie – who thrived on loan at left-back to help the Gunners end their 22-year Premier League title drought.

With Riccardo Calafiori also ahead of Lewis-Skelly in the pecking order, a move away from the Emirates Stadium might be the England international's best option as he looks to kick on his career.

Having risen through Arsenal's youth ranks and broken into the first team in 2024/25, Lewis-Skelly made just five Premier League starts last term amid stiff competition for places.

While he's already been capped six times by England, he'll need to be playing more regular club football if he's to truly establish himself at international level.

Lewis-Skelly still has four years remaining on his Gunners contract and is valued by Transfermarkt at just under £38.5m.

However, Man United have been told to pull out all the stops to bring Hall to Old Trafford.

With Eddie Howe stepping down as Newcastle boss on Friday, more player exits from St. James' Park might well follow – and Hall could be among them.

talkSPORT pundit Flex has told Man United to put in a substantial opening bid for the 21-year-old.

2 Four-cap England international Hall has made over 100 appearances for Newcastle since joining from Chelsea three years ago Credit: Getty

"We’re not in charge of the purse, but I’m saying you slap £50million down – opening bid – and just ruffle some feathers in there," he said on Inside Devils.

Man United have been busy adding to their squad during Michael Carrick's first full transfer window as head coach.

Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos are the headline arrivals so far, joining from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively.

The Red Devils have also added Wales goalkeeper Karl Darlow on a free transfer following his departure from Leeds.

Having continued their pre-season with a 2-1 friendly win over Atletico Madrid in Sweden on Saturday – with wonderkid JJ Gabriel playing his first senior minutes – Carrick's men get the 2026/27 campaign underway with a trip to newly promoted Hull on August 22.

They then take on another promoted side, Ipswich, in their home opener eight days later.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta’s response to Vinicius Jr question sends Arsenal fans into a frenzy
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta again outlined Arsenal's transfer ambitions, amid continued talk of a move for Vinicius Jr.

The Brazil superstar remains linked with a switch to the Gunners, with his Real Madrid future yet to be resolved.

2 Could we see Vinicius Jr lighting up the Premier League this coming season? Credit: Getty

Vinicius is out of contract at the Bernabeu next summer, and talkSPORT reported last month that Arsenal were considering a surprise swoop for the 26-year-old forward.

And now comments from Arteta have heightened Gunners fans' excitement around the possibility of what would be surely the most momentous transfer of the summer.

Arsenal 'won't sit still'

Asked 'when's Vini joining?' after Arsenal's 4-1 pre-season friendly win over Girona, Arteta smiled.

And he went on to tell reporters about the prospect of more signings as the Gunners prepare for their Premier League title defence: "Well, we are already active trying to improve and evolve the team – that's clear.

"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else, and you just can see the transfer market and our opponents what we are doing.

"We won't sit still and we are very ambitious what we want to do."

Could that ambition extend to bringing Vinicius to the Emirates Stadium?

Gunners fans have been getting carried away with themselves following that interview.

One said: "Remember same reaction from Wenger when Ozil signed."

Another added: "That smile says it all."

2 Vinicius has scored 128 goals in 376 appearances for Real Madrid Credit: Getty

Well, Arsenal fans have been warned that the situation might be a misdirection, as Transfer Insiders host Rickie Haywood-Williams suggested.

"I think this is the biggest red herring in history in terms of live transfers," he said on talkSPORT.

"Because I feel like Vinicius Jr has been trying to get a new contract at Real Madrid for the last couple of years.

"In that time, they’ve signed [Kylian] Mbappe – Mbappe is on incredible money and he [Vinicius] obviously is going to want parity with that or somewhere close, and I think he’s using the Premier League as a bit of a bargaining chip to try and up the ante on his money, to try and get a bigger contract."

Gunners' squad takes shape

Arsenal have made two new additions to their squad during the current transfer window.

Goalkeeper Illan Meslier has come in on a free transfer after leaving Leeds, while winger Christos Tzolis has arrived from Club Brugge in a deal worth £34m.

Title-winning full-back Piero Hincapie has also made his loan move from Bayer Leverkusen permanent.

And the Gunners are closing in on Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal are back in pre-season action against Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday.

Their first competitive game of the new campaign sees them face FA Cup winners Manchester City in the Community Shield at Wembley on August 16 – before the Premier League curtain-raiser at home to newly promoted Coventry five days later.

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold told to explore controversial Premier League return at specific club
Sports.content:
Liverpool should be open to re-signing Trent Alexander-Arnold.

That's the strong belief of talkSPORT's Angelina Kelly, who called on supporters to embrace the possibility of the right-back returning to Anfield.

3 Alexander-Arnold won two Premier League titles with Liverpool after coming through the Reds' academy Credit: Getty



The relationship between Alexander-Arnold and Reds fans became strained after he opted against signing a new contract with his boyhood club and joined Real Madrid last summer, with some going as far as to boo their former hero.

But the 27-year-old's move to Spain has proved far from successful so far, after he started just 14 LaLiga games last season and failed to score in any competition for the first time since his maiden senior campaign of 2016/17.

And Kelly believes Liverpool should at least think about bringing Alexander-Arnold back to Merseyside amid question marks over their own right-back position.

Joining Nick Bright on talkSPORT's Transfer Insiders, she said: "I know what it’s like for a player to, in your opinion, betray the club – especially one of your own, especially being a Liverpudlian. I get it.



"When Real Madrid come calling, it is hard to say no – we have to be honest with that – and he’s made the move and it hasn’t really worked out.

"And you look at Liverpool and you think do they need a new right-back?



"I mean, [Jeremie] Frimpong didn’t look great last season – I think he’s probably better playing further forward – [Conor] Bradley injured…

"I think maybe they should cut their losses and just explore the Trent situation.



"I’m not saying you’ve got to sign him immediately – let’s just explore this. Because Real Madrid have signed another right-back in Denzel Dumfries – that is not good news for Trent [who has been warned to expect to lose his place].

"So, why can’t everyone just take some ownership…take a bit of accountability and we can all come back together and be happy?

3 Alexander-Arnold faces right-back competition from new arrival Denzel Dumfries Credit: Getty

"You know, Marcus Rashford and Manchester United, they're having not exactly the same but a similar situation of having to come back.



"I think that there is a way back, and surely there’s one Liverpool fan listening that would have him back – I can’t be on my own here.

"I just think that…you may as well try it because…he was so good at Liverpool…

"Back at Liverpool where a few games, a few goals maybe, a few assists or something – he does something. If he ends up helping Liverpool, like, win the Premier League or get to a Champions League final – if he does something really, really good for Liverpool, I know the fans are loyal, but surely that’s his way of saying sorry and making up for it [his departure]?

"If he can make up for it, why not?"

Reminded by Bright that she'd said fans should accept Alexander-Arnold back in a Liverpool shirt, Kelly affirmed: "They should have him back because on paper, things have gone wrong, yes – but there's always a road back.



3 Alexander-Arnold has played 354 games for Liverpool... so far

"People sometimes deserve second chances and I think Trent does.

"So, the way things are going – right-back situation, you've got a gap there – get him back in."

Liverpool have completed two first-team signings so far this summer, bringing in France U21 defender Jeremie Jacquet and World Cup-winning Spain forward Victor Munoz from Rennes and Osasuna respectively.

Sports.title: West Ham’s ‘next Declan Rice’ set for permanent transfer to Champions League club
Sports.content:
West Ham have agreed to sell academy graduate Freddie Potts to Club Brugge in a deal worth around £10million, talkSPORT understands.

The 22-year-old was expected to be a key member of the Hammers' squad in their upcoming Championship season, as they seek an immediate return to the top flight.



5 Freddie Potts looks set to depart West Ham after making 32 senior appearances Credit: Getty

But Potts - the son of club icon Steve - now looks set to end his 17-year association with the club he first joined as a six-year-old.

talkSPORT understands the midfielder has been permitted to travel to Belgium for a medical with top-flight side Club Brugge.

Despite a move appearing close, Potts was named on West Ham's bench for their final pre-season friendly against German second division side FC Magdeburg.



The young Englishman did not feature in the clash, though, as the Irons rounded off their season's preparations with a 1-1 draw.

And the east London outfit now look to have been dealt a late blow ahead of their campaign, with Potts seemingly destined to leave.



If his move to Brugge goes through, the midfielder will be swapping the Championship for Champions League football, after the Belgian giants qualified by clinching league glory last term.

Potts, who has drawn comparisons to former West Ham captain Declan Rice, is being lined up as a replacement for Raphael Onyedika.



The Nigeria international is closing in on a move to Bundesliga outfit Eintracht Frankfurt for a rumoured £7.6m fee.

Pott twist

Potts' anticipated West Ham exit comes just as he looked set to play a greater role for the club in the Championship.

The local lad made 22 Premier League appearances last season, starting 12 times as the Hammers were relegated on the final day.

5 Potts captained West Ham in a 1-1 draw with Rangers in pre-season Credit: Getty



5 Potts' dad, Steve, made over 500 appearances for West Ham in 17 years at the club Credit: Getty

But having spent the 2024/25 season on loan at Portsmouth in the second tier, he was expected to feature more in the upcoming campaign.

The departure of key man Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham in a £85m deal appeared to pave the way for this.

Potts wore the captain's armband during West Ham's pre-season friendly draw with Rangers in July, suggesting he would be among Nuno Espirito Santo's starting midfielders.



It appears Potts himself even expected this, having recently shared his plans to become an established player at the London Stadium.

In an interview with BBC Radio London, he said: "I want to play as much as I can for West Ham this season.

"I want to show that I've got the experience in the Championship from before with previous clubs. I'm excited for the challenge that comes ahead."

5 Potts has never played outside of English football in his fledgling career Credit: Getty



Potts also spoke of the desire throughout the club to bounce back to the Premier League at the first attempt following relegation.

He added: "I think it's going to be a very good season for us."

"We can see the love for the club from the fans, and we want to replicate that on the pitch.

"We're very confident going into this season that we can achieve the goal that everyone wants to achieve and no doubt the fans will back us."

End of the road?

Should he finalise his departure, Potts will leave West Ham having made 32 first-team appearances.



He made his senior debut in a 1–0 loss against Dinamo Zagreb in the Conference League in 2021, with his Premier League bow coming last August, coming on as a half-time substitute in a 5-1 loss to Chelsea.

5 Nuno Espirito Santo is looking to win promotion from the Championship for the second time in his career with West Ham Credit: Getty

West Ham will play their first competitive game of the season next week, as they host league rivals Portsmouth in the Carabao Cup first round.

They will then get their league campaign underway a week later with an away trip to fellow relegated side Burnley on August 16.

Sports.title: Spain's 'down to earth' World Cup hero Marc Cucurella praised for wholesome interaction with postman as he lets him wear his winner's medal
Sports.content:
Spain's 'down to earth' World Cup hero Marc Cucurella praised for wholesome interaction with postman as he lets him wear his winner's medal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Spain star Marc Cucurella thrilled his local postman after the World Cup winner offered him the medal he won Stateside last month to wear after dropping off his deliveries.

The former Chelsea defender has been a Horsham resident for some years, moving there after a previous home was targeted by burglars shortly after his 2023 transfer to the west London club.

The West Sussex enclave provided a peaceful sanctuary for Cucurella and his young family, with locals frequently sharing their positive experiences on social media if they crossed the defender's path.

But few can claim the experience his postman Gary enjoyed during one of his last rounds for the departing Real Madrid star.

Sharing his story with Horsham's social media account, the postman said: 'Had the pleasure of chatting to local World Cup winner Marc Cucurella while delivering his post today.

'Very nice, down-to-earth guy. Let me hold his winners' medal.

Marc Cucurella was praised for his thoughtful interaction with his local postman in Horsham

Gary the postman was allowed to try on Cucurella's gold World Cup winners' medal

'I reckon I am the first Englishman to hold a World Cup winners' medal in 60 years.'

Fans were quick to show their support for Cucurella's once-in-a-lifetime gesture, with one commenting: 'The biggest and greatest accolade for any football player. And he was kind enough to share that.'

Another added: 'Amazing stuff. He sounds like a really nice guy.'

One chronicler of life in Horsham wrote: 'Amazing. We keep hearing great things and sorry to be losing him. Wishing him the best of luck in his new adventures'.

In the photograph, Cucurella showed off his new braided hairstyle, a notable departure from his iconic curls.

Switching up his look has been just one piece of the 28-year-old's post-World Cup celebrations, with the player also making good on his promise to ink the face of his manager Luis de la Fuente on his body.

Horsham's social media account has previously shared snapshots of Cucurella's life in the south of England, and cheered on their 'local boy' in Spain's World Cup final against Argentina.

Since becoming a resident in the market town, Cucurella and his family have slotted in seamlessly to local life, interacting with other parents at their children's schools and even becoming regular visitors to Indian restaurant Hen & Chicken.

Life in Horsham is likely one of the reasons that Cucurella's partner Claudia Rodriguez admitted that she was feeling mixed emotions about his move back to Spain to join Real Madrid.

Posting on Instagram after the £47.4m deal was announced, she wrote: 'I don't know how to say goodbye to my home.'

'Thank you to everyone who has been a part of this experience; I feel so lucky for everything we've shared these past years. I arrived with two babies and I'm leaving with two little boys and a British girl, and I don't know how I'm going to explain to them that Chelsea is no longer part of our lives.

'Everything we've experienced these past years has been a pure learning experience; we've lived through it all, but above all, we've enjoyed this journey. Thank you to everyone who has been a part of this chapter of our lives, thank you to my girls, whom I'm going to miss a lot, and thank you to every Blue I've met. I wish you all the best; London will always be Blue.'

Cucurella's partner Claudia Rodriguez spoke last month about her sadness at leaving England

Rodriguez's comments come in stark contrast to how she felt before the family moved into their latest house in England.

In the wake of the traumatising burglary, the influencer told Daily Mail Sport that she had been afraid to go to sleep.

'The security is one of things I'm more worried about,' Rodriguez admitted. 'It's very hard when you are not comfortable at your home.

'I'm scared to sleep alone with my kids, for example. So for today, the most important thing for me, I think, is the security of me and my family.'

Sports.title: Son of music legend Phil Collins and half-brother of actress Lily Lily joins former Bundesliga champions - but there's a very slim chance he will face Harry Kane
Sports.content:
Son of music legend Phil Collins and half-brother of actress Lily Lily joins former Bundesliga champions - but there's a very slim chance he will face Harry Kane

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Phil Collins's son Mathew has signed for former Bundesliga champions 1860 Munich as he continues his football career.

The German side confirmed they have signed Collins, a 21-year-old midfielder on a one-year contract.

Mathew, who was born in Switzerland, had previously been part of the youth set-up at Bundesliga side Hannover 96.

He then moved to WSG Tirol in Austria, before joining second tier side Austria Salzburg last summer.

Collins made four first-team appearances for Austria Salzburg last season, before leaving the club at the end of the campaign.

Phil, 75, had attended one of his matches in November, with Mathew sharing another picture alongside his music legend father in April.

Mathew Collins has signed for former German champions 1860 Munich in the fourth tier

Mathew is the son of music legend Phil Collins, the former drummer and singer of Genesis

Several years ago, rock great Phil opened up on his son's passion for sport.

'Mat loves music, but loves his football even more,' said Phil, the former drummer and later lead singer of rock band Genesis.

'He is certain he'll turn professional. 'The other day he said, "Another five years and I'll be gone."

'He also looks at everything, Bundesliga, French league, everything.'

Mathew's latest challenge with 1860 Munich comes after the historic German side dropped into the fourth tier last season.

1860 Munich had finished eighth in the third-tier 3. Liga last term, but the club were relegated after failing to obtain a licence ahead of the new season.

The club were founding members of the Bundesliga and won the German title in 1966, as well as German Cups in 1942 and 1964.

1860 Munich last featured in the top flight in the 2003-04 season, but have since slipped down the divisions after financial difficulties and the recent failure to receive a licence for the third tier.

Despite being part of the lower leagues, Mathew still could have the chance to face England captain Harry Kane this season should 1860 Munich be drawn against their local rivals Bayern Munich in the German Cup this season.

Mathew had shared a photo with his father after he had watched one of his matches for Austria Salzburg last season

Mathew's half-sister Lily, the star of Emily in Paris, said she 'couldn't be prouder' following his move

Phil isn't Mathew's only superstar relative, with half sister Lily having starred as an actress, most notably in the lead role in Emily in Paris.

Lily showed her support for Mathew's latest move, responding on Instagram: 'Couldn’t be prouder of you! Sooooo exciting!'

Phil revealed this weekend that his children Mathew, Lily, Joely, Simon and Nic had all been summoned to say their final goodbyes to the singer after he almost drank himself to death two years ago.

The 75-year-old singer admitted things could have gone 'terribly wrong' back in April 2024 when he was lying unconscious in a Swiss hospital, prompting his long-term manager to call his five kids to his bedside to make some tough decisions.

Phil told The Sunday Times Magazine: 'Because there were some decisions to be made about 'Do we keep Phil on life support?' kind of thing. My kidneys were packing up, my organs were just seizing up. People were coming to say goodbye...

'But I don't remember them coming, I didn't have no idea this was going on. They were all worried that they wouldn't see me again. It could have gone terribly wrong.'

Phil recovered, though he has a number of other health issues, including type 2 diabetes and nerve damage in his hands, and needs crutches to walk following multiple surgeries on his spine and knees.

Sports.title: Under-fire Gianni Infantino gets backing from Asian nations following UEFA's charge to depose president after his disastrous money-making plan
Sports.content:
Under-fire Gianni Infantino gets backing from Asian nations following UEFA's charge to depose president after his disastrous money-making plan

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gianni Infantino's hopes of surviving as FIFA president have been boosted after four Asian nations publicly backed him following the abolition of divisive plans to sell stakes in the World Cup.

UEFA partnered with the North, Central America and Caribbean confederation (CONCACAF) and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) to force Infantino to drop plans to sell a £3.1billion stake in the World Cup to private investors.

UEFA and CONCACAF have since called on Infantino to quit - but their ploy to depose the Swiss football administrator has hit a roadblock after Kuwait, Qatar, Sri Lanka and Lebanon reiterated their confidence in his leadership.

UEFA and CONCACAF make up 90 of FIFA's 211 member associations. Although that is above the 20 per cent threshold to trigger a vote of no confidence, it falls short of the majority needed to topple Infantino.

With Infantino retaining support from Africa while South America are expected to take the same position, AFC members would be required to oust the FIFA president.

New Zealand could join Europe and CONCACAF's resistance, but it is doubtful that the remaining 10 members of the Oceania Football Confederation would follow suit.

In a statement welcoming the decision to abandon the private equity proposal, the AFC refrained from defying the FIFA leadership.

Gianni Infantino's plan to sell a £3.1billion stake in the World Cup was shown a red card

Infantino's presidency is at risk, with UEFA and CONCACAF calling for him to go, but Asia could yet come to his rescue

The subsequent championing by Kuwait, Qatar, Sri Lanka and Lebanon reinforced the impression that Infantino retains significant backing across Asia.

The other 40 AFC member associations have yet to comment publicly, suggesting they support the association's statement, which does not challenge his presidency.

Australia, also an AFC member, welcomed the decision to scrap the investment plan and said: 'Attention must now turn to the future.'

While UEFA and CONCACAF have enough support to force a vote of no confidence, they do not currently have the numbers to remove Infantino.

Public opposition stands at 43 per cent of FIFA's membership, below the majority required to unseat him.

That said, the undeclared associations will not necessarily vote in a block with their confederations.

If 16 nations were to break ranks and join the opposition, Infantino's presidency would be in a perilous position.

On Saturday, AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa said: 'I am proud that all our member associations stood united and entrusted the AFC with seeking answers on their behalf regarding this crucial issue concerning the future of global football governance.

'I thank them for their patience, solidarity, and unity, and I assure them that the AFC will always act in their best interests.

'The future of global football must always be shaped through sound consultation, collective dialogue, and respect for the established governance structures of our game.'

UEFA, however, took a more direct position: 'UEFA welcomes FIFA's decision to withdraw its plan to sell a stake in its competitions - including the World Cup - into private hands.

'The proposal was unanimously rejected by UEFA's national associations and by many other federations and confederations of all sizes around the world, whose job it is to protect football.

'We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast-track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

'It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again.

'That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

'The shabby, back-room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through was anything but transparent. This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun.'

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has led the charge against Infantino this week

Infantino, a Lebanese citizen, has been backed by Kuwait, Qatar, Sri Lanka and Lebanon since scrapping the plans

Countless European nations, including England, Wales, the Netherlands and Norway, endorsed the statement.

A spokeswoman for the English FA added: 'We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.'

CONCACAF, as they have all week, followed suit: 'CONCACAF and its 41 Member Associations welcome the withdrawal of the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

'The Confederation also commends its 41 Member Associations and the wider football family for the courage and unity they have shown this week.

'At a moment that demanded principled leadership, our members stood together in defence of football's long-term interests and the principles of good governance. That unity has prevailed.

'A proposal of this magnitude does not reach that stage by accident. It is a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first.

'This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A full review of this leadership must now take place.

'This concern is not CONCACAF's alone. It is shared across many confederations, Member Associations and those who serve and love the game.

'When people entrusted with protecting the game conclude they can no longer do so from within, the football family is entitled to ask how such a proposal was allowed to proceed, and who bears responsibility for it.'

Sports.title: Ex-Manchester United star Casemiro scores an OWN GOAL on his Inter Miami home debut - as Lionel Messi returns to club action after Argentina's World Cup final defeat by Spain
Sports.content:
Ex-Manchester United star Casemiro scores an OWN GOAL on his Inter Miami home debut - as Lionel Messi returns to club action after Argentina's World Cup final defeat by Spain

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Casemiro endured an Inter Miami home debut to forget as he scored an own goal during their 2-2 MLS draw with Columbus Crew on Saturday.

The 34-year-old joined the American outfit on a free transfer after leaving Manchester United - where he earned £375,000-per-week - at the end of the 2025-26 Premier League campaign.

He made his debut on July 26 - playing the full duration in a 1-0 win at Montreal.

And less than a week later he started in front of his new home supporters but with a different outcome.

Leading 1-0 thanks to Luis Suarez's long-range strike, Inter Miami were pegged back on 34 minutes when Casemiro finished past his own goalkeeper.

The Brazilian was at fault for the build-up to the own goal too when he gave away possession inside his own half.

A goal is a goal 🤩 pic.twitter.com/0DZyLQwtIp — The Crew (@ColumbusCrew) August 2, 2026

Casemiro (centre left) scored an own goal on his Inter Miami home debut as they drew 2-2

The 34-year-old was later booked for a foul on Columbus Crew's Sekou Bangoura (centre)

His pass was intercepted by Hugo Picard who passed to Daniel Gazdag. Gazdag played the ball out wide to Taha Habroune and as his low delivery went across the box, a desperate Casemiro could only stretch to divert it past team-mate Rocco Rios Novo.

The Brazil international cut a sheepish figure as the Nu Stadium was stunned into silence. He was later booked too for a foul on Sekou Bangoura.

Noah Allen's goal deep into first-half stoppage time restored the noise inside the ground as Inter Miami took the lead and that volume increased early in the second half when Lionel Messi came on.

Miami talisman Messi came on in the 53rd minute to a rapturous applause in what was his first outing since captaining Argentina to their abject World Cup final defeat by Spain on July 19.

The 39-year-old immediately took the armband from Suarez but he was unable to steer his team to three points as Brais Mendez scored a late equaliser.

Mendez curled a free-kick from the right side that went untouched off the post and into the net in the 84th minute.

Messi is back after leading Argentina to its second-straight World Cup Final appearance. 👏 pic.twitter.com/F91Bo3BC4v — Major League Soccer (@MLS) August 2, 2026

Lionel Messi (right) made a return to Inter Miami action after losing the World Cup final in July

Much like events that occurred in the World Cup, the encounter was delayed by 40 minutes due to inclement weather.

The draw ended Inter Miami's six-game winning streak but they are now unbeaten in seven matches.

Sports.title: Sky Sports reporter Rachel Brookes opens up on her exit and 'horrendous' fan abuse as she reveals 'supportive' chat with Lewis Hamilton
Sports.content:
Sky Sports reporter Rachel Brookes opens up on her exit and 'horrendous' fan abuse as she reveals 'supportive' chat with Lewis Hamilton

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Sky Sports presenter Rachel Brookes has revealed she had a very supportive conversation with Lewis Hamilton after her decision to leave her role, but denied fan abuse had led to her quitting.

Brookes had publicly announced that she had quit her role as a reporter for Sky Sports back in June, which came days before the Austrian Grand Prix.

Brookes, 51, has been part of Sky Sports coverage over the past 14 years, interviewing drivers before and after races.

Speaking on Essential F1, Brookes acknowledged that while it had appeared sudden it had been planned, allowing her time to say farewells to several of the drivers.

Brookes highlighted a conversation with Hamilton, with the Ferrari star offering his support and giving her a hug in the paddock.

'It appeared very sudden, but it wasn't,' Brookes said.

Rachel Brookes has opened up on her decision to quit her role as a reporter on Sky Sports' F1 coverage

Brookes confirmed that her departure had been planned, despite appearing sudden, and had received well-wishes from several drivers

'I had a chance to say goodbye to people in the paddock, to people I worked with, teams, drivers.

'I actually had a chance to say goodbye to Lewis. I had a lovely chat with Lewis. I got some time with Lewis to have a conversation.

'He was, as you would imagine, really, really lovely, very supportive. I won't divulge everything that was said but it was caught by some photographers.

'There's a lovely photo at the end of it where he gives me a massive hug and he says "I hope I see you back in the paddock soon," which was really lovely.

'In Canada, I was finishing media in the TV interview pen and Charles Leclerc had just finished his written interviews and was just walking back out. I was stood by my camera and he just gave me the biggest hug. Didn't say a word just gave me the biggest hug.

'So obviously someone had told him and I just said "thank you" and he left.

'There were a few drivers I didn't get to say goodbye to, just as it happened. I was at home the day after it had been announced and I get these little video messages from a couple of drivers as well, who said "we're going to miss you". It was really, really lovely.

'The paddock is a family. It's an amazing place. I kind of didn't think anyone would notice but the teams and the drivers, it is one big family and it is amazing. I was quite overwhelmed by the response from everybody.'

Lewis Hamilton was among the drivers to have spoken to Brookes, with the Ferrari star having been 'very supportive' during their conversation

Brookes had confirmed her plan to remain involved in Formula One despite leaving Sky, having told fans she would keep them posted on her future ventures.

Her initial announcement had come days after Brookes had revealed the 'utterly horrendous' abuse she received from fans following an interview with Max Verstappen last season.

Brookes insisted her decision to quit Sky Sports was not linked to the abuse she had received.

'It was nothing to do with comments and abuse I got online last year at all,' Brookes said.

'That was resolved very quickly, and I’ve got a great relationship with Max. So absolutely nothing to do with that.

'I know a lot of people thought that, and there were some articles written. Absolutely not the case at all.'

Brookes had spoken to four-time world champion Verstappen after the Spanish Grand Prix last May.

Verstappen had been handed a 10-second penalty at the race having collided with Mercedes' George Russell.

After former world champion Nico Rosberg suggested on commentary that Verstappen may have deliberately collided with his rival, Brookes put it to the Dutchman on camera.

Brookes told the Road to Success podcast: 'I said to Max, "Was it deliberate?". 'And his response was, "Does it matter?."

She then responded: 'Yeah, I think it does to the fans watching and to the kids'.

'I want people to see how good you are, and you make it difficult when you do stuff like that.'

Speaking in June, Brookes said had been privately praised by her peers in broadcasting for asking Verstappen the question, but had been targeted by 'horrific' abuse from fans.

Brookes insisted her departure was not related to receiving 'horrific abuse' from fans after an interview with Max Verstappen last year

Brookes had asked the Verstappen (right), whether he had deliberately collided with George Russell (left) at the Spanish Grand Prix

'I got a lot of messages from people in broadcasting, in sports broadcasting, saying: "Well done for asking the question",' Brookes said.

'Because nobody else in that pen that day asked him that question – and even my colleagues said they wouldn't have asked that question, because they'd have been too scared to ask it.

'But then the fans, the social media side of it, was horrendous. I got people telling me I should never be able to have children because I'm a bad example. I got the most horrific stuff you could imagine.

'And this is from a lot of these profiles with dads with kids with daughters and things like that, where you just look at it and think: "Take a step back. It's a Formula 1 race. It's sport".

'But the stuff I got sent was horrendous, utterly horrendous. So I just closed my comments.'

Verstappen, who had admitted he had made a 'mistake' post-race, ultimately dropped from fifth place to tenth at the Grand Prix.

The Dutchman would go on to miss out on the world title by just two points to Lando Norris.

Boxer is rushed to hospital after knockout as promoter Frank Warren issues statement

Boxer Lee Reeves has been hospitalised after being knocked out during his defeat by Gary Cully on Saturday night.

Reeves was immeadiately attended to by after being stopped in the 10th round of his defeat

Sports.title: Athletes who hate their sports: From a Premier League winner who doesn't watch football to an Ally Pally world champion that isn't a fan of darts
Sports.content:
Athletes who hate their sports: From a Premier League winner who doesn't watch football to an Ally Pally world champion that isn't a fan of darts

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

There are a number of pulls when it comes to a career in sport.

The chance to spend every day doing what you love, earning your living along the way. Or maybe the pursuit of glory, the drive to be the best at what you have dedicated your life to. How about the sometimes staggering prize money on offer, which can lead to the chance of fame and a lifestyle most can only dream of?

Few consider that, for some, it's not really a choice. It's what athletes know – what they have always done, so they will continue to do.

That seems to be the case for three-time darts world champion Michael van Gerwen, who this week spoke about how he's not a fan of darts and doesn't actually follow his sport.

And he's not alone. Some of the top names in tennis, football and more have expressed their dislike and distaste for the games that have given them so much.

Here, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at some of the world's top athletes who aren't actually too fond of the sport they have found success in.

Three-time darts world champion Michael van Gerwen revealed this week that he does not enjoy watching darts

Michael van Gerwen – Darts

Three-time world champion Michael van Gerwen has dropped down to world No 7 after the Matchplay, and his stocks have fallen significantly since his last world title in 2019.

The Dutchman has been speaking about his relationship with darts – the sport in which, perhaps for the first time in a decade, he is no longer the biggest star.

'I never did in my life,' he told Winmau of watching games. 'I don't even like watching darts.'

Luke v Luke (Littler and Humphries) has been the talk of the town for the last couple of years, while Littler has taken his game to a new dimension in recent months in becoming the first darts player to pick up £3million worth of earnings in two years.

Van Gerwen does make an effort to keep tabs on his rivals, but don't expect to see him in the crowd of any events he's not involved in any time soon, or listening to the likes of Wayne Mardle or Dan Dawson analysing the game on the tele.

But he doesn't totally hate the game. Just prefers to play it – which is fair enough, all things considered.

'Sometimes if a friend like Vincent (Van der Voort) used to play or things like that, or if Luke against Luke are playing maybe a final,' Van Gerwen continued on his viewing habits. 'I put on some live scores, but I'm not going to watch it at all.

'I'd rather play than watch. Simple as that. I always say the same, so it would be really weird to change my opinion.'

Ben White – Football

Arsenal defender Ben White has proven to be a bit of a diverse character in football in recent years. It all came to a head in November 2022, when he fell out with England assistant manager Steve Holland – supposedly over his attitude towards the game.

White is not a fan of watching football unless it's to analyse his own performances. Reports also emerged three years ago that White was not watching other analytical videos while with England.

'I watch myself for analytical reasons,' White recently claimed to The Overlap. 'I watch England, maybe, but I'm always busy doing something. I wouldn't just sit down and watch a game.

'I didn't ever watch football when I was younger. I still don't now.'

But, as is the case with Van Gerwen, it's not all hate with White. He just wants to be out there playing.

'I just loved the game,' he continued. 'I was always playing it, never watching.

'So I don't know too much about the older generations, but I know (Patrick) Vieira was a very good player. But I don't know the details.'

Ben White (right) has become known for his dislike of watching football

Serena Williams – Tennis

Serena Williams is perhaps the most famous name in women's tennis history, and one of the most dominant too.

'I don't love tennis today, but I'm here, and I can't live without it,' she told TennisNow in 2012. 'So I'm still here and I don't want to go anywhere any time soon.'

That's despite winning seven Australian Opens, seven Wimbledon titles, six US Opens and three French Opens. But it's not just tennis – it's sport on the whole.

'It's not that I've fallen out of love, I've actually never liked sports, and I never understood how I became an athlete,' she continued. 'I don't like working out, I don't like anything that has to do with working physically.'

Not too much of an issue, though, it seems...

Serena Williams revealed in 2012 that she doesn't love tennis - or sport on the whole

Nick Kyrgios – Tennis

Tennis bad boy Nick Kyrgios has had a bit of a love-hate relationship with his sport.

The Australian, who is planning retirement at the age of 31, reached his first Grand Slam final in 2022 at Wimbledon. He would lose to Novak Djokovic, but has also regularly made headlines for his actions away from the actual tennis, such as his shouting during matches.

One wonders if his relationship with tennis is related to that. He said in 2015: 'I don't really like the sport of tennis that much. I don't love it.'

He does, though, have love for a different sport.

'It was crazy when I was 14,' he continued. 'I was all for basketball and I made the decision to play tennis. I got pushed by my parents and to this day I can still say I don't love the sport. It is just crazy how things go.

'It's good when you're out there on a tennis court. There's nowhere to hide. It's all you, tactically, physically, mentally. But I just love basketball, I love the sport. I always have. I try when I'm on the road with tennis not to watch too many basketball videos and stuff like that, to keep me focused, but it's tough.'

What could have been.

Nick Kygrios has a love-hate relationship with the sport - and would rather have been a basketball player

Mark Williams – Snooker

Things seem to be going a little better for Mark Williams since his comments in 2019, when he became one of the few athletes to actively say they 'hate' their sport.

Currently World No 8 and a 2025 World Championship finalist, the Welshman was going through a tough patch back in 2019 when he had just beaten Fraser Patrick 6-2 in the first round of the UK Snooker Championship.

Despite actually being ranked No 3 in the world, Williams had failed to win a ranking event all year. He lashed out at snooker, and, like Kyrgios, his mind was elsewhere.

'I really struggled but somehow he struggled more than me and made it easy for me on a couple of frames,' Williams said. 'It's going all right, I'm enjoying myself when I'm on the golf course.'

When questioned on snooker, he added: 'Hate it. I'm just enjoying playing golf more.'

He had also talked about retirement in 2017, before going on to become world champion for a third time a year later.

Maybe he feels differently now.

Mark Williams admitted to 'hating' snooker in 2019 after teasing retirement a few years earlier

Tyson Fury – Boxing

Potentially the biggest name in modern boxing doesn't actually like boxing.

Tyson Fury has retired and un-retired countless times, but attributes his many returns to an addiction that helps him deal with his mental health struggles.

'I've tried to walk away many times and been unsuccessful,' he told DAZN in 2024. 'I meant it when I retired after Dillian Whyte back in 2022, I really meant that wholeheartedly. I could have put my hand on the Bible and meant it, but it was difficult to let it go.

'I've been in love with boxing from a little boy. It's been a love-hate relationship. When it's good, it's very good and when it's bad, it's very toxic. Now I am a fully grown adult with a family of my own.

'I wanted to walk away a lot of times but it always drags me back. Boxing is an addiction. It abuses my body, my mind, my soul. But I feel like it takes me to ecstasy. The rush is unbelievable. It gives me the biggest highs ever, but it also gives me the lowest lows. Boxing is more addictive than any drug ever. Ever. You can't let it go.'

It only takes a quick viewing of his reality show to see how much his family have begged him to pack it in. It seems, though, their words aren't enough.

Fury is set to take on Anthony Joshua in an all-British mega-fight later this year, having eased past Mariusz Wach last weekend. After that, he may well retire again – but will seemingly always keep on coming back.

Tyson Fury has tried to retire from boxing a number of times but finds himself returning

Benoit Assou-Ekotto – Football

A pattern emerges in the list of players who don't like their sport. They engage with it in some form all the time – every decision is based on their career, they have to analyse everything about it, and they spend most of their time performing it.

'I play it enough, don't I?' former Tottenham full back Benoit Assou-Ekotto once argued in an interview with Sky Sports.

'I don't watch football. I don't talk about football away from the game either. I suppose that is unusual. My interests are my friends and music, especially hip-hop. I like Ice Cube and 50 Cent.'

Assou-Ekotto played more than 200 times for Spurs, and didn't do too much wrong. Perhaps his argument proves you don't have to be totally obsessed with what you are doing to reach the top level – or maybe it suggests he could have gone higher if he was.

Former Tottenham defender Benoit Assou-Ekotto (right) is another sports star who does not enjoy watching their sport

Andre Agassi wrote in his autobiography that he 'hates' tennis despite his widespread success

Andre Agassi – Tennis

We have saved the most brutal for last – eight-time Grand Slam tennis champion Andre Agassi hates tennis.

'I play tennis for a living even though I hate tennis,' he wrote in his autobiography. 'I hate it with a dark and secret passion and always have.'

Tell us what you really think, Andre.

It's unclear exactly why the American feels that way, but it could be something to do with top players being on tour for more than 30 weeks a year, having tennis dominate their lives, and the stress involved.

Agassi won all there was to win. Others on this list have too. Still – it is not always enough. Showing that, sometimes, being a sports star may not be all it can seem to be.

Sports.title: Man United icon Casemiro's Inter Miami career off to embarrassing start after nightmare home debut
Sports.content:
Man United icon Casemiro's Inter Miami career off to embarrassing start after nightmare home debut

Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro endured a nightmare home debut for Inter Miami

View 2 Images Former Man Utd midfielder Casemiro had a debut to forget for Inter Miami. (Image: (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images))

Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro had a home debut to forget new club Inter Miami. The Brazilian scored an own goal in the 34th minute as Inter Miami drew with the Columbus Crew.

‌



The 34 year-old played a wayward pass to the opposition, diverting the ball past his own keeper as he tried to make amends by intercepting a cross. His blunder drew the Columbus Crew level after Luis Suarez's opener in the 16th minute.

‌



Casemiro was visibly frustrated by his mistake, but Inter Miami regained the advantage before the break. Noah Allen found the net in the fifth minute of first-half added time to put the home side back in front.

‌



Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Brais Mendez scored in the 84th minute to ensure a share of the spoils with a late equaliser. Despite his blunder, Casemiro played the full 90 minutes for the second consecutive match.

His first start delivered a 1-0 victory over Montreal that was marred by a serious injury sustained by his new team-mate German Berterame.

‌



The former Real Madrid star departed Manchester United at the end of the campaign, when his contract expired. The Brazil international enjoyed an impressive final season with United but revealed his intentions to move on at the start of the year.

The experienced midfielder represented his country at the World Cup before his new club was announced following Brazil's last-16 elimination. Casemiro penned a one-year contract, with an option to prolong his stint until 2029.

View 2 Images Casemiro scored an own goal in Inter Miami's draw with Columbus Crew. (Image: (Photo by Leonardo Fernandez/Getty Images))

‌



Speaking earlier in the week, Casemiro disclosed he'd fantasised about lining up alongside MLS sensation Lionel Messi. The World Cup runner-up entered the fray from the substitutes' bench against Columbus to realise his former adversary's ambition.

"The amount of trouble Messi gave me. of course, I dreamed of playing with him," Casemiro said. "I always wanted to play with the best. I could never stop him, I always needed the help of my teammates.

"I am very happy to be alongside him now and I want to continue winning titles with him. I want to enjoy being alongside him, help him and make him even greater. He is one of the gods of football, if not the God of football himself, and I want to help."

‌



Casemiro's switch has arrived with its own share of controversy, though. The MLS confirmed they were examining his transfer after Inter Miami struck an agreement with LA Galaxy for the rights to secure his signature.

"The league is gathering all relevant information and will refrain from further comment until the review is complete," the MLS said.

"While Inter Miami CF and the LA Galaxy have reached a settlement for the discovery priority [first rights] to sign Casemiro, the terms will be released upon conclusion of the tampering investigation."
