Sports.title: Josh Kerr jokes 'pressure is for tyres' as he celebrates Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow
Sports.content:
Josh Kerr jokes 'pressure is for tyres' as he celebrates Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow

The world record holder relaxed after he won the One Mile race in three minutes 54.12 seconds, ahead of rising Australian star Cameron Myers, who took silver, while Kenya’s Timothy Cheruiyot won bronze

View 3 Images Josh Kerr with his Commonwealth Gold one mile medal (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Josh Kerr joked that 'pressure is for tyres' today as he celebrated a turbo-charged Commonwealth gold in front of his home crowd in Glasgow.

‌



The world record holder won the One Mile race in three minutes 54.12 seconds, ahead of rising Australian star Cameron Myers, who took silver, while Kenya’s Timothy Cheruiyot won bronze. The field also included fellow Scot Jake Wightman, who finished fifth.

‌



Kerr, 28, explained that he trained in the stadium as a teenager, learning how to 'win and lose'. Kerr joked that he did not feel the pressure after his world record mile two weeks ago adding: "Pressure is for tyres."

‌



View 3 Images Josh Kerr wins Commonwealth Gold in front of his home crowd (Image: Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

On being named as 'King of Scotland,' he added: "Stop it. It was incredible, the fans packed the stadium and I knew that I had to seize the moment. I learned my craft there in Scotstoun stadium, it is where I learned how to win and lose. Winning in front of the home crowd was just incredibly special."

He thanked his childhood coach and said: "I am very, very proud to be an Eric Fisher athlete." Kerr said that he hoped to set an example for young athletes. Eric, who is still coaching in Glasgow, said he was very proud to guide both Kerr and Wightman when they were teenagers.

‌



A raucous home crowd roared with delight as Kerr took the lead in the final lap and crossed the finish line comfortably ahead of his rivals. The First Minister presented the athletes with their medals at a ceremony later in the evening.

View 3 Images Josh Kerr after his Commonwealth Gold (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Mr Swinney described Scotland’s performance in the Games as “truly historic and inspiring”. He said: “We’ve enjoyed some truly historic performances from Team Scotland at the Commonwealth Games – in swimming, bowls, athletics to name a few.

‌



“I hope that the Glasgow Games will encourage future generations to continue and build on this legacy of sporting greatness.”

The 11-day sporting extravaganza will end with tonight's closing ceremony at the Ovo Hydro. The slimmed down version of the Commonwealth Games has saved the British taxpayer around £600m - and may have secured the future of the event.

The total public funding allocated to stage the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games was £778 million. Birmingham City Council and local partners contributed £184m (25%) of that total.

Article continues below

The remaining 75% (£594m) was covered by the UK central government. Organisers of Glasgow 2026 say that using hotels instead of a village, along with smaller arenas and fewer events, cut costs to around £160m. Victoria in Australia was due to host the event and paid £199m to pull out which has funded Glasgow 2026 without taxpayers paying a penny.

Phil Batty, the chief executive of Glasgow 2026, said: “This definitely isn’t the last hurrah for the Commonwealth Games. What we’ve seen is a wholesale shift in what the Commonwealth Games needs to do to sustain itself, not just through 2030, but through 2034, 2038 and beyond."

Sports.title: Boxer Lee Reeves rushed to hospital after KO loss to Gary Cully as Frank Warren issues statement
Sports.content:
Boxer Lee Reeves rushed to hospital after KO loss to Gary Cully as Frank Warren issues statement

Lee Reeves had to be taken to hospital in Dublin on Saturday night as Gary Cully knocked him out to claim the BUI Celtic super-lightweight title

View 3 Images Gary Culley (left) after knocking down Lee Reeves (Image: Damien Eagers/PA Wire)

Irish boxer Lee Reeves was rushed to hospital after being knocked out by compatriot Gary Cully. The pair were fighting for the BUI Celtic super-lightweight title on the Mark Chamberlain vs Pierce O'Leary undercard.

‌



Dublin's 3Arena played host to Queensberry Promotions' No Turning Back on Saturday evening, with the main event resulting in Chamberlain snatching the IBO super-lightweight world championship from opponent O'Leary.

‌



But those who arrived for the undercard witnessed Reeves and Cully contest a breathless battle. Reeves, the clear underdog, applied pressure early on and heading into the later rounds, appeared to be on top.

‌



However, in the tenth, with both fighters tiring, he walked onto a heavy left hand from Cully and was immediately knocked unconscious. He received medical attention on the canvas and was transported directly to a local Dublin hospital for precautionary care and treatment. Promoter Frank Warren released a statement after the fight.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Anthony Joshua told exactly how he can beat Tyson Fury READ MORE :

"All our thoughts and prayers are with Lee Reeves and his family at this time as he remains in hospital," Queensberry promoter Warren wrote on social media after the event.

‌



"Everyone at Queensberry is thinking of him and we're in constant contact with his team regarding his condition as we hope for positive news."

View 3 Images Gary Culley celebrates his win (Image: Damien Eagers/PA Wire)

Cully, who captured the title, had to witness his opponent receive oxygen in the ring before being stretchered out of the arena. He, too, relayed some well wishes.

‌



"My prayers and thoughts are with Lee Reeves. Hopefully he's okay," said Cully. "He came in there as a big underdog after fighting relatively at a lower level up until now, but he really showed that he can operate at a higher level. Huge credit to him."

He acknowledged he was forced to the brink during the clash, in which he had a point deducted in the fifth round after his gumshield came out for a fifth occasion. He said: "It doesn't come into your mind when you're in there because I'm a fighter, I've always been a fighter and that's just what I do but I did have to dig deep in there.

View 3 Images Warren issued a statement (Image: Getty)

‌



"I really had to think in there and that shot that came in the tenth round was a well-timed shot. I had to stay switched on and stay concentrated. The keyword for this camp was concentration."

This bout marked Cully's second fight at super-lightweight following his move up from 135 lbs. He admits he feels much better competing at this higher weight class.

"It just brings a lot more enjoyment to my boxing, it makes me work a lot harder and I think it's shown in my last two fights," he added. "I had to dig deep in there tonight. If I had to go to the well at 135 in there, I don't know if I would have had it in me. I've found a new lease of life at this weight and now I'm ready to push on."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed

Gianni Infantino has come under waves of criticism for a controversial World Cup as well as FIFA plans to sell commercial stakes in their premier footballing competitions

View Image Gianni Infantino has been criticised this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino looked to bag a staggering £22.2million salary through FIFA's proposed Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, only for the proposal to spark widespread fury. UEFA and the FA condemned plans for the organisation to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, with member associations vowing to boycott the tournament altogether.

‌



As per the Times, Infantino could have made tens of millions of pounds through the scheme, which has since been canned following backlash. Meanwhile, UEFA claim that they have lost confidence in the FIFA president as a result.

‌



A statement from the European football governing body read: "We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

‌



Gianni Infantino is so delusional he does not know his time is well and truly up READ MORE :

“It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental.

"No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence, but also that of many other members of the football family."

The English FA also supported UEFA's stance, with a spokesperson for the organisation adding: " We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart."

‌



CONCACAF, meanwhile, are in favour of a " comprehensive reckoning" of Infantino's presidency, adding in their own statement: " It is a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first. This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour."

Sports.title: Arsenal put FIVE title-winners up for sale as Man Utd ‘investigate’ transfer deal
Sports.content:
Arsenal put FIVE title-winners up for sale as Man Utd ‘investigate’ transfer deal

Both Manchester United and Arsenal have been active in the transfer market this summer and the two Premier League rivals could potentially do business together before the end of the window

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is keen on more business this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United are mulling over a move for Myles Lewis-Skelly, with Arsenal open to offers for a number of stars. The Red Devils are keen to add to their fullback options before next month’s deadline.

‌



Newcastle’s Lewis Hall has emerged as a prime target for Michael Carrick but a deal could be difficult. The Magpies have already lost Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer, while Bruno Guimaraes appears to be on the verge of a move to Arsenal.

‌



That might make a move for Hall considerably more expensive, which has forced United to look at potential alternatives. According to The Independent, Arsenal academy graduate Lewis-Skelly is one of the options being considered.

‌



It is being reported that the Red Devils have a long-standing interest in the 19-year-old and are investigating whether a deal is possible this summer. There was a ‘possibility’ of a move last term, with the defender out of favour but he managed to re-establish himself in the first team towards the end of the campaign.

Mikel Arteta directly pressed on Vinicius Jr before ending Arsenal press conference suddenly READ MORE :

As it stands, Lewis-Skelly is one that Arsenal would want to keep but that situation could change should they complete mega-money deals for Vinicius Jr and Guimaraes.

There are however a number of other players that the North London side would prefer to let go in an attempt to balance the books. It is suggested that Arsenal will listen to offers for Reiss Nelson, Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli and Viktor Gyokeres, while midfielder Christian Norgaard looks set for a move to Everton.

‌



On Arsenal’s business for the next month, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said: “Well, we are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear. We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else.

View 2 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly is of interest to Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

“And you can just see it. The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing, we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do.”

Article continues below

He added: “Because the margins are very small. And because we want to get better and the level is going to increase, we need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don't have in the team, to have bigger margins. And that's the way we have to think.”

Arsenal have already made three signings this summer, with Christos Tzolis and Ilian Meslier having arrived, while Piero Hincapie has been signed permanently. When it comes to the Red Devils, they have also completed three deals for Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow.

Sports.title: Oscar Pistorius' new life out of prison – Back in sport, job secured, living in mansion
Sports.content:
Oscar Pistorius' new life out of prison – Back in sport, job secured, living in mansion

Oscar Pistorius was released from prison in 2024, having been convicted of murdering his girlfriend, Reeva Steenkamp, 13 years ago

View 2 Images Oscar Pistorius was convicted of murder in 2015 (Image: Charlie Shoemaker, Getty Images)

Oscar Pistorius has returned to the world of sport after his release from prison. The South African Paralympic champion was found guilty of murdering his girlfriend, Reeva Steenkamp, 13 years ago, after an appeals court overturned an initial verdict of manslaughter.

‌



Upon his release from prison in 2024, Pistorius has since built a new life away from the public eye. While he was banned from competing in the Commonwealth Games as a result of his conviction, it appears as though the six-time Paralympic gold medallist has since turned his focus to other sports.

‌



As per the Daily Mail, the 39-year-old plays padel at his local court, and has also entered Ironmen events under an alias. It is said that Pistorius came 55th in a 70-mile cycling event in Durban last year.

‌



Oscar Pistorious' new lover is double of tragic Reeva Steenkamp he shot dead READ MORE :

Meanwhile, in the 'physically challenged' category, the double leg amputee came third. Beyond his sporting pursuits, the report states that Pistorius has secured employment with a sound engineering firm.

He remains living in a mansion named Bateleur, alongside his uncle, Arnold, amongst the wealthiest individuals in the area.

Arnold brought up Pistorius from the age of 15.

‌



The property is reported to feature a swimming pool and a gym enabling the former Paralympian to maintain his fitness.

Speaking to the Daily Mail, one resident said: "We don't want to know about him around here.

"He's like a ghost. He's disappeared off the face of the earth and most people are happy for it to stay like that.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's ill-fated scheming does not mean a 64-team World Cup should be written off
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's ill-fated scheming does not mean a 64-team World Cup should be written off

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is somehow still clinging to his job but a consultation process is still taking place over the possible expansion of the World Cup in 2030

View 4 Images Cape Verde and their goalkeeper Vozinha captured the imagination of football fans around the world (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The news - the predictable news - that FIFA has already begun a consultation process ahead of making a decision about expanding the World Cup to include 64 teams was met not only with widespread incredulity but with utter cynicism.

‌



And there was one of the many fundamental problems with Gianni Infantino’s heinous, thankfully ill-fated scheme to sell off a chunk of the World Cup to billionaire cronies.

‌



It meant everything suggested by FIFA will feel rotten. This expansion idea was immediately seen, certainly in Europe, as just another ruse to make more money for FIFA and for the private investors that Infantino wanted to ingratiate himself with - and make fortunes from. No-one could have been blamed for looking at it from that point of view.

‌



UEFA declare loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino in bombshell new statement READ MORE :

The secret of comedy is timing, but there was nothing funny about FIFA saying they are, essentially, rushing through their consultation period - a decision will be made as soon as August 14 - just a couple of days after Infantino’s plot to raise $20billion by auctioning off rights packages to the World Cup was revealed. Bigger World Cup, more money for those private investor mates that, mercifully, will now not be directly involved in the tournament.

No wonder the news that the prospect of a 64-team World Cup is being accelerated by FIFA fat-cats was met with almost complete scorn. That is where power-crazed, money-obsessed Infantino has taken FIFA.

Yet would a 64-team World Cup be that bad? If the extra revenue was not going to private investors - and that prospect has been summarily headed off by UEFA’s threat of a boycott - would a 64-team World Cup be one of FIFA’s worst offences? No.

‌



View 4 Images Curacao were another small nation to make their mark on World Cup 2026 (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Hands up, I was against the tournament being expanded to 48 from 32 teams but was soon converted once Cape Verde started doing their stuff. I was converted when Curacao equalised against Germany, even though they were hammered 7-1.

I was converted by the entertainment provided by the group stages. I was converted by the joy of every nation’s set of fans.

‌



The only downside I could find was that the third games in the group stages were open to contrivance. That is because whittling 48 teams down to 32 for the knockout stages involves having eight third-placed finishers as qualifiers.

As it happened, there was no evidence of contrivance, but quite simply, 64 into 32 goes better. Sixteen groups of four, top two in each group qualify. Easy.

View 4 Images Gianni Infantino is under increasing pressure to stand down as FIFA president (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

‌



The next World Cup in 2030 - the centenary edition - is being staged in Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay hosting opening-round matches. There will be enough venues to accommodate 64 teams.

As UEFA and its president Aleksander Ceferin are now at permanent odds with FIFA and Infantino, they might not like the idea of an expansion to 64 teams. They will probably oppose it.

Yet the Euros is a 24-team competition, meaning 43.63 per cent of its member nations qualify for the finals. A 64-team World Cup would mean 30.34 per cent of FIFA member nations would qualify.

‌



View 4 Images Spain lifted the World Cup trophy at the end of a 48-team tournament that was widely deemed a success (Image: David Ramos/Getty Images)

Those of us who were originally in the camp that thought the World Cup should be for the elite only have long lost the argument. It turns out it was not a bad one to lose. Did you begrudge any of the teams at the 2026 World Cup their time in the sun?

And now it is a 48-team tournament - there will be no consultation process about any possible reduction in competitors - what is an extra 16 teams between friends? Italy might even qualify.

Article continues below

Understandably, an expansion would be negatively linked with Infantino’s scheming. But he will be long gone by then, surely. And the 64 teams who compete at the 2030 World Cup can enjoy themselves, untainted by his presidency and private ownership.

Sports.title: Liverpool have been given green light for 'dream' Bradley Barcola alternative
Sports.content:
Liverpool have been given green light for 'dream' Bradley Barcola alternative

Liverpool are in the market for a Mohamed Salah replacement for the new Premier League season

View 2 Images Liverpool want to sign Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty)

Liverpool are stepping up their efforts to sign Bradley Barcola from PSG. But there are other potential options out there if a move fails to materialise, notably AFC Bournemouth's Brazilian sensation, Rayan.

‌



The Reds are preparing an opening bid for Barcola, who is understood to be keen on a move to Anfield. However, the Frenchman's price tag could prove a sticking point.

‌



Barcola is valued by the Ligue 1 champions at £145million. Not only would that represent a Premier League record transfer, it is also some way above the £100m mark that Liverpool chiefs would prefer to do business at.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Should the winger's price prove insurmountable in negotiations, the Reds could turn their attention to Rayan instead. The 19-year-old has been linked with a host of clubs, including the Liverpool, after impressing for Bournemouth following his January move to the south coast.

‌



Indeed, talkSPORT reports that the Bournemouth star is considered a 'dream' target for the Reds. However, the teenager's release clause of £85m will not kick in until 2027, meaning that Andoni Iraola may need to fork out more for his signature in the short term.

One person who is very aware of Rayan's abilities is Cherries midfielder, Marcus Tavernier. The 27-year-old showered his team-mate with praise following Bournemouth's 3-0 win over Crystal Palace in May, even going so far as to predict that his stay at the Vitality Stadium would be short lived given his exceptional talents.

View 2 Images Rayan could prove a good alternative to Barcola (Image: Getty)

‌



He told Sky Sports: "Rayan and Kroupi? It’s been unbelievable, they are two world-class talents. I don’t think they will be at Bournemouth for a long period of time give the quality they have got.

"It’s brilliant to have them on the pitch. As a team we give the young players the confidence to go out and play with freedom."

Barcola is evidently still Liverpool's main target, with the Reds expected to submit an offer imminently. But with the sums involved in securing a deal, there's no guarantee a move will happen - and that could lead Iraola to look elsewhere.

Article continues below

PSG argue that the France international is now a back-to-back Champions League winner and should be priced above the likes of Morgan Rogers - who went to Chelsea for £117m - and City's £116m move for Elliot Anderson.

It is understood that Barcola is not planning to sign a new deal in France and has just two years remaining on his current contract.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
