World.title: 'If India is so great, why settle in Dubai?' Raj Thackeray targets Vivek Oberoi, R Madhavan
World.content:
MNS chief

on Sunday launched a sharp attack on industrialists and public figures who praise Prime Minister

and the BJP government while choosing to live abroad, questioning their claims that India had improved significantly under the current administration. Speaking at the 20th anniversary rally of the Maharashtra Navnirman Vidyarthi Sena in Mumbai, Thackeray cited actors

and R Madhavan as examples and linked their decisions to what he described as growing frustration among the country's youth.

Claiming that the government had itself acknowledged in Parliament that entrepreneurs were leaving India, Thackeray argued that many of those who publicly endorse the government's narrative were unwilling to build their own lives in the country.

"Vivek Oberoi, who played Modi's role in the movie on Modi's life, lives in Dubai. R. Madhavan, who goes on about how everything became great during Modi's time and how the country changed, moves to Dubai with his family.

If you think Modi has made everything so great, then why are you settling abroad? These people will come here to work in government-sponsored films and then go back to Dubai," he said.

He added that the trend was not limited to actors, saying, "Industrialists are going abroad."

Thackeray said the migration of entrepreneurs and young professionals reflected a deeper crisis of confidence, arguing that Indian cities had failed to provide the quality of life that many young people expected.





"This government made a big fuss about 'Smart Cities.' Where are those Smart Cities? Not a single city here is proper. Today, kids are going abroad. Why? Because they don't feel like living here. The cities are ruined; there's no place to take children out. Abroad, there are excellent roads, fields, gardens, cleanliness, sports complexes, everything. Because of all this, these kids feel like going abroad and settling there.

And we feel nothing about it?" he said.

The MNS chief also weighed in on Prime Minister Modi's remarks condemning abusive language directed at him and his mother, saying he agreed that such language was unacceptable but accused the BJP of nurturing a culture of online abuse.

"The language used against him was indeed inappropriate. No one should use such language about anyone. It was wrong. But tell this to your people too.

Since 2012, the troll army that your party has nurtured trolls everyone, from Mahatma Gandhi, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, to Indira Gandhi, to all of us including me, in the filthiest ways. Today, if artists in Maharashtra take a stand against the government, they get trolled.

Tell your people about all this sometime. You reap what you sow," he said.

He continued, "The Prime Minister said wrong things were said about his mother. That was indeed wrong. Such things shouldn't happen. But tell your party people that others have mothers too. Tell the trolls you've nurtured. You say, 'The kids have been forgiven.' But who will apologize for what your people did? Those who ordered lathis on students, those who split students' heads open, who will they ever apologize?"

Addressing student activists, Thackeray argued that recent protests should not be viewed merely through the lens of the NEET examination controversy.

He said the unrest reflected wider concerns over unemployment, privatisation, poor infrastructure, corruption and the lack of opportunities.

"The protests that happened weren't just because of the NEET exam chaos. Go beyond that and think about what's simmering in the minds of the boys and girls, the young men and women," he said, warning that further public anger could erupt if those concerns remained unaddressed.

World.title: Students from around the world experience the Jain way of life in Rajasthan
World.content:
Participants in the Jain Summer Program pose for a group photograph at Jain Vishwa Bharati in Ladnun, Rajasthan, on July 29. Photo by Aman Dhage/The American Bazaar

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

(Aman

Dhage

contributed to the report.)

(By arrangement with

)

Nestled amid the arid plains of Rajasthan, about 230 miles west of Delhi, Ladnun is the kind of town many travelers might pass without a second glance. Its narrow streets, whitewashed temples, and unhurried pace stand in stark contrast to Indiaâs bustling metropolitan centers.This summer, however, the quiet town has become an unlikely destination for seekers of one of the worldâs oldest philosophies.For more than three centuries, Ladnun has been the spiritual home of the Terapanth order of Jainism, a reformist sect known for its disciplined monastic tradition and emphasis on nonviolence, self-restraint, and spiritual inquiry. Last month, those traditions welcomed an unusual group of visitors: nearly three dozen students, scholars, and faculty members from eight countries who are spending three weeks not merely studying Jainism, but living it.The immersive summer program, which began July 20 and concludes on Friday, is the result of a collaboration among Florida International University, California State University Long Beach, the Jain Education and Research Foundation (JERF), Jain Visva Bharati Institute, and southern California philanthropist Dr. Jasvant Modi, whose support made the initiative possible.Rather than treating Jainism as an academic subject confined to classrooms and textbooks, the organizers designed a program that allows participants to experience the philosophy through daily practice.Each morning began with meditation. Students attended lectures on Jain philosophy, Prakrit â the ancient language of many Jain scriptures â and the foundational principles of âAhimsaâ (nonviolence), âAnekantavadaâ (the multiplicity of viewpoints), and âAparigrahaâ (non-attachment to possessions). They also interacted with monks and nuns, observed their disciplined routines, and experienced a lifestyle centered on simplicity, compassion, and mindfulness.âIt has been a very eventful week, and it has been a tremendous experience,â said Anne Vallely, a professor at the University of Ottawa and one of the foremost scholars of Jainism in the Western world.Describing the demanding schedule, she added, âWe have our lessons from 9:00 in the morning, and they go really into 10 oâclock, 11:00 at night.âThe program reflects months of planning by scholars in India and the United States.Florida International University, home to the first endowed chairs in Jain Studies in the United States, worked closely with California State University Long Beach, to develop the curriculum. The Jain Education and Research Foundation helped coordinate the academic and logistical aspects of the initiative, while Jain Visva Bharati opened its sprawling campus and monastic community to the international participants.At the heart of the effort is a broader mission: introducing Jain philosophy to a global audience at a time when its central teachings of nonviolence, environmental sustainability, restraint, and respect for diverse perspectives have taken on renewed relevance.Much of that vision has been championed by physician, entrepreneur, and philanthropist Dr. Jasvant Modi, whose years of support for Jain education and higher learning have helped establish academic programs across the United States. Modi, who has contributed tens of millions of dollars to educational and religious causes in the United States, India, and globally, provided the principal financial support for this yearâs summer school.âI was born in India in the Jain faith, and those principles of Ahimsa, compassion, and respect for all living beings have guided my entire life as a physician,â the La CaÃ±ada, California,-based physician entrepreneur told The American Bazaar. ââ After my medical career, I realized philanthropy allows me to heal on a larger scale, not just one patient at a time. I contribute to Jain education because I believe Americaâs young students must be exposed to this ancient wisdom of tolerance, non-possessiveness, and plurality, which is so undervalued today. âThe program also coincided with another milestone.This year marks the 300th anniversary of the founding of the Terapanth order, giving participants an opportunity to witness commemorative events while learning about one of Jainismâs most influential traditions. Established in the 18th century by Acharya Bhikshu, the Terapanth order is distinguished by its centralized leadership and disciplined monastic structure. Its monks and nuns travel extensively to spread Jain teachings rather than remaining in permanent monasteries.Throughout the three weeks, students discovered that learning extended far beyond formal lectures.Meals became lessons in mindful eating. Silence became a form of reflection. Conversations with monks and nuns often continued long after scheduled sessions ended. Participants learned not only the philosophical foundations of Jainism but also how those principles shape everyday decisions, from food and consumption to conflict resolution and environmental responsibility.For many students, the immersive setting transformed abstract ideas into lived experience.âIâm surrounded by scholars and Iâve gotten to meet with sadhvis and sadhus, and itâs just been lovely,â said Carol Rodriguez, one of the participants, who holds a Ph.D. in Jain Studies from the University of Florida.The Cuban-born scholar earned her bachelorâs and masterâs degrees in Jain Studies from Florida International University in Miami, where she translated portions of the Lilavatisara, a 13th-century work by Jain monk Jinaratnasuri.The international composition of the group further enriched the discussions. Participants brought diverse academic backgrounds and cultural perspectives, creating conversations that reflected Jainismâs emphasis on dialogue and multiple viewpoints rather than absolute certainty.Organizers hope the program will serve as a model for future international collaborations in religious studies, philosophy, sustainability, and peace education.Unlike traditional study abroad programs, the Ladnun initiative invites participants to become temporary members of a living spiritual community, where learning occurs as much through observation and daily practice as through formal instruction.As the summer school concludes on July 7, participants will return to universities and communities around the world carrying more than lecture notes and academic credits. They will leave with firsthand experience of a philosophy that has quietly endured for millennia and memories of a small Rajasthan town where, for three weeks, Jainism was not simply studied, but lived.

World.title: 'That hurts us': CWG silver medalist Lovlina flags 'missing' Northeast on Glasgow restaurant's India map
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Commonwealth Games silver medallist and Assam boxer

said she felt 'hurt' after noticing that the Northeast was missing from a map printed on napkins and displayed outside a popular Indian restaurant in Glasgow.

The restaurant owners acknowledged the mistake and assured the Indian boxing contingent that it would be corrected.

The incident took place when the Indian boxing team visited Mister Singh's India, The Home of Curry for a celebratory dinner after securing a record 10 medals, seven gold and three silver, at the Commonwealth Games.

Lovlina noticed that the restaurant's branding showed an incomplete map of India without the Northeast.

She immediately raised the issue with the management.

Addressing the restaurant management during an interaction, Lovlina said the omission was upsetting.

"Please don't take this the wrong way. I felt a little hurt by this. In the map of India, our North East is missing. Yes, even outside, the map that's displayed has cut off the North East. As someone from the North East, that really hurts us. That's all I wanted to say.





Please keep this in mind next time. Thank you so much," she said.

Boxing Federation of India (BFI) president Ajay Singh, who was present at the restaurant, said there was no confrontation and that the issue was resolved amicably.

"There was no confrontation. It was an aberration and we pointed that out, me and Lovlina. They accepted their mistake and assured us that it will be corrected," Singh told PTI.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The restaurant is a popular Indian dining destination in Glasgow and has hosted several visiting sports teams and dignitaries over the years.

Lovlina won a silver medal in the women's 75kg boxing event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.

The Tokyo Olympic bronze medallist lost a closely fought final to Australia's Emma-Sue Greentree by a 4-1 split decision, missing out on her first Commonwealth Games gold medal.

The silver was Lovlina's maiden Commonwealth Games medal after earlier exits at Gold Coast 2018 and Birmingham 2022.

India's boxing team has produced its best-ever Commonwealth Games campaign, winning a record seven gold and three silver medals. Overall, India has collected 35 medals at the Glasgow Games: 11 gold, 16 silver and eight bronze to occupy fourth place in the medal standings.

World.title: Under-12 world champion Divi Bijesh among participants in 39th National Chess Championship
World.content:
Chess prodigy Divi Bijesh (FIDE rating 2006) of Kerala, who recently claimed the under-12 title at the FIDE World Cup 2026 in Georgia, is among the 600 players from across the country taking part in the 39th National Under-11 Open and Girls FIDE-rated Chess Championship, which began at the Urwa Indoor Stadium in Mangaluru on Sunday. The championship will end on Saturday.

The 11-year-old Ms. Bijesh is pitted against Aadhya Deo (FIDE rating 1471) of Tripura in the first round. Among the other top-ranked girls taking part in the championship are Yakshini P. (FIDE rating 1819), who was pitted against Anushka Manoj Kumar (FIDE rating 1471) of Telangana, and woman candidate Nakshatra Gumudavelly (FIDE rating 1816) of Karnataka, who was pitted against Yuktha R. (FIDE rating 1470) of Tamil Nadu.

Among the boys, 11-year-old FIDE Master (FM) Advik Amit Agrawal of Maharashtra (FIDE rating 2376) was pitted against 10-year-old Adithya Sreejith (FIDE rating 1532) of Kerala in the first round. Ten-year-old FM Sarbartho Mani (FIDE rating 2273) of West Bengal was pitted against 11-year-old Reyansh Kamerkar (FIDE rating 1532) of Maharashtra, while 11-year-old Nidhish Shyamal (FIDE rating 2219) of Telangana was pitted against 11-year-old Shawn Joy (FIDE rating 1531) of Karnataka.

In this classical chess championship, each game lasts about four hours. There are 11 rounds in the tournament. International arbiter (IA) V. Vijayaraghavan has been designated chief arbiter, while IA Ajesh Kumar A. and IA Prashant Raval have been designated deputy arbiters. Live matches on 30 boards each in the boys’ and girls’ sections can be watched every day on chessworld.ai.

At the inauguration of the programme, Dakshina Kannada Chess Association president Amarashree Amarnath Shetty said this was the first time Mangaluru was hosting a national-level chess tournament and only the second time Karnataka was hosting such an event.

Hoping for more national sporting events in Mangaluru involving national and international-level athletes, Dakshina Kannada Member of Parliament Capt. Brijesh Chowta called upon participants and their parents to move around the city. “This is the safest and cleanest city in the country. There are a lot of good things about this city. Please spread good words about Mangaluru,” he said.

Mangaluru Police Commissioner Sudheer Kumar Reddy said the best minds are taking part in the championship. The event provided an opportunity for players to make a mark at the highest level of chess. Mangaluru City South MLA D. Vedavyas Kamath also spoke. Additional Deputy Commissioner K. Raju attended the event.

The championship was inaugurated with grandmaster Thejkumar M.S. of Karnataka and Mr. Reddy making a few moves on the chessboard.

World.title: Kerala floods 2026: clean-up begins in Kottayam as rain fury leaves trail of destruction
World.content:
Even as rainfall intensity eased, the flood situation in Kottayam remained precarious on Sunday (August 2, 2026), with a steady inflow of water from the high ranges continuing to trouble low-lying areas in the western parts of the district.

As floodwaters began receding from several areas, residents in the worst-hit regions started the painstaking task of cleaning up. Houses along the upper reaches of the Meenachil river, which remained submerged after the river overflowed, were left covered in thick layers of mud and silt. Roads were inundated at several locations. Villages along the banks of Vembanad Lake were the worst affected.

While the eastern parts of the district saw water levels gradually fall, the trail of destruction left behind by the deluge continued to disrupt normal life in Erattupetta, Pala, Kanjirappally and Koottickal. Several houses have become uninhabitable after being filled with mud and debris.

District Collector Chetan Kumar Meena has declared a holiday for all educational institutions in the district, including professional colleges, on Monday in view of the continuing rain-related calamities. The holiday will also be applicable to anganwadis, tuition centres and special classes. However, examinations that were scheduled earlier will be conducted as planned, the Collector said.

Worst-affected

The sudden surge of water that swept through Erattupetta on Saturday caused extensive damage, with Karakkad, located along the banks of the Meenachil river, emerging as one of the worst-affected areas. Over 100 houses were inundated, several of them suffering structural damage. Power supply was disrupted after KSEB transformers and electric poles were damaged, while a well that served as a key source of drinking water for residents collapsed. The region also reported agricultural losses running into lakhs of rupees.

The floods also dealt a severe blow to traders in Erattupetta and Pala, where nearly 200 shops were inundated. Textile merchants who had stocked up ahead of Onam suffered losses running into lakhs of rupees. Cleaning operations are continuing in shops and houses, with residents saying the accumulation of mud was far heavier than in previous floods.

Students shifted

In Pala, waterlogging continued in areas such as Kottaramattom and Mutholy, with several low-lying roads remaining submerged. Students were shifted from an entrance coaching centre after floodwaters entered the premises.

Meanwhile, the mortal remains of Regina Johny and her son Josephin, who died in a landslip at Payyanithottam, were laid to rest at St Alphonsa Church on Sunday.

In Theekoy, Animal Husbandry and Dairy Development Minister Bindhu Krishna assured assistance to dairy farmer Anil Kumar, who lost 11 cows in the floods. After learning about the loss, the Minister contacted him over the phone and assured him of support. She said she would visit Theekoy on Monday to hand over replacement cattle to the farmer and assured that steps would be taken to ensure the speedy disbursal of compensation, including assistance for the loss of livestock.

Collector chairs meeting

A district-level Disaster Management Authority meeting chaired by the Collector on Sunday reviewed the prevailing situation and assessed the progress of relief and rehabilitation activities. Department heads briefed the meeting on the current situation and the response measures being undertaken. Though water levels have started receding in several areas, the district continues to remain above the alert threshold.

As of Sunday, 34 relief camps were functioning in Kottayam taluk, providing shelter to 419 people.

World.title: Kishan Reddy pushes for indigenous manufacturing in EV sector, self sufficiency in critical minerals
World.content:
Hyderabad

Union Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy, on Sunday, encouraged indigenous manufacturing in the Electric Vehicle and allied sectors, even as he underscored that India should become self-sufficient in critical minerals used by the industry.

Mr. Reddy was speaking at the unveiling of KETO Motors’ commercial bus, which he flagged off along with Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) Vice-Chairman and Managing Director Y. Nagi Reddy, in the presence of Venkatesh Challa, Director, KETO Motors Limited.

The Minister said the country faced a supply issue of these minerals after Operation Sindoor as China, from where they are imported, disrupted supplies for up to eight months. In order to achieve self sufficiency, the National Critical Mineral Mission was launched with an outlay of ₹34,000 crore.

“Critical minerals such as lithium, cobalt, nickel and copper, which will serve as the backbone for future sectors like electric vehicles, solar panels, semiconductors, defence and AI, hold strategic importance comparable to oil,” he said, and pointed out that the Government of India, along with other players, is acquiring mining blocks in countries where such minerals can be mined and processed for India.

He said there was complete support from the Union government for the electric vehicle sector. “Electric mobility is not merely an alternative to petrol and diesel vehicles. It is paving a strong path for the country’s energy security, pollution control, import reduction and technological self-reliance,” he said.

Touching upon KETO Motors’ developments, he said,“The success achieved by KETO Motors stands as a testament to indigenous capability. Let us hope that KETO Motors continues to contribute significantly to the nation’s economic growth and employment generation by developing eco-friendly transportation systems through advanced research in the future.

Mr. Nagi Reddy said that the only way to address traffic congestion caused largedly by the massive number of private vehicles was to improve public transport, including buses. Under the PM eDrive scheme, as many as 800 buses would join the TGSRTC fleet this December and another 1,400 buses the following December under the gross cost contract model. He added that in the coming years, very few Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) buses would remain.

World.title: Kerala floods 2026: Two taluks in Idukki record over 200 mm rainfall
World.content:
Two taluks in Idukki district witnessed over 200 mm of rainfall on Saturday, triggering a series of landslips and widespread damage across the region.

According to India Meteorological Department (IMD) data recorded from Friday morning to Saturday morning, Peerumade taluk recorded 213 mm of rainfall, while Thodupuzha taluk recorded 212.2 mm. The district received an average rainfall of 143 mm during the same period.

Climatologist Gopakumar Cholayil noted that both the taluks receiving over 200 mm of rain directly contributed to the landslips. “When over 100 mm of rainfall occurs in a single hour in a localised area, it can be considered a cloudburst. Both the taluks received extremely heavy rainfall, leading to massive damage. Based on private rain gauge data, the actual rainfall in these areas was very high,” he said.

At midnight

He further noted that in the recent landslips, extreme rainfall often hit during midnight while residents are in a deep sleep. “People often realise the actual impact of such extreme rainfall only after casualties occur,” he said.

Following the torrential downpours, the district had witnessed numerous landslides and mudslides.

A rain gauge on the Tyford Tea Estate recorded 384 mm of rainfall from Friday morning to Saturday morning. The estate is part of the Idukki Rain Monitoring project, an initiative by the Kanjirappally-based Swaruma Charitable Society.

Zachariah Njavallil, general secretary of the Swaruma Charitable Society said many tea and cardamom plantations have long-standing practices of tracking rainfall data. “Swaruma installed another rain gauge at Mukkulam in Kokkayar panchayat, which recorded 304 mm of heavy rainfall on Saturday morning. These recent extreme rainfall reports indicate the need for more localised rain gauges. We will install additional gauges across various parts of the district soon,” said Mr. Njavallil.

As many as 187 people, comprising 73 men, 81 women, and 33 children, have been shifted to 13 relief camps across the district.

The district, meanwhile, experienced lighter, moderate rainfall on Sunday, averaging 71.29 mm over the preceding 24 hours. Water levels in the Idukki reservoir rose to 2,340.40 ft (37.78% capacity) on Sunday, while the water level at the Mullaperiyar dam reached 116.70 ft. The water level in the Idukki dam has surged by more than 10 ft within two days. The spillway shutters of the Malankara, Kallarkutty, Pambla and Kallar dams remain open.

The District Collector Dineshan Cheruvatt has declared a holiday for all educational institutions, including Anganwadi, nurseries, schools, and colleges, in view of the heavy rainfall prediction in the district on Monday.

World.title: Friendship Day observed with tree conservation drive in Visakhapatnam
World.content:
Friendship Day was observed with a tree conservation initiative in Visakhapatnam on Sunday, as participants offered prayers at a big banyan tree estimated to be about 140 years old on Railway Station Road in Dondaparthy.

The programme was organised by the Green Climate Team, an NGO working for environmental protection and tree conservation in association with Vanamali, CTG, IIAM, ActionAid and Rotary Couples.

Green Climate Team founder-secretary J.V. Ratnam said the organisation would promote seed rakhis, organise Vriksha Bandhan programmes and encourage the planting and protection of palm groves.

Vanamali CTG administrator Malla Saritha urged people to conserve natural resources and forests. Referring to the Bishnoi community’s tradition of protecting trees, she said the practice highlighted the importance of safeguarding the environment.

IIAM professor Varalakshmi said students would participate in Vriksha Bandhan programmes to be held till August 28 to promote awareness on forest conservation and climate change.

Representatives of the participating organisations, volunteers and students took part in the programme.

World.title: Flood warnings withdrawn as Godavari recedes at Bhadrachalam
World.content:
The Godavari began receding at Bhadrachalam on Sunday, bringing relief to people in riverside villages in the Bhadrachalam Agency.

The water level fell to 42.1 feet by 7 p.m., below the first warning level of 43 feet, with around 8.94 cusecs being discharged downstream.

The river had remained above the third warning level of 53 feet until 11 p.m. on Saturday.

With inflows from the upper reaches declining, the third, second and first flood warnings were withdrawn within about 19 hours.

Vehicular traffic resumed on the Bhadrachalam-Charla highway as floodwaters receded from several stretches. People sheltered at flood relief centres in Dummugudem, Charla and Burgampadu mandals also began returning home.

World.title: ‘Excel Shankar’ film launched in Visakhapatnam
World.content:
The launch ceremony of “Excel Shankar,” the third production of BFF Productions, was held at the production office in Akkayyapalem in Visakhapatnam on Sunday (August 2, 2026). Former Deputy Mayor Dadi Satyanarayana inaugurated the office by cutting the ribbon and conveyed his best wishes to the cast and crew.

The programme began with traditional puja rituals. Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Satyanarayana said he hoped the Telugu film industry would establish a stronger presence in Visakhapatnam in the coming years, generating employment opportunities for artistes and technicians.

The film is directed by T.S. Rayudu, with B. Santosh Kumar associated with the screenplay, dialogues, lyrics and creative supervision. Actors Pooja, Babu Dev, Chandrasekhar, Samudram Venkatesh, Pillu Prasad, Satish Reddy, Tulasi, Sagar and others attended the launch programme.

World.title: Plantation corporation’s continued possession of over 3,900 ha of lease-expired forestland ‘unauthorised,’ Kerala Forest department tells CEC
World.content:
The Central Empowered Committee (CEC) constituted by the Supreme Court has sought a detailed response from the Kerala Forest department on allegations of the continued occupation and commercial use of more than 3,900 hectares of lease-expired Reserved Forest (RF) by the Plantation Corporation of Kerala Ltd. (PCK), including for pineapple cultivation by private parties.

During a hearing on July 20, 2026, on a petition filed by T.J. Krishnan, president of the Ecological Conservation Society, North Paravur, the Kerala Forest department apprised the CEC that the land concerned was “lease-expired RF lands” and that PCK’s continued possession of the land and plantation operations were “unauthorised.”

The petitioner alleged that the PCK continues to occupy and use large tracts of RF land despite the expiry of lease and that portions of it had been leased, subleased, licensed or otherwise allotted to private farmers for pineapple cultivation, adversely affecting wildlife habitats and elephant movement corridors.

The petition sought directions to examine the legality of the continued occupation of the lease-expired RF land, conduct an independent field inspection of the Kalady Group Plantations and adjoining elephant movement areas, investigate the reported allotment of land to private parties, and assess the ecological impact of pineapple cultivation, fencing and land-modification activities.

The society further urged restoration of damaged forest areas, removal of solar fences and other barriers restricting elephant movement, suspension of further pineapple cultivation and related land-development activities, and preparation of a scientifically informed habitat restoration and wildlife corridor management plan. The petitioner has also sought the cancellation of a government order dated April 2, 2025, which permits pineapple cultivation in the lease-expired RF land.

During the hearing, Deepak Mishra, Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (PCCF) (Forest Management), Kerala, clarified the Forest department’s position before the CEC.

As per the submissions recorded by the CEC, the Forest department stated that portions of the land had been leased, subleased, licensed or otherwise allotted to private parties for pineapple cultivation. It further submitted that pineapple cultivation, fencing and related activities had adversely affected wildlife movement, habitat connectivity, soil stability, water resources and the ecological integrity of the area.

The Forest department informed the committee that 3,902.80 ha. (9,644.02 acres) of forestland—3,666.43 ha. in Malayattoor-Idiyara RF and 236.37 ha. in Kodassery RF—had been leased to PCK for 50 years under various government orders issued between 1961 and 1966. A lease deed was executed between the Chief Conservator of Forests and the Managing Director of the PCK on July 9, 1971. The leased forestland falls under three forest divisions, comprising around 2,450 ha in Vazhachal, 1,211 ha in Malayattoor and 239 ha in Chalakudy.

After hearing the matter, the CEC directed the PCCF (Forest Management) to examine relevant records and submit a detailed response on the issues raised in the petition within two weeks.

Meanwhile, N. Badusha, president of the Wayanad Prakruthi Samrakshana Samiti, urged the State government to immediately take back the lease-expired forestland from the PCK. He alleged the PCK had violated the lease conditions by cultivating pineapple and other crops that attract elephants, thereby aggravating human-wildlife conflict. “Restoring the land as forest and removing fences to reopen elephant corridors should be prioritised to mitigate the conflict,” Mr. Badusha added.

World.title: Second phase of AJK polls conclude amid renewed rigging allegations by PPP
World.content:
The second phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections took place on Sunday, with polling held in eight out of the nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and all 12 refugee constituencies.

Polling began at 8am and continued till 5pm for the refugee seats, while the process concluded at 6pm in Muzaffarabad after an hour-long extension.

The electoral process in LA-27 (Muzaffarabad-I) was postponed due to heavy rain, AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal said, DawnNewsTV reported.

Over 300 candidates were in the fray for the Muzaffarabad seats and the 12 seats for refugees settled in different regions.

What has happened so far:

Polling postponed in LA-27 due to rain; 4 other seats up for grabs in Muzaffarabad district, 2 each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley

Voting held across country for 12 refugee seats — 7 in Punjab, other 5 divided between different provinces

Bilawal condemns ‘attack’ on party’s regional president, says PPP worker killed in LA-31

PML-N disputes PPP claim, says man died from heart failure

PPP alleges electoral malpractices at some polling stations in at least 11 constituencies

Continuing his rigging allegations, PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Sunday accused the PML-N of “robbing” votes in the second phase of the AJK elections as well.

In a post on X later in the day, he condemned an “attack” on the party’s regional president, Chaudhry Latif Akbar — also the candidate for LA-31 (Muzaffarabad-V).

Accusing “miscreant elements of the PML-N” of being behind the incident, Bilawal said PPP worker Mushtaq Shah was killed in the same constituency.

“The PML-N is robbing the votes of the people of Azad Kashmir through bullets, batons and coercion,” he alleged.

The PPP chairman demanded that those responsible for the attack on Akbar and the “murderers” of the party worker be arrested immediately.

In a separate statement, Bilawal said, “The PML-N has crossed all limits. Attacks are taking place on our voters and the president of the state (AJK).”

He remarked that in Muzaffarabad, the PPP’s “politics of dignity and principles was in contest with the PML-N’s threat, rigging and coercion”.

The PPP shared a complaint written to the Election Commission regarding a “physical assault” on Akbar.

The party said the LA-31 candidate was “engaged in the electoral process on polling day” when the alleged incident took place, accusing three individuals.

It said a first information report (FIR) was being registered and urged the Election Commission to order an inquiry into the “security lapse” that resulted in the incident.

AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, who belongs to the PPP, took notice of the incident and ordered the chief secretary and the police chief to take those responsible to justice.

The AJK PM termed the attack “a slap on the politics of dignity and principle in Kashmir”.

Akbar also wrote two letters to the Election Commission. In one, he alleged that an attempt on his life was made at Polling Station 177 “by PML-N workers” and wrote of the PPP worker’s death.

He further claimed that his polling agents were not allowed to “sit in the polling area” at 14 polling stations.

In the second letter, Akbar said PPP leader Syed Mumtaz Hussain Naqvi sustained bullet wounds in a “[murderous] attack” at a polling station in a building.

Addressing a press conference, PPP leader Nayyar Hussain Bokhari claimed that eight party workers had been injured in the ongoing elections so far.

Bokhari contended there was a “state of lawlessness” in AJK.

Polls in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with the first set of polls held in Mirpur division on July 27, the second held today, and the third phase set for August 10 across Poonch division.

Ahead of today’s elections, internet services were restored in parts of Muzaffarabad division after remaining suspended for 54 days on July 29. At the time, it was not clear whether the restoration covered the entire division or was limited to the state capital.

Addressing the media on Sunday, the AJK CEC said that a letter had been written yesterday to request the restoration of internet services.

He added that the outcome would be known today, without providing further details.

“We will work according to the law; we will not come under pressure from anyone,” CEC Mughal said to a question.

PML-N says man did not die from bullet, had heart failure

On its part, the PML-N disputed the PPP’s stance on a man’s death in Muzaffarabad, saying that he died due to heart failure and did not suffer any bullet injury.

Responding to the PPP’s stream of allegations in a media talk in Rawalpindi, PML-N Punjab Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb said a man aged between 68 and 70 years was trying to resolve a “scuffle” when he suffered heart failure.

She noted that there was a physical altercation between groups of the PML-N and the PPP, describing the incident as “unfortunate”. She further said that Shah’s family has refused to have a post-mortem examination conducted.

“Will you do politics on bullets? Will you sabotage a democratic process by spreading such fake claims?” Aurangzeb said.

She further said, “My brothers, this politics of bullet, this politics of robbing votes, this does not suit parties like us.”

The PML-N leader went on to emphasise that the PPP leadership had given sacrifices and spent their “entire lives” in making efforts to strengthen democracy.

She remarked that ex-prime minister Benazir Bhutto “did not give sacrifice to see this day”.

“You should remember that you are Zulfikar Ali Bhutto’s grandson. We will keep reminding you because we will not let their sacrifices go to waste.”

She further said that the PPP was aware that the public did not vote for it. “Are elections won by crying, grabbing collars, issuing threats or making accusations? Elections are won with courage.”

The PML-N leader also took exception to Bilawal’s remarks of “snatching away seats” and “taking out seats”, saying: “Bilawal, you say good things. What kind of statements are you making now?”

Aurangzeb compared the PPP’s attitude to that of the PTI, saying the former’s “narrative” should not be the same.

“Find out so that you may not have to cry in Sindh,” the PML-N leader cautioned the PPP, noting people in Sindh were seeking performance similar to that of the Punjab government.

Aurangzeb recalled the Charter of Democracy signed between the PPP and the PML-N in 2007, stressing that its purpose was not to let democratic processes be sabotaged.

Noting that the PPP was in power in AJK and had its administrative machinery in the region, the PML-N leader questioned if Bilawal’s “own government is carrying out rigging against you”.

She remarked that if one considered the PPP’s allegations to be true, the party would have to “accept” that its own government “carried out rigging against Bilawal”.

Aurangzeb said the PPP-led administration was preventing the transportation of the required electoral equipment.

She also commented on Bokhari showing ballot papers stamped with votes for PML-N, saying, “This is an election of thousands of votes. He was showing two stamps on two ballot papers.”

The Punjab minister took aim at the PPP’s governance, saying that it had nothing to show for its performance. She quipped that voters were yet to head to polling stations early in the morning while the PPP had already started holding media talks on rigging.

Aurangzeb said that if the PPP still had reservations, there were relevant platforms such as the Election Commission and tribunals to approach, rather than hold press conferences.

“Contest the elections. Do not cry out loud,” she said.

In a similar tone, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah also regretted the rigging allegations levelled by the PPP.

“Unfortunately, a democratic party, which is also a signatory to the Charter of Democracy, has been alleging rigging since 10:30 in the morning,” he said while addressing the media in Islamabad.

Flanked by Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam, Sanaullah claimed that the second phase of polls in AJK was conducted in a “peaceful manner”.

The inter-provincial coordination minister said the electoral process was completed at 96 per cent of polling stations, adding that vote counting was underway.

Sanaullah maintained that it was the “most transparent and non-violent electoral process”, adding that a few incidents had occurred during the day.

Referring to the alleged attack on PPP leader Akbar, Sanaullah said it was a dispute involving another family in the area and that there had been “no physical confrontation”, only a verbal argument.

Contesting the PPP’s claim about the second reported incident involving a party worker, the PML-N leader said a citizen named Mushtaq was involved in a scuffle with his family members, one of whom pushed him.

“He reportedly went home afterwards and then suffered a heart attack as he was a cardiac patient. They [PPP] claimed that shots were fired, but not a single bullet was fired,” the premier’s adviser asserted.

Sanaullah added that the PML-N condoled his death, but that the “deceased individual was not a PPP worker”.

PPP alleges electoral malpractices

On Sunday, the PPP alleged electoral malpractices shortly after polling commenced, with several of the complaints claiming its polling agents at some stations were not allowed to observe the voting process.

At 2pm, the party also wrote a separate letter to the Election Commission requesting follow-up on 25 complaints filed by it regarding 11 constituencies.

The PPP said it had not received any formal written response or acknowledgement from the electoral watchdog on the status of any of the 25 complaints.

“Given the gravity, number and geographical spread of the violations documented, the Party respectfully submits that a formal response from the Commission is now overdue and urgently required.”

On the other hand, the PML-N’s social media posts revolved around voters across Muzaffarabad and Punjab showing up to cast ballots with “enthusiasm”.

Several posts highlighted that a large number of voters were flocking to the PML-N’s election camps, rather than those of rival parties.

The PML-N also wrote to the Election Commission in response to a PPP complaint about LA-40 (Valley-I), terming the latter’s allegations against its candidate Muhammad Naeem Khan as “baseless”.

In the letter, seen by Dawn, the PML-N asserted that the allegations “regarding administrative failures are unsubstantiated and appear to be an attempt to create unnecessary controversy around the polling process”.

The PML-N urged the electoral watchdog to ensure that “no misleading or politically motivated complaint is allowed to undermine public confidence in the integrity of the polling”.

At a polling station in LA-32 (Muzaffarabad-VI), the PPP accused PML-N supporters of “ballot stuffing”. It further said that a government employee had been deployed as a polling agent for the PML-N at a separate polling station.

In LA-30 (Muzaffarabad-IV), the PPP claimed PML-N workers removed a ballot box at the Banaw Langah polling station and placed it outside, where they were allegedly “stamping ballot papers”.

In Charakhpora Union Council of LA-31 (Muzaffarabad-V), the PPP said “bogus voting” was taking place at the Sharik Kamal Bandi-Khalsa polling station.

The party said the alleged act “directly subverts the integrity of the poll”, adding that the polling station also did not have adequate security despite being declared “sensitive”.

The PPP also alleged a PML-N MPA at a polling station in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Abbottabad of obstructing the voting process for the refugee seat of LA-45 (Kashmir-VI).

In LA-25 (Neelum-I), the PPP said the voting process at a polling station had been halted after reports emerged of PML-N supporters tearing up ballot papers.

The PPP also said its polling agents at a polling station in LA-25’s Khawaja Sari reported that “fraudulent votes are being cast” there. It urged the Election Commission to dispatch officials and law enforcement to halt the alleged action.

‘Polling agents excluded’

The party alleged that its polling agents were not allowed to sit at polling stations for refugee seat LA-34 (Jammu-I) in Cantonment and Lahore’s Sheranwala Gate, calling on the Election Commission to intervene.

The PPP wrote to the electoral watchdog about a similar complaint emerging from a polling station in Janabad, Sargodha, for LA-34.

Sharing another letter addressed to the Election Commission about LA-34, the PPP said “elected members” of the PML-N were present inside a Pakpattan polling station and “stamping ballot papers”.

It further claimed that its polling agent was “barred from entering the same polling station”.

“The deliberate exclusion of the PPP’s oversight representative while PML-N’s own elected officials conduct fraud inside the station is not a coincidence — it is a coordinated strategy to commit electoral fraud without any independent witness,” it alleged.

The party urged the electoral watchdog to dispatch law enforcement to the polling station and remove the PML-N supporters allegedly involved in “ballot stuffing”.

Regarding LA-42 (Valley-III), the PPP filed a complaint over party candidate Asim Sharif Butt’s polling agent being “physically prevented” from entering a polling station in Muzaffargarh’s Alipur Tehsil.

The PPP also claimed its polling agents at three polling stations in LA-30 (Muzaffarabad-IV) were denied from observing the electoral process.

Similarly, the party said polling agents of candidate Ishfaq Zaffar were not permitted to take their seats at three polling stations in LA-32 (Muzaffarabad-VI).

Terming it a “serious violation” of the electoral code of conduct, the PPP sought disciplinary action against the presiding officers who allegedly refused the agents from discharging their duties.

At one of those polling stations, the PPP claimed a “violent confrontation” was underway between supporters of PML-N candidate Raja Farooq Haider and PPP supporters.

Other issues

In a separate statement in the morning, the party claimed that no polling staff was present at any of the 196 polling stations in LA-27, adding that this raised the concern that there was a “deliberate” attempt to delay the polling.

Similarly, the party alleged that polling staff had reached late at 71 polling stations of LA-28, due to which the voting process was facing delays. The PPP claimed that a similar situation was being witnessed at several polling stations of LA-30, where polling staff had not arrived on time.

Regarding LA-31, the PPP said it had written to the Election Commission on behalf of its candidate Akbar, urging it to take action over difficulties faced by voters due to the closure of the Rangla-Katkair Road in Muzaffarabad.

The party said over 50 vehicles carrying voters were stuck due to the road’s closure.

PML-N slams ‘blame game’

Earlier in the day, PML-N’s Muqam called on political parties not to indulge in a “blame game”.

“Nothing is to be gained from a blame game,” he said during a press conference in Islamabad, adding that law enforcement personnel were also deployed to ensure security.

“They should not act in a manner that ‘why was I not given seats’,” Muqam said, stressing that it was the public whose votes allocate seats.

The minister urged all political parties to let the electoral process take place in a peaceful manner, stressing that making allegations without evidence cannot change the results.

At the same time, Muqam also highlighted “arbitrary transfers and administrative decisions” in AJK, where the PPP is in power. He said the moves “seemed discriminatory”.

He recalled that the PML-N had accepted the results of elections in Gilgit-Baltistan held in June, where the PPP emerged the winner and formed the government.

Defending the results from Mirpur, Muqam asserted that the people voted for PML-N due to its performance.

On the other hand, PPP leader Nadeem Afzal Chan also held a press conference where he called on the Election Commission to play its role in “proving” the election process in AJK to be free and fair.

“Azad Kashmir is an international issue … people’s eyes are on it,” the former MNA said, adding that if the commission did not recognise the public and assure a free election, “tomorrow we will not be able to ratify this election under any circumstance”.

He recalled that after the Mirpur polls, there was a detailed discussion within the party about boycotting the second and third phases. However, the party leadership refused the idea of a boycott.

Chan cautioned that if the PPP was “compelled” to move towards such steps for the third phase, it would benefit those who wanted to prove the election “dirty”.

“I see this becoming an ultra Form-47 election,” he said.

He said that in negotiations in Muzaffarabad, the PPP had provided proof of rigging in four constituencies, as well as agreeing to hold re-polling in any other constituencies in which there were objections.

He also called for a benchmark for voting, saying, “General polling was less than 30 per cent. But wherever you won, it was 80pc, 90pc, 75pc … this doesn’t even happen in urban cities like Islamabad and Lahore.”

‘Admission of rigging’

The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the PML-N emerged in the lead during the first phase of polls. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging in Mirpur and demanded re-polling.

Scuffles, violence and allegations of rigging had marred the polls in Mirpur, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice.

To defuse the tensions, senior leaders of both parties met multiple times in Azad Kashmir over the weekend to “explore a legal resolution” to the dispute. The latest round of talks followed two earlier meetings on Thursday and Friday.

A PML-N source told Dawn that discussions focused on the PPP’s allegations and its demand for re-polling in certain constituencies. “It was not planned or pre-planned rigging but isolated acts at places where supporters of one candidate enjoyed numerical dominance over their opponents. Such incidents have unfortunately been part of the territory’s polling atmosphere and have also been witnessed in previous elections,” the source quoted the PML-N leaders as telling their counterparts.

Referring to this statement in a X post on Sunday, Bilawal said: “Despite this admission from the rigging party, the [EC] has still failed to take action on our complaints from phase 1. Had they done so, the credibility of today’s phase 2 election would have been restored.

“The PPP reserves the right to protest and demand re-election in phases where rigging took place, and the election commission failed to act. We have already sent multiple written complaints about ballot stuffing and illegal removal of our polling agents in today’s election. It is hoped the election commission acts swiftly and at least maintains fairness in round 2.”

According to the sources, during meetings with the PML-N, PPP initially raised objections to the results in four constituencies — Charhoi, Sehnsa and Nakyal in Kotli district, and Barnala in Bhimber district during phase-I of the election. However, it later withdrew its allegations regarding Sehnsa and Barnala.

Saturday’s discussions centred on Charhoi, where PPP AJK President Chaudhry Yasin lost to PML-N’s Raja Riasat, and Nakyal, where PPP candidate Javed Iqbal Budhanvi was defeated by PML-N’s Raja Ayaz Ahmed.

Meanwhile, the Sharif family also held discussions at Jati Umra. According to a statement issued by the PM’s Office, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif held consultations with his elder brother and PML-N chief Nawaz Sharif at Jati Umra to take stock of mounting political challenges, including the rift with the PPP over the AJK elections.

A senior PML-N leader told Dawn that the party leadership had taken serious note of the PPP chairman’s increasingly combative rhetoric against the Sharif family over the AJK polls and his warning that the PPP could reconsider its support for the federal government if the remaining phases of the elections were manipulated in favour of the PML-N.

Election numbers

According to the AJK Election Commission, 207 candidates are in the fray for the nine constituencies in Muzaffarabad division, comprising five seats in Muzaffarabad district and two each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley districts.

Another 137 candidates are contesting the 12 refugee constituencies, including six seats representing refugees from the Kashmir Valley and six from Jammu.

A total of 809,621 voters are registered in Muzaffarabad division, while the 12 refugee constituencies have a combined electorate of 438,834. According to the commission, 1,483 polling stations have been established across Muzaffarabad division, of which 533 have been declared highly sensitive, 741 sensitive and 209 normal. Another 1,057 polling stations have been set up for the 12 refugee constituencies.

Out of 12 refugee seats, seven seats are in Punjab, one seat is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, one seat (Jammu-VI) is divided between Pun­jab, Islamabad and KP, one seat is divided between Sindh and Balo­chistan (Valley-I), and one seat (Jammu-I) is shared among refugees living in Balochistan, Punjab and Sindh. Valley-V seat is divided between Punjab and Islamabad.

In Rawalpindi and Islamabad, about 27,000 registered male and female voters will elect lawmakers for LA-43 (Valley-IV), LA-44 (Valley-V), and LA-39 (Jammu-VI) seats. A total of 175 polling stations have been established, out of which 18 polling stations in Rawalpindi have been declared sensitive. A total of 34 candidates are in the fray.

In Gujrat, almost 2,000 policemen will perform security duties at scores of polling stations for the LA-38 elections. The total number of polling stations in these districts is 115, with 75 in Gujrat, 24 in Wazirabad and 16 in Mandi Bahauddin. The total number of voters is 50,225 in the entire constituency. As many as 11 candidates are contesting this seat.

In Sindh, officials said the elections will be conducted on LA-34 (Jammu-I) and LA-40 (Kashmir Valley-I) with polling stations established across Karachi and other districts of Sindh.

In LA-34 (Jammu-I), a total of 17 candidates are contesting the election, which has 698 registered voters in Karachi’s seven districts and 477 voters in 13 other districts of Sindh. For LA-40 Kashmir (Valley-I), 11 candidates are in the race. The constituency has 4,200 registered voters in Karachi and 403 voters in 17 other districts of Sindh.

In Balochistan, seven polling booths have been established across the province for the Kashmir Valley-I constituency, where 1,174 registered voters are expected to cast their ballots. Balochistan shares this seat with Sindh.

For the Jammu-I constituency, six polling booths have been set up, with a total of 182 registered voters, including 85 men and 97 women, eligible to vote. Polling stations have been established for AJK refugee voters residing in Balochistan at various locations, including Quetta, Pishin, Qila Saifullah, Hub, Loralai, Sibi, Mastung, Zhob and Barkhan.

In KP, 41 polling stations, mostly in Swat and Mansehra, have been set up for the LA-45 (Kashmir VI) seat.

Additional input by Ameer Hamza

World.title: At least 15 injured in explosion in Swat's Kabal tehsil
World.content:
At least 15 people were injured in an explosion in Swat district’s Kabal tehsil on Sunday, said the spokesperson for the area’s rescue service.

The nature of the explosion has not yet been ascertained. Security forces and rescue teams are at the site, while rescue operations are underway.

Rescue 1122 spokesperson Bilal Ahmed Faizi said more than 15 injured people had so far been shifted to different hospitals following the suspected explosion.

He added that relief and rescue activities were continuing, with further details to be shared later.

This is a developing story that is being updated as the situation evolves. Initial reports in the media can sometimes be inaccurate. We will strive to ensure timeliness and accuracy by relying on credible sources, such as concerned, qualified authorities and our staff reporters.

World.title: Security forces kill mastermind of Hangu police checkpost attack: sources
World.content:
Security forces have killed the mastermind behind the July 30 attack on a police checkpost in Hangu, which claimed the lives of nine police officials, a senior security official told Dawn on Sunday.

Security sources said the slain terrorist was identified as Amir Mauviya, and he was killed during an intelligence-based operation in Hangu’s Chapri Naryab.

According to the sources, the slain terrorist held an important position among Fitna-al-Khawarij in Kurram, and was wanted in several other terrorism cases.

Fitna-al-Khawarij is a term the state uses for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

The sources added that under Operation 11 Garaj, operations against terrorists had been intensified.

The attack on the Khazina Banda checkpost had claimed the lives of nine police personnel, including a deputy superintendent of police, and left 28 injured. Police officials said an exchange of fire had broken out after the terrorists attacked the checkpost, and 15 terrorists were killed in retaliatory action.

More recently, two police personnel sustained minor injuries in an improvised explosive device explosion targeting a police van near Pir Zakorhi Bridge near the Peshawar-Islamabad motorway toll plaza on Sunday.

On July 29, a policeman was martyred and four terrorists were killed during an operation in Swat’s Matta tehsil, police and security sources said.

It was merely five days after a terrorist attack on a joint police checkpost in KP’s Tank district martyred 15 people, including 14 security personnel.

Among those martyred were 12 soldiers, two policemen and a government official, the military’s media affairs wing said.

It added that the attackers attempted to breach the checkpost’s perimeter, but their attempts were “swiftly and decisively foiled” by security forces, who eliminated 12 terrorists.

Inter-Service Public Relations (ISPR) said the attackers then rammed an explosive-laden vehicle into the perimeter wall and infrastructure at the checkpost was seriously damaged by the impact of the resulting blast.

Security personnel and law enforcers have been coming under attack in KP, which continues to face terrorism.

According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS) monthly security assessment released on Saturday, Security personnel deaths in terrorism incidents in KP, excluding merged districts, increased from 12 in June to 38 in July and terrorist deaths from 37 to 108, reflecting a rise by 192pc. But civilian deaths fell from 26 to seven, a decline by 73pc. One peace committee member was also killed.

Security personnel deaths in merged districts rose from six to 11 and terrorist deaths fell from 72 to 55. Civilian deaths, meanwhile, rose by 86pc, increasing from seven to 13.

World.title: Electoral rolls shrink by 589,458 in less than two months as ECP removes 1.48m deceased voters
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s electoral rolls contracted by 589,458 voters between May 7 and July 2, 2026, as the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) removed a large number of deceased voters from the electoral database, more than offsetting fresh registrations during the period, it emerged on Sunday.

According to official ECP statistics analysed by Dawn, the total number of registered voters fell from 137,163,857 on May 7 to 136,574,399 on July 2.

A senior ECP official said 895,000 new voters were enrolled during the period, but the deletion of around 1.48 million deceased voters resulted in a net decline of 589,458 voters nationwide.

The number of male voters dropped from 73,286,821 to 72,835,859, a decrease of 450,962, while female voters declined from 63,877,036 to 63,738,540, down by 138,496.

The reduction narrowed the gender gap among registered voters from about 941,000 to 910,000. Overall, 99 of the country’s 144 districts recorded a decline in registered voters, while 45 districts posted a net increase.

Punjab

Punjab accounted for the overwhelming share of the decline. The province lost 478,909 voters, with the total falling from 77,955,543 to 77,476,634, representing 81.2 per cent of the nationwide reduction.

Nine of the 10 districts with the largest declines were in Punjab.

According to ECP figures, Faisalabad recorded the largest decrease, with 41,264 voter entries removed, bringing the district’s total down from 56,18,044 to 55,76,780.

It was followed by Sheikhupura, with a decline of 31,783 voters, from 22,68,275 to 22,36,492; Gujranwala, with a drop of 30,302 voters, from 29,79,820 to 29,49,518; and Sialkot, which lost 30,129 voters, bringing the number down from 29,84,882 to 29,54,753.

The number of voters in Gujrat dropped by 29,553, followed by Sargodha with a decline of 26,675, Multan with 26,420, Kasur with 24,367 and Bahawalpur with 22,259.

Likewise, Khanewal saw a decline of 19,504 voters, Rahim Yar Khan 18,574, Lahore 16,633, Narowal 15,914, Toba Tek Singh 15,395, Rawalpindi 13,577, Mandi Bahauddin 13,480 and Attock 11,180.

The number of voters in Nankana Sahib and Muzaffargarh declined by over 10,000 each. Another nine districts saw a decrease of over 5,000 each. These included Okara, which saw a decline of 9,784 voters; Khushab, 8,226; Chakwal, 7,377; Dera Ghazi Khan, 6,755; Wazirabad, 6,723; Rajanpur, 6,621; Kot Addu, 6,358; Lodhran, 6,348; and Chiniot, 5,396.

Sindh

Sindh recorded the second-largest provincial decline, losing 97,216 voters, with the total dropping from 28,772,963 to 28,675,747.

Karachi South recorded the largest decline in the province, with 20,243 fewer voters, making it the only non-Punjab district among the top 10 districts with the biggest declines.

The number of voters in the district fell from 13,30,682 to 13,10,439. It was followed by Karachi East, where the removal of 16,873 voters brought the total down from 18,15,780 to 17,98,907. Keamari lost 9,983 voters, Karachi West 8,394, Hyderabad 7,573, Khairpur 7,228 and Sanghar 6,240.

KP

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) recorded a comparatively small net decline of 9,046 voters, with the provincial total falling from 23,415,995 to 23,406,949. However, it was the only province where more districts recorded gains than losses.

In overall terms, the province lost 9,049 voters, accounting for 1.53 per cent of the total decline. While the number of male voters slipped by 16,884, the number of female voters increased by 7,838.

Haripur lost 4,978 votes, followed by Abbottabad with 4,182, Charsadda with 3,946, Kohat with 3,352, Nowshera with 3,313, Lower Dir with 3,153 and DI Khan with 2,895.

Other districts to have lost over 2,000 votes included Mardan, Hangu and Bannu.

Balochistan

In Balochistan, the number of voters declined by 2,226, accounting for a 0.38pc decrease. The total fell from 57,65,008 to 57,62,782, reducing the number of male voters by 6,518 while increasing the number of female voters by 4,292.

Loralai and Sibi saw declines of 1,048 and 1,025, respectively. Most districts recorded marginal changes, restricted to two or three digits.

Islamabad Capital Territory saw a small decline of 2,061 voters, from 12,54,348 to 12,52,287. Those removed from the electoral rolls comprised 1,118 men and 940 women.

Despite the overall decline, 45 districts recorded an increase in registered voters between May 7 and July 2. KP led the gains, with 20 of its 36 districts adding voters. Of Balochistan’s 36 districts, 13 saw an increase, while nine of Sindh’s 30 districts recorded a rise in voter numbers. In Punjab, only three of the province’s 41 districts witnessed an increase in the voter count.

In KP, the biggest increase was recorded in Peshawar, which added 4,835 voters, taking the total from 22,46,457 to 22,51,292. Other major gains in the province included Bajaur with 3,797, Lower Dir with 3,153, Buner with 1,738 and Mansehra with 1,603. Other districts with increases of over 1,000 included Malakand, Khyber and South Waziristan (Lower).

In Balochistan, Quetta remained ahead with an increase of 4,052 voters, followed by Pishin, which saw an addition of 2,523 voters. In 11 other districts, the increase ranged between 65 and 573.

Sindh also saw growth in nine districts. Karachi Central recorded the highest increase in the province, with 4,428 new voters, rising from 22,60,158 to 22,64,586. Jacobabad gained 3,928 voters, Ghotki 2,479, Naushahro Feroze 2,103 and Korangi 1,024. Other districts with nominal growth included Larkana, Malir, Tharparkar and Thatta.

In Punjab, only three districts saw gains, which were offset by much larger deletions elsewhere. The largest increase was recorded in Bahawalnagar, where the number of voters surged by 16,094, from 20,12,083 in May to 20,28,177 in July, followed by Sahiwal with 4,755 and Vehari with 1,089.

World.title: Bodies of Nepalese climber Nirmal Purja, 3 other mountaineers recovered on Broad Peak: Alpine Club
World.content:
GILGIT: The bodies of celebrated Nepali climber Nirmal Purja and three other mountaineers accompanying him on a summit of the Broad Peak mountain in Gilgit-Baltistan were recovered on Sunday — three days after all 10 members of the team were reported missing after an avalanche.

On Saturday, his expedition organising company Elite Exped announced that all members of the team, which also included Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, had died.

The bodies of three climbers were recovered by then, as well as the remains believed to be of a climber from the United States, Naila Kiani of the ACP told Dawn on Sunday.

Meanwhile, the ACP announced in a statement that Purja’s body had been found.

“The Alpine Club of Pakistan shares this update with profound sorrow. The ground rescue team has reached Nirmal Purja ‘Nims Dai’ at approximately 5,700m on Broad Peak, where three additional bodies have also been sighted, though their identities remain unconfirmed. The ground team will bring the bodies down to the Japanese camp.

“Recovery efforts continue under extremely difficult terrain conditions. This information reflects preliminary field reports and remains subject to further confirmation. We urge the public to await official updates before sharing unverified details,” the statement said.

In a subsequent post, the organisation said three other bodies, identified as China’s Wang Zhong and Nepal’s Nima Sherpa and Kili Pemba Sherpa, had also been recovered.

The “four identified climbers are currently being brought down to Camp 1 (C1) and downwards by the ground rescue team,” the post said.

It said ACP continued to monitor the ongoing recovery operation on Broad Peak, and rescuers had also “confirmed the presence of one additional body at a significantly higher elevation”.

However, “due to the extremely hazardous terrain and prevailing conditions, it is unlikely that a recovery attempt will be made at this stage,” it added.

Prior to the announcements, ACP General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that the ground rescue team was heading towards the advanced base camp on the mountain to carry out the operation. He said that the mountain’s terrain, risk of avalanches and steep slopes were posing challenges in the way of rescue efforts, adding that helicopters could not be employed due to weather conditions.

Later, the ACP said in a statement that an eight-member ground team, comprising climbers from Pakistan and Nepal, reached Camp 1 (C1) before 9am. “They will conduct a search and recovery mission on the slopes of Broad Peak under extremely difficult conditions,” the statement added.

Purja’s expedition team included 10 members, including him. Six of them were Nepalese while there was one each from Pakistan, Oman, the US and China.

The bodies of two climbers, Oman’s Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy and Nepal’s Pur Bahadur Gurung, were recovered on Friday, as well as the remains believed to be of American climber Sarah Mallory Geis. On Saturday, the body of Nepal’s Gyalu Sherpa was also recovered, ACP President Irfan Arshad told Dawn.

Kiani told Dawn that on Saturday, five other bodies were also spotted on Broad Peak through aerial reconnaissance.

Rising 8,051 metres, Broad Peak is the world’s 12th-highest mountain and a technically difficult climb.

Seven years before setting out to summit it, Purja had climbed Annapurna, the 10th-highest mountain in the world, in 2019. He then began taking on other 8,000-metre peaks.

He set a record for the fastest ascent of the world’s 14 highest mountains, completing the feat in six months in 2019. He became widely known internationally after the Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, ‘14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible’, was released two years later.

The 43-year-old climber also served in the British military with the Gurkhas and ​later in special forces.

Elite climbers said Purja was a “charismatic, colourful” character. “If we talk about his ​legacy, it’s hard not to focus on how he was at the forefront of shaking up the high altitude guiding,” British climber Kenton Cool, who has climbed Everest 20 ​times, the most by a non-Sherpa, told Reuters on Saturday.

In its announcement of the rescue team reaching Purja’s body, the ACP remembered him as a “man who made the impossible possible”.

“He carried the Nepali flag to the highest points on Earth with pride, and his achievements brought new recognition to Nepal’s climbing community […] But his impact reached far beyond any one nation, more than the records themselves, he gave people everywhere a reason to believe that the impossible was simply something no one had dared attempt hard enough yet, inspiring dreamers and climbers across the globe to chase what once seemed unreachable.”

The statement said, “His loss on the very mountains he so loved is a devastating blow to the global mountaineering family. But his legacy of pushing limits, of proving that the impossible is only impossible until someone dares to do it, will endure in every climber, everywhere, who follows the trail he blazed.

“Our deepest condolences go out to his family, loved ones, and the entire climbing community during this immensely difficult time. Rest well, Nims Dai.”

Additional input from Reuters

World.title: Routine life disrupted in Hyderabad after rain lashes city
World.content:
HYDERABAD: Civic life remained paralysed in Hyderabad as the city received intermittent rainfall on Sunday.

According to the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD), the Met Office in Latifabad recorded 42mm of rain until 5pm, while the City Office recorded 40mm.

Power outages were also reported in Hyderabad. The Hyderabad Electric Supply Company (Hesco) spokesperson claimed that electricity supply remained suspended on 285 of the company’s 722 11kV feeders.

In Hyderabad city, which has 166 feeders, 66 feeders were unable to provide electricity, he confirmed.

A view of railway station main road submerged with rain water after rainfall on Sunday, — Photo by Umair Ali

All major arteries and roads in the city were inundated due to rainfall. Meanwhile, water supply was severely affected as the facilities of the Hyderabad Water and Sewerage Corporation (HWSC) remained without electricity.

In the absence of electricity and with roads inundated, business activities were also affected. Trade activities in the City Cloth Market, Tower Market, Anaj Mandi and Latifabad Units 5, 10, 11 and 12 were disrupted as roads remained submerged.

A view of Hyder Chowk during rain on Sunday,. — Photo by Umair Ali

Elsewhere in Sindh, Mithi district recorded the highest rainfall, at 126mm, until 8am on Sunday, according to the PMD. It was followed by Chhor, which received 81mm of rain, and Badin, with 69mm.

A day earlier, PMD had forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall across parts of Punjab, Sindh and Balochistan until Aug 4.

World.title: SSGC assures citizens there is no gas leak, says odourisation plant testing led to complaints
World.content:
The Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) said on Sunday that complaints of a suspected gas leak near Karachi’s Abul Hasan Isphahani Road since the previous night were due to the testing of odourisation plants during the commissioning of a new pipeline.

While gas is often thought to have a distinctive smell, it is in fact odourless. Gas suppliers deliberately add odorants to the gas as a safety measure to alert consumers to potentially life-threatening leaks.

In a media alert issued on Sunday, the SSGC said that odourants used to give gas its distinctive smell were added in larger quantities for testing purposes. This resulted in a stronger-than-usual smell, prompting reports of a gas leak from various parts of Karachi.

“The SSGC administration wishes to make it clear that all system pressures are normal and that no gas leak of any kind has been reported,” the statement said. “The smell is solely due to the relatively larger quantity of odourants added to the gas during the testing of the odourisation plants.”

The company requested its customers to remain calm and continue their regular activities.

Gas leaks can be life-threatening, causing explosions and fires as well as death by suffocation.

In January, three women suffocated to death, while another fainted in a gas leak incident in an apartment in Rawalpindi’s Bahria Town Phase VII.

World.title: At least 72 died in Spain's Ceuta migrant rush
World.content:
At least 72 people died during the mass influx in recent days of migrants into Spain’s Ceuta enclave, when tens of thousands of people mostly swam around the border post from Morocco, local officials said on Sunday.

Most of the estimated 60,000 people who rushed into Spain’s north African territory have returned to Morocco since the territory’s largest mass migrant crossing.

“The latest figure that we have is 72,” the government’s delegate to Ceuta, Miguel Angel Perez Triano, told reporters, when asked about the number of fatalities.

The previous toll was 67 deaths.

Spanish police and troops patrolled the streets of Ceuta on Sunday as the enclave largely returned to normal after the sudden mass influx of migrants from Morocco that had occurred between Wednesday and Friday.

Only small groups of migrants were still walking around after most who crossed the small border barrier returned voluntarily to Morocco in 48 hours.

AFP on Saturday saw migrant minors milling around in a disused industrial park in Ceuta. Others were seen dozing on the pavements outside.

“All the children here want to go to (mainland) Spain,” said one of the few adults at the site, Moroccan man Aziz Dabch, 41.

The largest migrant rush into the enclave has caused an international crisis for Spain, with European partners criticising Madrid for its immigration policies.

Outside a housing project near Ceuta port, Spanish soldiers detained a group of nine tired-looking migrants who were sitting on the pavement, guarded by troops with an armoured car, an AFP reporter said.

Small inflatable boats from a rescue unit scoured the waters around the border barrier that extends into the Mediterranean Sea, where a new 500-metre (1,640-feet) floating boom reinforced security.

Civil Guard were also taking migrants off a bus to escort them back to the border post to return to Morocco.

The border crossing was calm, with groups of workers picking up trash, clothes and rubbish left behind during the mass crossing.

Rumours

Spain has blamed criminal gangs for spreading rumours that a recent Spanish Supreme Court ruling on immigration would allow migrants easier passage.

Some analysts suggested Morocco could allow migrants to cross the border to put diplomatic pressure on Spain, which has recently improved ties with Rabat’s arch-enemy neighbouring Algeria.

In 2021, around 10,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta, taking advantage of Morocco easing border controls as a way to pressure Spain.

Moroccan officials have so far not offered any statement on the crisis.

But some of those who crossed the border said they had heard the border was open — a rumour quickly amplified on social media.

The EU said it would hold a video call on Tuesday after 22 bloc members issued a joint open letter calling for an urgent meeting to agree a speedy coordinated response, and to prevent further uncontrolled crossings.

Italy on Saturday implemented a one-month suspension of its Schengen agreement with Spain allowing for visa-free movement between borders.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, in a letter to EU leaders, blasted the “selfish” reaction by some EU countries.

Pope Leo XIV on Sunday spoke to the situation in Ceuta in his daily prayers on Sunday, saying he was following it “with concern” and hoping for a solution of “peace, stability and justice”.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.
